He simply said, 'Then we had better start.' What followed was a quiet, breathless *race* across the open sky — two ships chasing the same bright word hanging at the edge of the clouds.
race:1.cnHint: 银牙的船已经起航，老舵手平静地宣告了这场对那枚词语碎片的____。
race:1.hook: The word glowed brighter the closer both ships drew, as if it was choosing.
race:1.line: 'A *race* on open sky — and Silverfang already has the wind.'

sentences.en: Bell spotted the rival crew first.
sentences.cn: 小铃最先发现了那支对手的船队。

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship was already moving, its sails catching the high wind above the market dome.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船已经在移动了，船帆捕捉着市集穹顶上空的高风。

sentences.en: Old Helm did not shout.
sentences.cn: 老舵没有喊叫。

sentences.en: He simply said, 'Then we had better start.'
sentences.cn: 他只是说，"那我们最好赶紧启航。"

sentences.en: What followed was a quiet, breathless *race* across the open sky — two ships chasing the same bright word hanging at the edge of the clouds.

medical:1.en: The word we found that evening was carved on a green tile: *medical*. Old Helm held it up and the tile projected a soft image — a floating island shaped like a leaf, full of low buildings and quiet people. Bell said the whole island was a place for healing. I had not known words could open doors to places so gentle.
medical:1.cnHint: 我们找到的词语碎片投出一幅影像，那是一座充满____设施的绿叶形浮岛。
medical:1.hook: Somewhere on that island, someone was waiting for exactly this word to arrive.
medical:1.line: 'A *medical* island — Old Helm, someone there needs what we are carrying.'

sentences.en: The word we found that evening was carved on a green tile: *medical*.
Old Helm held it up and the tile projected a soft image — a floating island shaped like a leaf, full of low buildings and quiet people.
sentences.cn: 老舵举起来，绿瓷砖投射出一个柔和的影像——一座形如叶子的浮岛，布满低矮的建筑和安静的人。

sentences.en: Bell said the whole island was a place for healing.
sentences.cn: 小铃说整座岛都是一个治疗的地方。

sentences.en: I had not known words could open doors to places so gentle.
sentences.cn: 我不知道词语竟然能打开通向这么温柔的地方的大门。

wear:1.en: The higher islands had sharp, cold air that bit at your ears. Bell handed me an extra layer without being asked. Old Helm told me to *wear* it every time we climbed above the cloud line, and to never ignore the cold just because the stars looked warm. I pulled the cloth tight and felt, for the first time, like I truly belonged to the troupe.
wear:1.cnHint: 高空岛屿寒气逼人，老舵手嘱咐我要____贝尔递来的加厚外衣。
wear:1.hook: The stars looked warm, but Old Helm's warning stayed in my ears.
wear:1.line: '*Wear* the extra layer — the cold up here does not care how brave you feel.'

sentences.en: The higher islands had sharp, cold air that bit at your ears.
sentences.cn: 更高的岛屿空气又尖又冷，会咬得你的耳朵疼。

sentences.en: Bell handed me an extra layer without being asked.
sentences.cn: 小铃没问就递给了我一层额外的衣服。

sentences.en: Old Helm told me to *wear* it every time we climbed above the cloud line, and to never ignore the cold just because the stars looked warm.
I pulled the cloth tight and felt, for the first time, like I truly belonged to the troupe.
sentences.cn: 我把布料紧紧裹住，第一次真正感觉自己属于这个剧团。

climate:1.en: The island of Greywood surprised us. Every other floating island we had visited was dry and breezy, but here a low mist clung to everything. Old Helm said the *climate* was shaped by the giant word-stone at the island's centre, which had been holding the word for 'rain' for three hundred years. Bell simply opened her umbrella and walked on.
climate:1.cnHint: 葛林伍德岛的____与众不同，岛中央那块古老的词语石已将"雨"字守护了三百年。
climate:1.hook: The word-stone hummed when I stepped close, as though it remembered me.
climate:1.line: 'Strange *climate* for a floating island — that stone has been working a long time.'

sentences.en: The island of Greywood surprised us.
sentences.cn: 绿林岛让我们大吃一惊。

sentences.en: Every other floating island we had visited was dry and breezy, but here a low mist clung to everything.
sentences.cn: 我们去过的其他浮岛都是干燥而多风的，但这里一层薄雾紧贴着万物。

sentences.en: Old Helm said the *climate* was shaped by the giant word-stone at the island's centre, which had been holding the word for 'rain' for three hundred years.
Bell simply opened her umbrella and walked on.
sentences.cn: 小铃只是打开了伞，继续向前走。

head:1.en: At the tallest point of the dock stood a bronze post with a single arrow. Old Helm said every new member of the troupe must place their hand on it and name the direction they wanted to *head* next. Bell had chosen east on her first day. When my turn came, I looked out at the dark, star-filled sky and said, 'Somewhere no one has found a word yet.'
head:1.cnHint: 码头最高处有一根铜柱，每位新成员要在此宣告自己想____的方向。
head:1.hook: Old Helm smiled like he had heard that answer before and hoped to hear it again.
head:1.line: 'You have to *head* toward the unknown — that is the only rule worth keeping.'

sentences.en: At the tallest point of the dock stood a bronze post with a single arrow.
sentences.cn: 码头最高的地方竖着一根青铜柱，柱顶有一个箭头。

sentences.en: Old Helm said every new member of the troupe must place their hand on it and name the direction they wanted to *head* next.
Bell had chosen east on her first day.
sentences.cn: 小铃在她的第一天选择了东方。

sentences.en: When my turn came, I looked out at the dark, star-filled sky and said, 'Somewhere no one has found a word yet.'
sentences.cn: 轮到我时，我看着漆黑的、闪烁的星空，说，"去某个还没有人发现过词语的地方。"

mistake:1.en: Old Helm spread the map across a flat stone and studied it by starlight. 'We turned left at the silver cloud,' he muttered, pressing a finger to the paper. 'That was a *mistake* — the Ember Isle lies east, not west.' The whole troupe groaned softly and turned around.
mistake:1.cnHint: 老舵主发现队伍走错了方向，需要原路返回。
mistake:1.hook: Behind us, the western path began to glow.
mistake:1.line: 'Turning left at the silver cloud was a *mistake* I will not repeat.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the map across a flat stone and studied it by starlight.
sentences.cn: 老舵在平石上铺开地图，借着星光研究起来。

sentences.en: 'We turned left at the silver cloud,' he muttered, pressing a finger to the paper.
sentences.cn: "我们在银色云那里向左转了，"他自言自语地说，手指按在纸上。

sentences.en: 'That was a *mistake* — the Ember Isle lies east, not west.'
The whole troupe groaned softly and turned around.
sentences.cn: 整个剧团都轻声叹了口气，然后转身。

staff:1.en: We landed on a wide platform where a travelling market had set up for the night. Lanterns swayed on ropes, and every member of the *staff* wore a sash the colour of moonlight. Bell counted them quietly — twelve workers, each holding a small glowing token that matched a star above.
staff:1.cnHint: 我们降落在夜市平台，发现全体____都佩戴着月光色腰带。
staff:1.hook: One worker's token flickered and went cold.
staff:1.line: 'Every member of the *staff* must keep their token lit at all times.'

sentences.en: We landed on a wide platform where a travelling market had set up for the night.
sentences.cn: 我们降落在一个宽阔的平台上，一个流动市集在那里夜间扎营。

sentences.en: Lanterns swayed on ropes, and every member of the *staff* wore a sash the colour of moonlight.
Bell counted them quietly — twelve workers, each holding a small glowing token that matched a star above.
sentences.cn: 小铃静静地数着——十二个工作人员，每人手里拿着一枚微弱的发光令牌，和上面的星星一一对应。

enhance:1.en: Bell pulled a tiny crystal from her coat and pressed it against the map's edge. 'This stone will *enhance* the lines,' she said, and the faded ink rose bright and clear under the starlight. Paths we had never seen before appeared, curving toward an island shaped like a sleeping bird.
enhance:1.cnHint: 领航员用一块水晶____了地图上模糊的线条，露出新的路径。
enhance:1.hook: The bird-shaped island was not on any record we carried.
enhance:1.line: 'Press it gently — too much force will *enhance* the wrong lines.'

sentences.en: Bell pulled a tiny crystal from her coat and pressed it against the map's edge.
sentences.cn: 小铃从外套里掏出一枚细小的晶体，贴在地图的边缘。

sentences.en: 'This stone will *enhance* the lines,' she said, and the faded ink rose bright and clear under the starlight.
Paths we had never seen before appeared, curving toward an island shaped like a sleeping bird.
sentences.cn: 我们从未见过的路径显现出来，蜿蜒指向一个形状像熟睡小鸟的岛屿。

famous:1.en: At the edge of the platform stood a tall sign carved with a single sentence: 'This is the *famous* Bridge of Whispers, where every traveller leaves one word behind.' Old Helm read it aloud and smiled. We each pressed a hand to the wood, wondering which word we would choose to leave.
famous:1.cnHint: 平台边缘的告示牌介绍了这座____的耳语之桥。
famous:1.hook: The bridge hummed as if it already knew our words.
famous:1.line: 'I crossed this *famous* bridge once before, but I left the wrong word.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the platform stood a tall sign carved with a single sentence: 'This is the *famous* Bridge of Whispers, where every traveller leaves one word behind.'
Old Helm read it aloud and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵大声读出来，咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: We each pressed a hand to the wood, wondering which word we would choose to leave.
sentences.cn: 我们各自把手按在木头上，琢磨着该留下哪个词。

project:1.en: Silverfang unrolled a long sheet of paper and laid stones on its corners to stop the wind taking it. 'This is our *project*,' she said, pointing to a hand-drawn plan of three connected islands. 'If we link them with light-rope, the whole cluster will drift together.' Bell leaned in, eyes wide.
project:1.cnHint: 竞争船长展示了她连接三座浮岛的____计划。
project:1.hook: One of the three islands had already begun to move.
project:1.line: 'Every person here has a part in this *project* — including you.'

sentences.en: Silverfang unrolled a long sheet of paper and laid stones on its corners to stop the wind taking it.
sentences.cn: 银牙展开一长张纸，用石子压在四个角上防止风吹走。

sentences.en: 'This is our *project*,' she said, pointing to a hand-drawn plan of three connected islands.
'If we link them with light-rope, the whole cluster will drift together.'
sentences.cn: 如果我们用光绳把它们连起来，整个群岛就能漂浮在一起。

sentences.en: Bell leaned in, eyes wide.
sentences.cn: 小铃探过身去，眼睛睁得很大。

record:1.en: An old keeper sat beside a stone pillar, writing in a thick book by lamplight. 'I keep the *record* of every troupe that passes through,' he said without looking up. Old Helm peered at the open page and saw names stretching back hundreds of years, each one paired with a single collected word.
record:1.cnHint: 一位老守护人向我们展示记录过往旅队的____册。
record:1.hook: Our troupe's name was already written on the next blank line.
record:1.line: 'The *record* shows no troupe has ever carried the word you hold.'

sentences.en: An old keeper sat beside a stone pillar, writing in a thick book by lamplight.
sentences.cn: 一位年迈的守护者坐在石柱旁，在灯光下用厚厚的簿子记录着什么。

sentences.en: 'I keep the *record* of every troupe that passes through,' he said without looking up.
Old Helm peered at the open page and saw names stretching back hundreds of years, each one paired with a single collected word.
sentences.cn: 老舵瞥了一眼翻开的那页，看到名字一直往回延伸几百年，每个名字后面都配着一个收集来的词。

regular:1.en: Bell pointed to a cluster of lights rising and falling in the dark. 'Those are *regular* signal pulses,' she said, timing them on her fingers. 'Every eight seconds — someone is trying to send a message.' We all counted together, and on the eighth beat a shape appeared briefly against the stars.
regular:1.cnHint: 领航员发现远处黑暗中有____出现的信号光。
regular:1.hook: On the ninth beat, the shape did not disappear.
regular:1.line: 'A *regular* pattern means someone planned this — it is not an accident.'

sentences.en: Bell pointed to a cluster of lights rising and falling in the dark.
sentences.cn: 小铃指着黑暗中一簇上下起伏的灯光。

sentences.en: 'Those are *regular* signal pulses,' she said, timing them on her fingers.
'Every eight seconds — someone is trying to send a message.'
sentences.cn: 每八秒一次——有人在试图发送信息。

sentences.en: We all counted together, and on the eighth beat a shape appeared briefly against the stars.
sentences.cn: 我们一起数着，第八下时一个身影短暂地在星空前显现出来。

security:1.en: A ring of small drones circled the outer edge of the island, humming quietly. 'They are part of the *security* system,' Old Helm explained, keeping his voice low. 'As long as we move slowly and carry no sharp tools, they will let us pass.' Bell tucked her crystal out of sight just in case.
security:1.cnHint: 老舵主提醒我们小心岛屿边缘的____系统，不要轻举妄动。
security:1.hook: One drone turned and faced us, lights blinking red.
security:1.line: 'Good *security* means even friends must prove why they have come.'

sentences.en: A ring of small drones circled the outer edge of the island, humming quietly.
sentences.cn: 一圈小型无人机在岛屿外边缘盘旋，嗡嗡作响。

sentences.en: 'They are part of the *security* system,' Old Helm explained, keeping his voice low.
'As long as we move slowly and carry no sharp tools, they will let us pass.'
sentences.cn: 只要我们移动缓慢，不携带任何尖锐工具，它们就会放我们过去。

sentences.en: Bell tucked her crystal out of sight just in case.
sentences.cn: 小铃把晶体收好了以防万一。

return:1.en: The market square of Ashveil Island smelled of roasted seeds and old wood. Old Helm pressed a glowing chip into my palm — a word-fragment pulled from the stone well at the centre. 'Every *return* to this square,' he said, 'means we found our way back alive.' I closed my fingers around it, and the map in my pocket hummed with new warmth.
return:1.cnHint: 在广场的石井旁，老船长把一枚发光的字片交给我，说每次____都是平安归来的证明。
return:1.hook: The map hummed — but the well had begun to glow on its own.
return:1.line: 'Every *return* to this square means we found our way back alive.'

sentences.en: The market square of Ashveil Island smelled of roasted seeds and old wood.
sentences.cn: 艾什维尔岛的市集广场闻起来像烤种子和陈年木头的混合味。

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed a glowing chip into my palm — a word-fragment pulled from the stone well at the centre.
sentences.cn: 老舵把一枚发光芯片按进我的掌心——是从中央石井抽取的一个词语碎片。

sentences.en: 'Every *return* to this square,' he said, 'means we found our way back alive.'
I closed my fingers around it, and the map in my pocket hummed with new warmth.
sentences.cn: 我握紧了它，口袋里的地图散发出新的温暖。

remove:1.en: Bell knelt beside a cracked lantern post at the edge of Duskpier Street. A strange fog clung to the boards and refused to lift. She reached into her coat, drew out a small silver tool, and began to *remove* the rusted plate blocking the lantern's vent. Light burst free at once, and the fog rolled back like a shy animal stepping into shadow.
remove:1.cnHint: 小铃在码头街用银色工具____了灯柱上的锈板，浓雾随之退散。
remove:1.hook: Behind the retreating fog stood a door nobody had noticed before.
remove:1.line: 'Let me *remove* this plate — the light will push the fog right back.'

sentences.en: Bell knelt beside a cracked lantern post at the edge of Duskpier Street.
sentences.cn: 小铃跪在暮港街边缘一个裂开的灯柱旁。

sentences.en: A strange fog clung to the boards and refused to lift.
sentences.cn: 一种奇异的雾气紧贴着木板，拒绝散开。

sentences.en: She reached into her coat, drew out a small silver tool, and began to *remove* the rusted plate blocking the lantern's vent.
Light burst free at once, and the fog rolled back like a shy animal stepping into shadow.
sentences.cn: 光爆发出来，雾气像一只羞怯的动物踩进影子里一样向后退去。

colleague:1.en: Silverfang leaned against a fruit stall and tossed me a small green star-fruit. 'My old *colleague* on the Driftwood Run used to say: eat before you navigate, or the stars will spin.' He caught my confused look and grinned. 'Yes, I had partners once. One of them hid a word-fragment somewhere on this island. I intend to find it first.'
colleague:1.cnHint: 银牙提到一位昔日____曾把字片藏在岛上，他打算抢先找到它。
colleague:1.hook: He was already walking away before I could ask that colleague's name.
colleague:1.line: 'My old *colleague* always said: eat before you navigate, or the stars will spin.'

sentences.en: Silverfang leaned against a fruit stall and tossed me a small green star-fruit.
sentences.cn: 银牙靠在一个水果摊上，朝我丢来一个小绿色星形果。

sentences.en: 'My old *colleague* on the Driftwood Run used to say: eat before you navigate, or the stars will spin.'
He caught my confused look and grinned.
sentences.cn: 他看我一脸困惑，咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: 'Yes, I had partners once.
sentences.cn: 是的，我曾经有搭档。

sentences.en: One of them hid a word-fragment somewhere on this island.
sentences.cn: 他们中有一个在这个岛上藏了一个词语碎片。

sentences.en: I intend to find it first.'
sentences.cn: 我打算先找到它。

normal:1.en: The night bazaar on Cinderloop Island felt almost *normal* — bright stalls, laughing voices, the smell of warm spiced broth. Almost. Every vendor had no shadow, and every price tag was written in a language that shifted when you looked away. Old Helm bought three items without blinking. 'You get used to it,' he told me, handing me a bowl of broth that tasted like home.
normal:1.cnHint: 夜市看起来____，可每个摊主都没有影子，价签上的文字还会变化。
normal:1.hook: Then every stall fell silent at exactly the same moment.
normal:1.line: 'It looks *normal* enough — just don't stare at the price tags too long.'

sentences.en: The night bazaar on Cinderloop Island felt almost *normal* — bright stalls, laughing voices, the smell of warm spiced broth.
Almost.
sentences.cn: 几乎。

sentences.en: Every vendor had no shadow, and every price tag was written in a language that shifted when you looked away.
sentences.cn: 每个摊主都没有影子，每个价签上的文字在你转身看时就会改变。

sentences.en: Old Helm bought three items without blinking.
sentences.cn: 老舵眨眼不眨地买了三件东西。

sentences.en: 'You get used to it,' he told me, handing me a bowl of broth that tasted like home.
sentences.cn: 他对我说，递给我一碗尝起来像家的味道的热汤。

succeed:1.en: The word-lock on the gate of Embervane Square needed a spoken phrase to open. Bell tried twice; the gate hummed and stayed shut. On her third try she changed the last syllable, and the lock clicked free. She turned to us, beaming. 'If you *succeed* on the third attempt, the island gives you a bonus fragment,' she said, plucking a second glowing chip from the air.
succeed:1.cnHint: 小铃第三次尝试后终于____开启了城门，还从空气中获得了一枚额外的字片。
succeed:1.hook: The bonus fragment showed a place none of our maps had ever named.
succeed:1.line: 'If you *succeed* on the third attempt, the island gives you a bonus fragment.'

sentences.en: The word-lock on the gate of Embervane Square needed a spoken phrase to open.
sentences.cn: 余烬方广场大门上的词语锁需要一句话才能打开。

sentences.en: Bell tried twice; the gate hummed and stayed shut.
sentences.cn: 小铃试了两次，大门嗡嗡作响，纹丝不动。

sentences.en: On her third try she changed the last syllable, and the lock clicked free.
sentences.cn: 第三次她改了最后的音节，锁咔哒一声打开了。

sentences.en: She turned to us, beaming.
sentences.cn: 她转向我们，眉开眼笑。

sentences.en: 'If you *succeed* on the third attempt, the island gives you a bonus fragment,' she said, plucking a second glowing chip from the air.

image:1.en: At the centre of Glasspool Plaza stood a tall mirror with no frame and no reflection — only a slow, shifting *image* of an island none of us recognised. Mountains of pale blue stone, a river of silver light, and a single lantern at the highest peak. Old Helm traced its outline with one careful finger. 'That,' he said quietly, 'is where we are going next.'
image:1.cnHint: 广场上的镜子里浮现出一座陌生小岛的____，老船长说那就是下一个目的地。
image:1.hook: The image flickered once, as if the island knew we were watching.
image:1.line: 'That *image* in the mirror — I have been looking for that island for ten years.'

sentences.en: At the centre of Glasspool Plaza stood a tall mirror with no frame and no reflection — only a slow, shifting *image* of an island none of us recognised.
Mountains of pale blue stone, a river of silver light, and a single lantern at the highest peak.
sentences.cn: 苍白的蓝石山峰，一条银光闪闪的河流，还有最高峰上一盏孤独的灯笼。

sentences.en: Old Helm traced its outline with one careful finger.
sentences.cn: 老舵用一根手指仔细地描绘着它的轮廓。

sentences.en: 'That,' he said quietly, 'is where we are going next.'
sentences.cn: "那，"他轻声说，"就是我们接下来要去的地方。"

ourselves:1.en: The rope bridge over Hollow Gap swayed hard in the night wind. Silverfang crossed first, then Old Helm, then me — palms sweating, stars spinning below. When we all reached the far ledge, Bell counted heads and laughed with relief. 'We did it *ourselves*,' she said, 'no ropes, no helpers, just us and a very rude wind.' The new island rose ahead, steady and bright.
ourselves:1.cnHint: 我们靠____走过了摇晃的绳桥，小铃笑着说没有任何外力帮助。
ourselves:1.hook: The island ahead pulsed with light, as if it had been waiting just for us.
ourselves:1.line: 'We crossed it *ourselves* — no help, just us and a very rude wind.'

sentences.en: The rope bridge over Hollow Gap swayed hard in the night wind.
sentences.cn: 绳桥在夜风中狠狠地摇晃着，跨越了空心谷。

sentences.en: Silverfang crossed first, then Old Helm, then me — palms sweating, stars spinning below.
sentences.cn: 银牙先过，然后是老舵，最后是我——手心冒汗，星星在脚下旋转。

sentences.en: When we all reached the far ledge, Bell counted heads and laughed with relief.
sentences.cn: 等我们都到了对面的崖边，小铃数了数人头，松了口气地笑了。

sentences.en: 'We did it *ourselves*,' she said, 'no ropes, no helpers, just us and a very rude wind.'
The new island rose ahead, steady and bright.
sentences.cn: 新的岛屿在前方升起，稳定而明亮。

catch:1.en: A word-fragment broke free from the old clock tower on Tidebell Street and spun upward like a leaf in a gust. Bell sprinted across the cobblestones, leapt onto a low wall, and stretched both arms wide to *catch* it before it reached the clouds. She landed, fragment in hand, sliding two steps on the smooth stone. 'Got it!' she called, holding it up like a tiny torch.
catch:1.cnHint: 小铃冲过石板街，纵身一跳，____住了从钟楼飞出的字片，没让它消失在云里。
catch:1.hook: The fragment lit up her face — and on it was a word none of us could read.
catch:1.line: 'Jump now — it is the only way to *catch* it before the wind takes it!'

sentences.en: A word-fragment broke free from the old clock tower on Tidebell Street and spun upward like a leaf in a gust.
sentences.cn: 一个词语碎片从潮钟街的老钟塔上裂开，像被阵风吹起的叶子一样向上旋转。

sentences.en: Bell sprinted across the cobblestones, leapt onto a low wall, and stretched both arms wide to *catch* it before it reached the clouds.
She landed, fragment in hand, sliding two steps on the smooth stone.
sentences.cn: 她落地了，碎片握在手中，在光滑的石头上滑行了两步。

sentences.en: 'Got it!' she called, holding it up like a tiny torch.
sentences.cn: "抓到了！"她喊道，把它举起来像一支小火把。

whatever:1.en: The troupe landed on a narrow island bridge lit by falling stars. Old Helm spread his arms wide and told us to gather *whatever* loose stones we could find along the edge — each one might carry a hidden word. Bell filled her pockets fast, eyes bright with hope.
whatever:1.cnHint: 老舵带领大家在星光桥上收集____石块，寻找隐藏的词语碎片。
whatever:1.hook: One stone hummed — and the bridge began to move.
whatever:1.line: 'Gather *whatever* you can find before the light fades!'

sentences.en: The troupe landed on a narrow island bridge lit by falling stars.
sentences.cn: 队伍降落在一座被流星点亮的狭窄岛桥上。

sentences.en: Old Helm spread his arms wide and told us to gather *whatever* loose stones we could find along the edge — each one might carry a hidden word.
Bell filled her pockets fast, eyes bright with hope.
sentences.cn: 小铃快速地把口袋装满，眼睛闪闪发亮，充满希望。

predict:1.en: A cracked signpost stood at the crossroads of two sky-roads. Old Helm studied the cracks like a map. 'I can *predict* which road holds the next word,' he said quietly, tracing a line with one finger. Bell leaned in close, and even Silverfang slowed his rival ship to listen.
predict:1.cnHint: 老舵在天空路口研究断裂的路标，声称能____下一个词语藏在哪条路上。
predict:1.hook: He pointed left — then the signpost cracked clean in two.
predict:1.line: 'I can *predict* which road will lead us to the word.'

sentences.en: A cracked signpost stood at the crossroads of two sky-roads.
sentences.cn: 一个裂开的路标竖立在两条空中之路的十字路口。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied the cracks like a map.
sentences.cn: 老舵像看地图一样研究着那些裂纹。

sentences.en: 'I can *predict* which road holds the next word,' he said quietly, tracing a line with one finger.
Bell leaned in close, and even Silverfang slowed his rival ship to listen.
sentences.cn: 小铃凑得很近，连银牙都放慢了对手船的速度来听。

road:1.en: The *road* ahead curved off the edge of the island and became a bridge of packed cloud. Bell checked her compass twice. Old Helm stepped onto it first, testing each step. The cloud held firm. Far ahead, a faint glow marked something worth reaching, and the whole troupe followed.
road:1.cnHint: 前方的____延伸成云朵桥梁，贝尔确认方向后，大家跟着老舵踏上了未知旅途。
road:1.hook: Halfway across, the cloud road began to thin.
road:1.line: 'This *road* of cloud is stranger than any I have walked.'

sentences.en: The *road* ahead curved off the edge of the island and became a bridge of packed cloud.
Bell checked her compass twice.
sentences.cn: 小铃检查了两遍她的罗盘。

sentences.en: Old Helm stepped onto it first, testing each step.
sentences.cn: 老舵第一个踏上去，测试着每一步。

sentences.en: The cloud held firm.
sentences.cn: 云托住了。

sentences.en: Far ahead, a faint glow marked something worth reaching, and the whole troupe followed.
sentences.cn: 远处，一抹微弱的光芒标记着值得到达的地方，整个队伍跟了上去。

solution:1.en: The gate to the next island was sealed with a lock shaped like a star. Old Helm circled it three times, frowning. Bell pulled a glowing stone from her pocket — a perfect fit. 'That is the *solution*,' she said with a grin, pressing it in. The gate swung open wide.
solution:1.cnHint: 贝尔用一块发光的石头解开了封印星门的锁，找到了打开大门的____。
solution:1.hook: Beyond the gate, something ancient stirred in the dark.
solution:1.line: 'A glowing stone — that is the *solution* to this lock!'

sentences.en: The gate to the next island was sealed with a lock shaped like a star.
sentences.cn: 通往下一个岛屿的大门被一把星星形状的锁封住了。

sentences.en: Old Helm circled it three times, frowning.
sentences.cn: 老舵绕着它转了三圈，皱着眉头。

sentences.en: Bell pulled a glowing stone from her pocket — a perfect fit.
sentences.cn: 小铃从口袋里拉出一块闪闪发光的石头——完美契合。

sentences.en: 'That is the *solution*,' she said with a grin, pressing it in.
The gate swung open wide.
sentences.cn: 大门向两边推开了。

total:1.en: Bell laid all the word-fragments on a flat rock and counted them aloud. The *total* came to nine, one short of the number Old Helm had promised would open the sky-chart. Silverfang appeared from behind a cloud pillar, holding up the missing piece with a sly smile.
total:1.cnHint: 贝尔清点词语碎片，发现____数量比所需的少一块，而银牙恰好拿着那一块出现了。
total:1.hook: Silverfang's smile faded as he read what the fragment said.
total:1.line: 'The *total* is nine — we are still one piece short.'

sentences.en: Bell laid all the word-fragments on a flat rock and counted them aloud.
sentences.cn: 小铃把所有的词语碎片放在一块平石上，大声数着。

sentences.en: The *total* came to nine, one short of the number Old Helm had promised would open the sky-chart.
Silverfang appeared from behind a cloud pillar, holding up the missing piece with a sly smile.
sentences.cn: 银牙从一根云柱后面出现，用狡猾的笑容举起那个缺失的碎片。

fail:1.en: The wind machine at the island's edge began to sputter and slow. Without it, our ship could not rise high enough to reach the next star-island. 'If it should *fail* completely, we are stuck,' Bell said, calm but serious. Old Helm rolled up his sleeves and opened the hatch below.
fail:1.cnHint: 岛边的风力机器开始熄火，贝尔担心一旦完全____，飞船就无法升空了。
fail:1.hook: From the hatch came a sound none of us expected.
fail:1.line: 'If this machine should *fail*, we cannot reach the next island.'

sentences.en: The wind machine at the island's edge began to sputter and slow.
sentences.cn: 岛屿边缘的风力机开始噗噗地减速。

sentences.en: Without it, our ship could not rise high enough to reach the next star-island.
sentences.cn: 没有它，我们的船无法上升到足够的高度去到达下一个星岛。

sentences.en: 'If it should *fail* completely, we are stuck,' Bell said, calm but serious.
Old Helm rolled up his sleeves and opened the hatch below.
sentences.cn: 老舵卷起袖子，打开了下面的舱口。

function:1.en: Bell handed me a small brass device covered in tiny dials. 'Its *function* is simple,' she said, 'point it at any carved word and it reads the island it belongs to.' I aimed it at a glyph on the wall. The dials spun, clicked, and a soft chime rang out across the night air.
function:1.cnHint: 贝尔给了我一个小黄铜装置，解释了它的____——能识别刻字所属的岛屿。
function:1.hook: The chime played a tune none of our maps had recorded.
function:1.line: 'Its *function* is to find which island every carved word belongs to.'

sentences.en: Bell handed me a small brass device covered in tiny dials.
sentences.cn: 小铃递给我一个小铜装置，上面覆盖着细小的刻度盘。

sentences.en: 'Its *function* is simple,' she said, 'point it at any carved word and it reads the island it belongs to.'
I aimed it at a glyph on the wall.
sentences.cn: 我对准了墙上的一个字形符号。

sentences.en: The dials spun, clicked, and a soft chime rang out across the night air.
sentences.cn: 刻度盘旋转、咔哒一声，一阵柔和的铃声响彻夜空。

method:1.en: Silverfang landed his ship beside ours without a sound. Old Helm raised an eyebrow. 'What is your *method* for such a silent landing?' he asked. Silverfang shrugged, looking almost friendly for once. 'Years of practice and a great deal of patience,' he said, then turned back to his own deck.
method:1.cnHint: 老舵对银牙无声降落的____感到好奇，银牙给出了一个出人意料的答案。
method:1.hook: Silverfang paused, then added one quiet word: 'Tonight.'
method:1.line: 'What is your *method* for landing so silently on these islands?'

sentences.en: Silverfang landed his ship beside ours without a sound.
sentences.cn: 银牙无声地将他的船停靠在我们的船旁边。

sentences.en: Old Helm raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 老舵抬起一条眉毛。

sentences.en: 'What is your *method* for such a silent landing?' he asked.
Silverfang shrugged, looking almost friendly for once.
sentences.cn: 银牙耸了耸肩，看起来这次几乎显得友好。

sentences.en: 'Years of practice and a great deal of patience,' he said, then turned back to his own deck.
sentences.cn: "多年的练习和大量的耐心，"他说，然后转身回到自己的甲板。

review:1.en: Old Helm spread the worn map across the market stones and called us close. 'Before we move on,' he said, 'we do a *review* of every word-fragment we have collected.' He pointed to each glowing piece in turn. I noticed a gap shaped like a crescent island I had never seen before.
review:1.cnHint: 老舵主让大家围坐在市场的石板上，对已收集的词语碎片做____，我发现地图上有一处空白。
review:1.hook: The crescent gap pulsed once, as if calling our names.
review:1.line: 'A careful *review* now saves us from flying blind later,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the worn map across the market stones and called us close.
sentences.cn: 老舵在市场的石头上铺开了那张破旧的地图，招我们靠近。

sentences.en: 'Before we move on,' he said, 'we do a *review* of every word-fragment we have collected.'
He pointed to each glowing piece in turn.
sentences.cn: 他依次指向每一块闪闪发光的碎片。

sentences.en: I noticed a gap shaped like a crescent island I had never seen before.
sentences.cn: 我注意到一个我从未见过的新月形岛屿留下的缝隙。

ahead:1.en: Bell climbed the tall signal post at the edge of the dock and shaded her eyes against the starlight. 'There is another island *ahead*,' she called down, voice bright with wonder. From below I could just make out a soft green glow floating in the dark sky, waiting for us like a lantern left on.
ahead:1.cnHint: 小铃爬上码头的高杆，望见了____方向漂浮着一座散发绿光的岛屿。
ahead:1.hook: The green glow blinked once, then began slowly drifting away.
ahead:1.line: 'Keep the bow pointed *ahead* and we will reach it before dawn,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell climbed the tall signal post at the edge of the dock and shaded her eyes against the starlight.
sentences.cn: 小铃爬上了码头边的高信号塔，眯起眼睛挡住星光。

sentences.en: 'There is another island *ahead*,' she called down, voice bright with wonder.
From below I could just make out a soft green glow floating in the dark sky, waiting for us like a lantern left on.
sentences.cn: 我隐约看到一团柔软的绿光浮在黑暗的天空中，像盏点亮的灯笼在等我们。

cheap:1.en: A vendor at the night market tried to sell us a so-called word-fragment for three sky-coins. Old Helm turned it over in his fingers and shook his head. 'This is *cheap* glass, not a true fragment,' he said with a kind smile. The vendor looked away, and somewhere behind us Bell quietly laughed.
cheap:1.cnHint: 一个摊贩试图把假碎片卖给我们，老舵主认出那只是____的玻璃，并非真正的词语碎片。
cheap:1.hook: Yet the glass caught starlight and spelled out one real letter.
cheap:1.line: 'I have seen real fragments — this one is far too *cheap* to be true,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: A vendor at the night market tried to sell us a so-called word-fragment for three sky-coins.
sentences.cn: 夜市里有个摊主想用三枚星币卖给我们一块所谓的词语碎片。

sentences.en: Old Helm turned it over in his fingers and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 老舵在手指间转了转，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'This is *cheap* glass, not a true fragment,' he said with a kind smile.
The vendor looked away, and somewhere behind us Bell quietly laughed.
sentences.cn: 摊主把目光移开了，我们身后小铃轻声笑了。

critical:1.en: The bridge between two drifting platforms began to crack under our feet. Bell shouted that the centre board was the *critical* piece — if it broke, the whole crossing would fall. Old Helm tossed her a rope without a word. She caught it, looped it around the board, and we crossed in ten quick steps.
critical:1.cnHint: 桥板开裂，小铃大喊中间那块木板是____的，老舵主扔出绳子，大家迅速通过。
critical:1.hook: Behind us the bridge gave way with a soft, echoing crack.
critical:1.line: 'That centre board is *critical* — hold the rope and do not stop moving,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The bridge between two drifting platforms began to crack under our feet.
sentences.cn: 两个漂浮平台之间的桥开始在我们脚下断裂。

sentences.en: Bell shouted that the centre board was the *critical* piece — if it broke, the whole crossing would fall.
Old Helm tossed her a rope without a word.
sentences.cn: 老舵没有说话，直接把一条绳子甩给了她。

sentences.en: She caught it, looped it around the board, and we crossed in ten quick steps.
sentences.cn: 她接住了，绳子一圈圈缠上木板，我们十步快速穿过。

motivate:1.en: I was tired and my pack felt heavy as stone. Silverfang appeared beside me, matching my slow steps. 'New member,' she said, 'let the next island *motivate* you. Every word we find there is a door no one else has opened.' I lifted my head, and somehow my pack felt lighter for the rest of the climb.
motivate:1.cnHint: 我疲惫不堪，银牙走到我旁边，用下一座岛屿的未知来____我继续前行。
motivate:1.hook: Above us, a door-shaped light flickered on the island's cliff face.
motivate:1.line: 'Let the mystery of the next island *motivate* you when your feet grow tired,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: I was tired and my pack felt heavy as stone.
sentences.cn: 我累得要命，背包沉得像块石头。

sentences.en: Silverfang appeared beside me, matching my slow steps.
sentences.cn: 银牙出现在我身边，放慢脚步跟上我。

sentences.en: 'New member,' she said, 'let the next island *motivate* you.
Every word we find there is a door no one else has opened.'
sentences.cn: 我们在那里找到的每个词都是一扇没人打开过的门。

sentences.en: I lifted my head, and somehow my pack felt lighter for the rest of the climb.
sentences.cn: 我抬起头，不知怎的，剩下的爬坡路上背包都轻了。

charge:1.en: At the sky-harbour a small ferry boat rocked at its post. The harbour keeper stepped forward and named his price. 'We *charge* two word-fragments per passenger,' he said, holding up two fingers. Old Helm counted our fragments, smiled, and handed them over without argument. We boarded as the stars shifted west.
charge:1.cnHint: 天空港口的渡船管理员说要____两枚词语碎片作为船费，老舵主数了数，欣然支付。
charge:1.hook: The ferry lifted off the dock before the last fragment hit the keeper's palm.
charge:1.line: 'We only *charge* two fragments — that is as fair as the sky itself,' the harbour keeper said.

sentences.en: At the sky-harbour a small ferry boat rocked at its post.
sentences.cn: 在天港停泊着一艘小渡船。

sentences.en: The harbour keeper stepped forward and named his price.
sentences.cn: 港口守护人走上前报了价格。

sentences.en: 'We *charge* two word-fragments per passenger,' he said, holding up two fingers.
Old Helm counted our fragments, smiled, and handed them over without argument.
sentences.cn: 老舵数了数我们的碎片，笑了笑，毫不犹豫地递了过去。

sentences.en: We boarded as the stars shifted west.
sentences.cn: 我们登船时星星向西移动。

complex:1.en: Bell unfolded a new section of the map and we all leaned in. The island ahead had a *complex* system of bridges, lifts, and hidden paths that looped back on themselves like a knot. Silverfang whistled low. Old Helm simply tapped the first path with one finger and said, 'We start here.'
complex:1.cnHint: 小铃展开地图新片段，前方岛屿的路线结构十分____，像一个难解的绳结。
complex:1.hook: One of the looping paths on the map seemed to move on its own.
complex:1.line: 'The layout looks *complex*, but every knot has one loose thread,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Bell unfolded a new section of the map and we all leaned in.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开了地图的新部分，我们都凑了过去。

sentences.en: The island ahead had a *complex* system of bridges, lifts, and hidden paths that looped back on themselves like a knot.
Silverfang whistled low.
sentences.cn: 银牙吹了声口哨。

sentences.en: Old Helm simply tapped the first path with one finger and said, 'We start here.'
sentences.cn: 老舵用一根手指点了点第一条路，说道，我们从这里开始。

itself:1.en: We found the new word-fragment resting in a small hollow at the centre of the night market square. It gave off a soft hum, almost like it was breathing. 'The word chose the place *itself*,' Old Helm said softly. No one argued. I reached down and lifted it, and the whole sky seemed to lean in to watch.
itself:1.cnHint: 我们在夜市广场中央发现了新的词语碎片，老舵主说它是____找到了这个地方，整片星空仿佛都在注视着我们。
itself:1.hook: The moment I lifted it, a new island appeared on the horizon.
itself:1.line: 'The fragment found this hollow by *itself* — the sky has its own way of guiding us,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: We found the new word-fragment resting in a small hollow at the centre of the night market square.
sentences.cn: 我们在夜市广场中心的小凹陷里找到了新的词语碎片。

sentences.en: It gave off a soft hum, almost like it was breathing.
sentences.cn: 它发出柔和的嗡鸣声，好像在呼吸。

sentences.en: 'The word chose the place *itself*,' Old Helm said softly.
No one argued.
sentences.cn: 没人反驳。

sentences.en: I reached down and lifted it, and the whole sky seemed to lean in to watch.
sentences.cn: 我弯下身拿起它，整个天空好像都倾身过来看。

join:1.en: The night market on Driftstone Island glowed with paper lanterns. Old Helm spread our map across a barrel and traced a dotted line. 'Two paths *join* here,' he said, tapping the crossing point. I leaned in and saw it — where the roads met, a new island bloomed like ink on wet paper.
join:1.cnHint: 在漂石岛的夜市上，老船长发现地图上有两条路____在一起，指向一座新岛屿。
join:1.hook: The ink was still warm beneath my fingertip.
join:1.line: 'Two paths *join* here, and that crossing is our next destination.'

sentences.en: The night market on Driftstone Island glowed with paper lanterns.
sentences.cn: 漂流石岛的夜市闪闪发光，纸灯笼照亮了四周。

sentences.en: Old Helm spread our map across a barrel and traced a dotted line.
sentences.cn: 老舵把地图铺在一个木桶上，用手指描了一条虚线。

sentences.en: 'Two paths *join* here,' he said, tapping the crossing point.
I leaned in and saw it — where the roads met, a new island bloomed like ink on wet paper.
sentences.cn: 我凑过去看，明白了——在道路的交汇处，一座新岛屿像墨水在湿纸上绽开。

significant:1.en: Bell held the glowing word-fragment up to the starlight. The crowd around the night stall fell quiet. 'This one feels different,' she whispered. Old Helm nodded slowly. 'It is *significant*,' he said. 'More than a map piece — it is a key.' The fragment pulsed once, and a distant island lit the horizon.
significant:1.cnHint: 小铃感觉手中的词语碎片非同寻常，老船长认为它____，不只是地图碎片，更像是一把钥匙。
significant:1.hook: A second island answered with a faint, distant glow.
significant:1.line: 'This fragment is *significant* — it opens something far bigger than a door.'

sentences.en: Bell held the glowing word-fragment up to the starlight.
sentences.cn: 小铃把闪烁的词语碎片举到星光下。

sentences.en: The crowd around the night stall fell quiet.
sentences.cn: 夜摊周围的人群安静了下来。

sentences.en: 'This one feels different,' she whispered.
sentences.cn: 这个感觉不一样，她低声说。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵缓缓点头。

sentences.en: 'It is *significant*,' he said.
'More than a map piece — it is a key.'
sentences.cn: 不只是地图碎片——它是一把钥匙。

sentences.en: The fragment pulsed once, and a distant island lit the horizon.
sentences.cn: 碎片闪动了一次，远方的岛屿在地平线上亮了起来。

step:1.en: The night-bridge between two islands was made of floating stones, each one glowing faintly. I watched Old Helm *step* from one stone to the next, unhurried, certain. 'The bridge only holds for those who trust it,' he called back. I took a breath, lifted my foot, and the first stone held firm under me.
step:1.cnHint: 老船长平稳地____上那座由漂浮石块组成的夜桥，告诉我只有信任它的人，桥才会承住他们。
step:1.hook: The third stone ahead flickered like a candle in wind.
step:1.line: '*Step* with confidence, and the bridge will meet you halfway.'

sentences.en: The night-bridge between two islands was made of floating stones, each one glowing faintly.
sentences.cn: 两座岛屿之间的夜桥由浮动的石头组成，每块都微微发光。

sentences.en: I watched Old Helm *step* from one stone to the next, unhurried, certain.
'The bridge only holds for those who trust it,' he called back.
sentences.cn: 桥只能支撑相信它的人，他回头喊道。

sentences.en: I took a breath, lifted my foot, and the first stone held firm under me.
sentences.cn: 我深吸一口气，抬起脚，第一块石头在我脚下稳稳地撑住了。

unique:1.en: Silverfang dropped a small jar on the market table. Inside swirled a colour I had never seen — somewhere between silver and dawn. 'Every island produces something *unique*,' she said proudly. 'This mist comes only from the Peak of Echoes.' Old Helm uncorked the jar and a faint melody drifted out into the cold night air.
unique:1.cnHint: 竞争船长展示了一种____的迷雾，它只产自回声峰，老船长一打开瓶盖，夜空中便飘出了轻柔的旋律。
unique:1.hook: The melody pointed, like a finger, toward the east.
unique:1.line: 'Every island is *unique*, but this mist is unlike anything else I have ever found.'

sentences.en: Silverfang dropped a small jar on the market table.
sentences.cn: 银牙在市场摊位上放下了一个小玻璃罐。

sentences.en: Inside swirled a colour I had never seen — somewhere between silver and dawn.
sentences.cn: 里面旋转着一种我从未见过的颜色——介于银色和黎明之间。

sentences.en: 'Every island produces something *unique*,' she said proudly.
'This mist comes only from the Peak of Echoes.'
sentences.cn: 这雾气只来自回声峰。

sentences.en: Old Helm uncorked the jar and a faint melody drifted out into the cold night air.
sentences.cn: 老舵拔开瓶塞，一阵微弱的旋律飘进了冷冷的夜空。

inside:1.en: The old lantern-keeper handed me a brass box at the edge of the night market. I shook it gently. Something rustled. 'Look *inside*,' said Bell, her eyes bright with curiosity. I lifted the lid and found a word-fragment nestled in blue cloth — our next map piece, waiting quietly as if it had always known I would come.
inside:1.cnHint: 老灯笼守护者给了我一个铜盒子，小铃让我看看____，结果发现了我们的下一块地图碎片。
inside:1.hook: The word on the fragment shimmered, then rearranged itself.
inside:1.line: 'Look *inside* — the answer is never as far away as you think it is.'

sentences.en: The old lantern-keeper handed me a brass box at the edge of the night market.
sentences.cn: 老灯塔守护人在夜市边缘递给我一个黄铜盒子。

sentences.en: I shook it gently.
sentences.cn: 我轻轻摇了摇。

sentences.en: Something rustled.
sentences.cn: 里面沙沙作响。

sentences.en: 'Look *inside*,' said Bell, her eyes bright with curiosity.
I lifted the lid and found a word-fragment nestled in blue cloth — our next map piece, waiting quietly as if it had always known I would come.
sentences.cn: 我打开盖子，发现一块词语碎片窝在蓝布里——我们的下一张地图碎片，安静地等待着，好像它一直都知道我会来。

majority:1.en: At the crossroads stall, Old Helm asked our troupe which path to take. Bell pointed left; Silverfang pointed right. I looked at the crowd of travelers around us — the *majority* were heading left, lanterns bobbing in that direction. Old Helm smiled and chose right. 'The rare road,' he said, 'is always worth the extra steps.'
majority:1.cnHint: 在岔路口，大____的旅人都往左走，但老船长却选择了右边那条少有人走的路。
majority:1.hook: The right-hand path vanished into a cloud of silver fog.
majority:1.line: 'The *majority* may be right, but tonight I trust the road less traveled.'

sentences.en: At the crossroads stall, Old Helm asked our troupe which path to take.
sentences.cn: 在十字路口的摊位，老舵问我们的队伍该走哪条路。

sentences.en: Bell pointed left; Silverfang pointed right.
sentences.cn: 小铃指向左边，银牙指向右边。

sentences.en: I looked at the crowd of travelers around us — the *majority* were heading left, lanterns bobbing in that direction.
Old Helm smiled and chose right.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了笑，选择了右边。

sentences.en: 'The rare road,' he said, 'is always worth the extra steps.'
sentences.cn: "冷门的路，"他说，"总是值得多走几步的。"

notice:1.en: I almost missed it. The word-fragment was pressed into the bark of a lantern-post, no bigger than a thumbnail. It was Bell who grabbed my sleeve. 'Did you *notice* that mark?' she asked. I looked again and saw the faint glow. Without her sharp eyes, we would have walked right past our next destination into the dark.
notice:1.cnHint: 小铃让我____一个刻在灯柱上的发光标记——那是我们差点错过的下一块地图碎片。
notice:1.hook: Below the mark, an arrow pointed straight down into the cloud layer.
notice:1.line: 'Did you *notice* that mark on the post? We would have lost the trail without it.'

sentences.en: I almost missed it.
sentences.cn: 我差点错过了。

sentences.en: The word-fragment was pressed into the bark of a lantern-post, no bigger than a thumbnail.
sentences.cn: 那段文字印在灯柱的树皮上，不比大拇指甲盖大。

sentences.en: It was Bell who grabbed my sleeve.
sentences.cn: 是小铃拽住了我的袖子。

sentences.en: 'Did you *notice* that mark?' she asked.
I looked again and saw the faint glow.
sentences.cn: 我再看一遍，看到了那微弱的光。

sentences.en: Without her sharp eyes, we would have walked right past our next destination into the dark.
sentences.cn: 要不是她的眼睛锐利，我们早就走过了，径直走进黑暗，错过下一个目的地。

taste:1.en: The night-market baker pressed a small star-shaped cake into my hand — free, she said, for first-time visitors. I took a bite. The *taste* was warm and faintly sweet, like toasted grain and cool sky together. Old Helm laughed at my expression. 'Now you understand why travelers always return to Driftstone Island,' he said.
taste:1.cnHint: 夜市面包师送给我一块星形糕点，它的____让老船长笑着说，这就是为什么旅人总会重回漂石岛。
taste:1.hook: At the bottom of the wrapper lay a folded map fragment, still warm.
taste:1.line: 'The *taste* of this island stays with you long after the ship has sailed away.'

sentences.en: The night-market baker pressed a small star-shaped cake into my hand — free, she said, for first-time visitors.
sentences.cn: 夜市的面包师傅把一个小星形蛋糕塞进我手里——免费的，她说，是给首次来访者的。

sentences.en: I took a bite.
sentences.cn: 我咬了一口。

sentences.en: The *taste* was warm and faintly sweet, like toasted grain and cool sky together.
Old Helm laughed at my expression.
sentences.cn: 老舵看着我的表情笑了。

sentences.en: 'Now you understand why travelers always return to Driftstone Island,' he said.
sentences.cn: "现在你明白为什么旅人总是回到漂流石岛，"他说。

differ:1.en: The night market on Cloud Bridge *differed* from every island we had visited before. Here, traders sold bottled starlight and shoes made of pressed cloud. Old Helm spread his arms wide and grinned. 'Each island writes its own rules,' he said. Bell was already sketching the stalls into her map.
differ:1.cnHint: 云桥夜市与以往的岛屿____，老舵手兴奋地张开双臂。
differ:1.hook: But one stall had no goods — only a locked door and a humming sound.
differ:1.line: 'These customs *differ* from anything I have seen in thirty years of sailing,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The night market on Cloud Bridge *differed* from every island we had visited before.
Here, traders sold bottled starlight and shoes made of pressed cloud.
sentences.cn: 这里的商人卖装在瓶子里的星光，还有用压实的云做成的鞋子。

sentences.en: Old Helm spread his arms wide and grinned.
sentences.cn: 老舵张开双臂，咧嘴笑了。

sentences.en: 'Each island writes its own rules,' he said.
sentences.cn: "每座岛都有自己的规则，"他说。

sentences.en: Bell was already sketching the stalls into her map.
sentences.cn: 小铃已经在把摊位素描进她的地图里了。

shape:1.en: A lantern-maker on the open plaza was bending wire into every *shape* you could dream of — stars, fish, tiny ships. Old Helm bought one shaped like a compass rose. The moment he held it up, the lantern glowed gold and a new island appeared on Bell's chart, faint but real.
shape:1.cnHint: 广场上的灯笼师傅把铁丝弯成各种____，老舵手买了一个，新岛屿随即出现在海图上。
shape:1.hook: The lantern then flickered once and pointed north, all on its own.
shape:1.line: 'The *shape* of that island on the chart matches this lantern exactly,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: A lantern-maker on the open plaza was bending wire into every *shape* you could dream of — stars, fish, tiny ships.
Old Helm bought one shaped like a compass rose.
sentences.cn: 老舵买了一个指南针玫瑰花形的。

sentences.en: The moment he held it up, the lantern glowed gold and a new island appeared on Bell's chart, faint but real.
sentences.cn: 他一拿起来，灯笼就闪闪发光，小铃的图表上出现了一座新的岛屿，模糊却真实。

twice:1.en: Bell rang the ship's bell *twice* — the signal that a new word had been found. I ran across the night-market square and nearly knocked over a cart of glowing fruit. Old Helm was kneeling beside a cracked cobblestone, brushing away dust to reveal letters pressed deep into the rock.
twice:1.cnHint: 贝尔敲了____下船铃，示意找到了新词语，我冲过夜市广场赶去查看。
twice:1.hook: The letters in the stone shifted, as though trying to rearrange themselves.
twice:1.line: 'I have rung this bell *twice*, so whatever is down there is important,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell rang the ship's bell *twice* — the signal that a new word had been found.
I ran across the night-market square and nearly knocked over a cart of glowing fruit.
sentences.cn: 我冲过夜市广场，差点撞翻一辆装着发光水果的推车。

sentences.en: Old Helm was kneeling beside a cracked cobblestone, brushing away dust to reveal letters pressed deep into the rock.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪在一块裂开的鹅卵石旁，拂去尘埃，露出深深压进岩石里的字母。

aspect:1.en: Every *aspect* of the night market felt alive — the smell of warm sugar, the hum of distant wind-harps, the way starlight pooled in the cracks between stones. Silverfang leaned against a railing and said it reminded him of the harbour town where he first learned to sail. For a moment his sharp eyes went soft.
aspect:1.cnHint: 夜市的每一个____都充满生机，就连竞争船长也陷入了温柔的回忆。
aspect:1.hook: Then Silverfang straightened up and said someone had been following us for an hour.
aspect:1.line: 'The most interesting *aspect* of this island is what it hides beneath the market,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Every *aspect* of the night market felt alive — the smell of warm sugar, the hum of distant wind-harps, the way starlight pooled in the cracks between stones.
Silverfang leaned against a railing and said it reminded him of the harbour town where he first learned to sail.
sentences.cn: 银牙靠在栏杆上说，这让他想起了他当年第一次学航海的港口小镇。

sentences.en: For a moment his sharp eyes went soft.
sentences.cn: 那一刻他锐利的眼神变得柔和了。

currently:1.en: 'The bridge is *currently* closed after midnight,' the gate-keeper told us, holding up a lantern to study our faces. Old Helm smiled, pulled a small folded word from his coat pocket, and placed it gently on the gate post. The lock clicked open by itself. The gate-keeper stepped aside without another word.
currently:1.cnHint: 守门人说桥____不通行，但老舵手拿出一个词语碎片，锁竟然自己开了。
currently:1.hook: Beyond the gate, the bridge stretched into a darkness where the stars did not reach.
currently:1.line: 'The path we need is *currently* hidden, but a word will open it,' Old Helm said calmly.

sentences.en: 'The bridge is *currently* closed after midnight,' the gate-keeper told us, holding up a lantern to study our faces.
Old Helm smiled, pulled a small folded word from his coat pocket, and placed it gently on the gate post.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑着从外套口袋里掏出一个折好的小词，轻轻放在门柱上。

sentences.en: The lock clicked open by itself.
sentences.cn: 锁自己打开了。

sentences.en: The gate-keeper stepped aside without another word.
sentences.cn: 门卫让开身子，没再说一个字。

decrease:1.en: As we climbed the stone steps away from the market, the noise began to *decrease*, replaced by a low wind carrying the scent of rain and pine. Bell counted the steps aloud — her habit on every new island. At step forty she stopped, pointed at a carved word in the wall, and whispered that we had found what we came for.
decrease:1.cnHint: 离开夜市后，喧嚣声逐渐____，贝尔数着台阶，在第四十级发现了刻在墙上的词语。
decrease:1.hook: The carved word pulsed once with pale blue light, then went still.
decrease:1.line: 'Watch how the star-count does not *decrease* as we climb — that means we are going the right way,' said Bell.

sentences.en: As we climbed the stone steps away from the market, the noise began to *decrease*, replaced by a low wind carrying the scent of rain and pine.
Bell counted the steps aloud — her habit on every new island.
sentences.cn: 小铃大声数着台阶——这是她在每座新岛上的习惯。

sentences.en: At step forty she stopped, pointed at a carved word in the wall, and whispered that we had found what we came for.
sentences.cn: 数到第四十级时她停下，指向墙上刻着的一个字，小声说我们找到了我们来这里的原因。

possibility:1.en: Old Helm unfolded the newest word and held it toward the sky. 'Every word is a *possibility*,' he said quietly. 'A door before it is opened.' Below us the night market glittered. Above us the stars were thick as spilled salt. I felt the word hum against my palm when he passed it to me, warm as a held breath.
possibility:1.cnHint: 老舵手展开新词语，说每一个词都是一种____，我接过词语时感到它在掌心颤动。
possibility:1.hook: Then the word folded itself into the shape of a key no one had asked it to make.
possibility:1.line: 'There is a *possibility* this word leads to an island no one in our troupe has ever seen,' Old Helm murmured.

sentences.en: Old Helm unfolded the newest word and held it toward the sky.
sentences.cn: 老舵展开最新的词语，朝天空举起。

sentences.en: 'Every word is a *possibility*,' he said quietly.
'A door before it is opened.'
sentences.cn: "打开前的一扇门。"

sentences.en: Below us the night market glittered.
sentences.cn: 我们下方的夜市闪闪发光。

sentences.en: Above us the stars were thick as spilled salt.
sentences.cn: 我们上方的星星密集得像洒出来的盐。

sentences.en: I felt the word hum against my palm when he passed it to me, warm as a held breath.
sentences.cn: 他把词语递给我时，我感到它在我的掌心嗡鸣，温暖得像一口屏住的呼吸。

crucial:1.en: Bell spread the chart on a night-market table and tapped one glowing point with her finger. 'This crossing is *crucial*,' she said. 'Miss it before dawn and the island drifts out of reach for a full season.' Silverfang was already heading for the ship. Old Helm scooped up the chart, and I ran after them both into the star-thick dark.
crucial:1.cnHint: 贝尔指着海图上的一个点说这次航行____，必须在黎明前出发，否则那座岛会漂走整整一季。
crucial:1.hook: The island on the chart was already moving — slowly, but moving.
crucial:1.line: 'Timing is *crucial* here — we leave now or we lose the island entirely,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell spread the chart on a night-market table and tapped one glowing point with her finger.
sentences.cn: 小铃在夜市的桌子上铺开海图，用手指点了点其中一个发光的点。

sentences.en: 'This crossing is *crucial*,' she said.
'Miss it before dawn and the island drifts out of reach for a full season.'
sentences.cn: 天亮前错过这个航线，岛屿就会漂出去，整整一个季节都回不来。

sentences.en: Silverfang was already heading for the ship.
sentences.cn: 银牙已经朝船走去了。

sentences.en: Old Helm scooped up the chart, and I ran after them both into the star-thick dark.
sentences.cn: 老舵卷起海图，我跟着他们两个冲进了星光密布的黑暗里。

enormous:1.en: The market square of Cinderrock Island stretched before us, lit by a hundred floating lanterns. At its centre stood an *enormous* stone clock, taller than three ships stacked together. Old Helm pressed his hand against it and smiled. 'The word is carved right here,' he said. We added it to our map, and a new island shimmered into view on the horizon.
enormous:1.cnHint: 在星落之夜的市集广场，团长发现了一座____的石钟，上面刻着新的词语碎片。
enormous:1.hook: But the clock's hands were turning backward, and no one knew why.
enormous:1.line: 'That *enormous* clock has not moved in a hundred years — until tonight.'

sentences.en: The market square of Cinderrock Island stretched before us, lit by a hundred floating lanterns.
sentences.cn: 灰烬岩岛的市场广场在我们面前展开，被一百盏浮动的灯笼照亮。

sentences.en: At its centre stood an *enormous* stone clock, taller than three ships stacked together.
Old Helm pressed his hand against it and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手按在它上面，笑了。

sentences.en: 'The word is carved right here,' he said.
sentences.cn: "词语就刻在这里，"他说。

sentences.en: We added it to our map, and a new island shimmered into view on the horizon.
sentences.cn: 我们把它加到地图上，一座新的岛屿在地平线上闪闪发光。

pet:1.en: A small stall near the edge of the square sold nothing but tiny glowing creatures in jars. Bell leaned close to one jar and laughed with delight. 'It looks just like a *pet* star,' she said. The creature blinked, and the word floated up from the jar like smoke, settling gently onto our map.
pet:1.cnHint: 小铃在街边摊位发现了一只像星星一样的____，它将一个新词语留在了地图上。
pet:1.hook: The creature's glow began to pulse faster, as if it was trying to warn us.
pet:1.line: 'Every navigator needs a *pet* like this — it always points toward the next island.'

sentences.en: A small stall near the edge of the square sold nothing but tiny glowing creatures in jars.
sentences.cn: 广场边缘的小摊子里，摆满了装在罐子里的微小发光生物。

sentences.en: Bell leaned close to one jar and laughed with delight.
sentences.cn: 小铃凑近其中一个罐子，高兴得笑了起来。

sentences.en: 'It looks just like a *pet* star,' she said.
The creature blinked, and the word floated up from the jar like smoke, settling gently onto our map.
sentences.cn: 那生物眨了眨眼，一个词从罐子里像烟一样飘起来，轻轻落在了我们的地图上。

restaurant:1.en: Old Helm led us down a narrow lane to a small *restaurant* built into the side of the island's cliff. The tables hung over open sky, and the stars looked close enough to touch. A folded menu on our table was not a menu at all — it was a map fragment with a new word printed in gold.
restaurant:1.cnHint: 团长带领大家来到悬崖边的____用餐，菜单竟然是一张新的地图碎片。
restaurant:1.hook: The waiter vanished before anyone could ask where the next island lay.
restaurant:1.line: 'Welcome — in this *restaurant*, every dish comes with a word and a new direction.'

sentences.en: Old Helm led us down a narrow lane to a small *restaurant* built into the side of the island's cliff.
The tables hung over open sky, and the stars looked close enough to touch.
sentences.cn: 桌子悬在敞开的天空之上，星星看起来近得仿佛伸手可触。

sentences.en: A folded menu on our table was not a menu at all — it was a map fragment with a new word printed in gold.
sentences.cn: 桌上折起的菜单根本不是菜单——那是一张地图碎片，上面用金色字印着一个新词。

driver:1.en: A cart rattled across the stone square pulled by two wind-filled sails on wheels. Its *driver* sat tall on a high bench, wearing a coat covered in small compass roses. She tossed Old Helm a rolled note as she passed. Inside was a single word and a rough drawing of an island we had never seen.
driver:1.cnHint: 一辆帆车的____向团长投来一张纸条，上面有一个新词和一座陌生岛屿的图样。
driver:1.hook: The cart was already gone, but its wheel tracks glowed faintly on the stone.
driver:1.line: 'I am the *driver* of the sky roads — follow the glow and you will find your next stop.'

sentences.en: A cart rattled across the stone square pulled by two wind-filled sails on wheels.
sentences.cn: 一辆大车在石板广场上吱呀吱呀地滚过，由两张风帆在轮子上驱动。

sentences.en: Its *driver* sat tall on a high bench, wearing a coat covered in small compass roses.
She tossed Old Helm a rolled note as she passed.
sentences.cn: 她经过时向老舵扔了一张卷起的纸条。

sentences.en: Inside was a single word and a rough drawing of an island we had never seen.
sentences.cn: 纸条里面只有一个词，还有一幅我们从未见过的岛屿的粗略草图。

dream:1.en: In the middle of the night market, an old woman sold bottled light. She said each bottle held a *dream* someone had left behind. Old Helm chose a small blue one, uncorked it, and a soft voice read out a word. The word landed on our map and the whole island seemed to breathe out slowly.
dream:1.cnHint: 夜市中，团长打开一瓶装着____的光瓶，里面传出的词语为地图添上了新的一角。
dream:1.hook: The blue light drifted upward and drew the shape of a door in the air.
dream:1.line: 'Every *dream* left in these bottles is a map waiting for the right traveller to open it.'

sentences.en: In the middle of the night market, an old woman sold bottled light.
sentences.cn: 午夜集市的中央，一个老妇人卖装在瓶子里的光。

sentences.en: She said each bottle held a *dream* someone had left behind.
Old Helm chose a small blue one, uncorked it, and a soft voice read out a word.
sentences.cn: 老舵选了一个小蓝瓶，拔开瓶塞，一个温柔的声音读出了一个词。

sentences.en: The word landed on our map and the whole island seemed to breathe out slowly.
sentences.cn: 那个词落在了我们的地图上，整个岛屿似乎缓缓舒了口气。

consumer:1.en: A trader at the far end of the square called out to anyone passing. 'Every *consumer* of starlight leaves a trace,' he said, pointing to the glowing footprints around us. He pressed a card into my hand. On it was a word, and below the word, an arrow pointing straight up toward a cloud island no one had noticed before.
consumer:1.cnHint: 一位商人告诉大家，每一个星光____都会留下踪迹，并递给我一张带有新词的卡片。
consumer:1.hook: Looking up, we saw the cloud island slowly beginning to drift away.
consumer:1.line: 'A wise *consumer* of starlight never wastes a single step on the wrong island.'

sentences.en: A trader at the far end of the square called out to anyone passing.
sentences.cn: 广场远端的一个商人向过路的人叫喊。

sentences.en: 'Every *consumer* of starlight leaves a trace,' he said, pointing to the glowing footprints around us.
He pressed a card into my hand.
sentences.cn: 他把一张卡塞进了我的手里。

sentences.en: On it was a word, and below the word, an arrow pointing straight up toward a cloud island no one had noticed before.
sentences.cn: 卡片上写着一个词，词下面有一支箭，指向正上方一个谁都没注意到的云岛。

interesting:1.en: Bell found a noticeboard covered in papers, each one left by a traveller who had passed through before us. One paper was blank except for a single line: 'The most *interesting* island is the one you build with the words you collect.' Below it, folded small, was a map fragment we added to our growing chart.
interesting:1.cnHint: 小铃在公告栏上找到一张纸条，上面写着只有用词语碎片才能找到最____的岛屿。
interesting:1.hook: The handwriting on the note matched Old Helm's exactly.
interesting:1.line: 'Nothing is more *interesting* than a word that opens a door no one else can see.'

sentences.en: Bell found a noticeboard covered in papers, each one left by a traveller who had passed through before us.
sentences.cn: 小铃发现了一个布告栏，上面贴满了之前经过这里的旅人留下的纸条。

Below it, folded small, was a map fragment we added to our growing chart.
sentences.cn: 下面折得很小的是一张地图碎片，我们把它加到了越来越大的图表中。

grade:1.en: Near the square's fountain, a judge sat at a small table scoring the lanterns that drifted past. He held up a card with a number each time. Old Helm asked what determined the *grade*. 'The brightness of the intention,' the judge said quietly, and handed us a slip of paper with tonight's highest-scoring word written on it.
grade:1.cnHint: 广场喷泉旁，一位评委向团长解释评分____的标准，并将今晚最高分的词语交给了我们。
grade:1.hook: The word on the slip was already glowing, and our map was pulling toward the east.

sentences.en: Near the square's fountain, a judge sat at a small table scoring the lanterns that drifted past.
sentences.cn: 靠近喷泉的地方，一个评委坐在小桌子前，给漂过的灯笼打分。

sentences.en: He held up a card with a number each time.
sentences.cn: 他每次都举起一张印着数字的卡片。

sentences.en: Old Helm asked what determined the *grade*.
'The brightness of the intention,' the judge said quietly, and handed us a slip of paper with tonight's highest-scoring word written on it.
sentences.cn: "意图的光芒，"评委轻声说，递给我们一张纸条，上面写着今晚得分最高的词。

decline:1.en: Old Helm spread the star chart across the cold stone and pointed to the island's edge. 'Look,' he said quietly. The light towers along the western rim showed a steady *decline* — each lamp lower than the last, like steps leading somewhere dark below the clouds.
decline:1.cnHint: 老舵主指着星图边缘，发现西侧灯塔的光芒正在逐渐____。
decline:1.hook: Whatever waited below those clouds was rising toward us.
decline:1.line: 'This *decline* in the lights means the island is sinking,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the star chart across the cold stone and pointed to the island's edge.
sentences.cn: 老舵在冰冷的石板上铺开星图，指向岛的边缘。

sentences.en: 'Look,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "看，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: The light towers along the western rim showed a steady *decline* — each lamp lower than the last, like steps leading somewhere dark below the clouds.

extra:1.en: Bell handed out lanterns before we left camp. She counted heads twice, then reached into her pack and produced one *extra* lantern — small, dented, but burning steady. 'Islands like this one have a way of swallowing torches,' she said, hanging it on my belt without asking.
extra:1.cnHint: 小铃分发灯笼时，多拿出了一盏____的，挂在了我的腰带上。
extra:1.hook: She never explained why she had packed a spare.
extra:1.line: 'Take this *extra* lantern — trust me, you will need it,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell handed out lanterns before we left camp.
sentences.cn: 我们离开营地前，小铃分发了灯笼。

sentences.en: She counted heads twice, then reached into her pack and produced one *extra* lantern — small, dented, but burning steady.
'Islands like this one have a way of swallowing torches,' she said, hanging it on my belt without asking.
sentences.cn: "像这样的岛屿有办法吞掉火把，"她说着，没问过我就把灯笼挂在了我的腰带上。

income:1.en: At the crossroads market, Old Helm bartered three words from his satchel for a warm meal and a rough map. 'Our *income* is words,' he told me as we walked away, 'and we spend them only when the road demands it.' I held my own first word a little tighter.
income:1.cnHint: 老舵主告诉我，旅行团唯一的____就是收集来的"词语"。
income:1.hook: I wondered how many words it would cost to reach the next island.
income:1.line: 'Words are our *income* — spend them wisely on this road,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: At the crossroads market, Old Helm bartered three words from his satchel for a warm meal and a rough map.
sentences.cn: 老舵在十字路口的集市用他口袋里的三个词换了一顿热汤和一张粗糙的地图。

sentences.en: 'Our *income* is words,' he told me as we walked away, 'and we spend them only when the road demands it.'
I held my own first word a little tighter.
sentences.cn: 我紧紧握着自己的第一个词。

medicine:1.en: A child sat on the harbour steps, guarding a basket of small blue bottles. 'What are those?' I asked. 'Star-dew *medicine*,' she said proudly. 'Old Helm buys one every time the troupe passes through. He says the high winds give everyone sore throats.' She held one up to the lantern light.
medicine:1.cnHint: 港口台阶上，一个孩子守着篮子里的星露____，等待旅行团经过。
medicine:1.hook: The blue glow inside each bottle pulsed like a tiny heartbeat.
medicine:1.line: 'This star-dew *medicine* soothes every throat the wind has scratched,' she said.

private:1.en: Silverfang waited at the far end of the bridge, alone, back turned to the crowd. Bell leaned close. 'He keeps a *private* log of every island the troupe has ever visited — names, winds, secrets. He has never shown it to anyone.' Across the bridge, Silverfang tucked something small and leather-bound into his coat.
private:1.cnHint: 小铃悄悄说，竞争船长有一本从不示人的____航行日志。
private:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he was looking our way.
private:1.line: 'That is a *private* record — no one reads it but me,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Silverfang waited at the far end of the bridge, alone, back turned to the crowd.

sentences.en: Bell leaned close.
sentences.cn: 小铃靠近了。

side:1.en: We camped on the sheltered *side* of a great rock that jutted from the island's edge. The wind roared past the far face of it, but here the air was still and warm, thick with the smell of night-blooming moss. Old Helm said the troupe always rested on the quiet side before a crossing.
side:1.cnHint: 我们在巨岩背风的____扎营，远处的风声如同怒吼。
side:1.hook: Come morning, we would have to walk straight into that roar.
side:1.line: 'Always camp on the sheltered *side* — the crossing will be hard enough,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: We camped on the sheltered *side* of a great rock that jutted from the island's edge.
The wind roared past the far face of it, but here the air was still and warm, thick with the smell of night-blooming moss.
sentences.cn: 风在大石头的另一边怒吼，但这里空气静止温暖，夜间开花苔藓的气味浓得化不开。

sentences.en: Old Helm said the troupe always rested on the quiet side before a crossing.
sentences.cn: 老舵说剧团在过海前总是在安静的一侧休整。

air:1.en: The moment we stepped onto the Night-fall Platform, the *air* changed. It tasted of cold metal and something sweet I could not name. Bell breathed in slowly, eyes shut, and smiled. 'That is the smell of a falling star passing close,' she said. 'It means the word we need is already near.'
air:1.cnHint: 踏上星落台时，小铃深吸一口____，说附近有一颗流星刚刚飞过。
air:1.hook: Somewhere just above us, something bright was dropping fast.
air:1.line: 'Breathe this *air* — a falling star has just passed over us,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The moment we stepped onto the Night-fall Platform, the *air* changed.
It tasted of cold metal and something sweet I could not name.
sentences.cn: 空气尝起来像冷金属加上什么我叫不出名字的甜味。

sentences.en: Bell breathed in slowly, eyes shut, and smiled.
sentences.cn: 小铃缓缓吸气，闭上眼睛，露出了笑容。

sentences.cn: 她说，这是流星擦过时才有的味道。

sentences.en: 'It means the word we need is already near.'

consumption:1.en: Old Helm watched the island's great signal fire and frowned. 'The *consumption* of fuel is too fast,' he said. 'Three times the normal rate since last week.' Bell checked her compass. If the fire burned out, the sky-roads mapped from its light would vanish with it, and we would lose our path entirely.
consumption:1.cnHint: 老舵主担心信号火的燃料____过快，一旦熄灭，天空航路就会消失。
consumption:1.hook: The fire shuddered once, as if it had heard him.
consumption:1.line: 'This *consumption* of fuel will leave us blind in the dark,' Old Helm warned.

sentences.en: Old Helm watched the island's great signal fire and frowned.
sentences.cn: 老舵看着岛上那场信号火，皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: 'The *consumption* of fuel is too fast,' he said.
'Three times the normal rate since last week.'
sentences.cn: 自上周以来，消耗的速度是正常的三倍。

sentences.en: Bell checked her compass.
sentences.cn: 小铃查了一下她的指南针。

sentences.en: If the fire burned out, the sky-roads mapped from its light would vanish with it, and we would lose our path entirely.
sentences.cn: 要是火灭了，那些靠火光映出来的空中航线就会跟着消失，我们就彻底没路了。

field:1.en: The troupe landed on a wide, flat island where the grass had been cut short and white lines painted across the ground. Old Helm called it a *field* — once a place where people raced and cheered, now silent under drifting stars. Somewhere beneath the grass, he said, a word was buried.
field:1.cnHint: 老舵主说，这片____下面埋着一个字。
field:1.hook: The ground trembled, and the painted lines began to glow.
field:1.line: 'Every *field* holds the memory of the crowd that once stood here,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The troupe landed on a wide, flat island where the grass had been cut short and white lines painted across the ground.
sentences.cn: 剧团在一座宽阔平坦的岛屿上着陆，草被割得很短，地上涂着白色的线条。

sentences.en: Old Helm called it a *field* — once a place where people raced and cheered, now silent under drifting stars.
Somewhere beneath the grass, he said, a word was buried.
sentences.cn: 他说，草下面某个地方埋着一个词。

personality:1.en: Bell studied the new map fragment with a careful eye. Each island, she explained, had its own *personality* — one island was bold and windy, another shy and wrapped in fog. Knowing an island's nature, she said, was the only safe way to land without trouble.
personality:1.cnHint: 领航员小铃解释，每座岛都有自己独特的____。
personality:1.hook: The next island on the map wore an expression no one could read.
personality:1.line: 'Its *personality* is wild and proud — we must land gently,' Bell warned.

sentences.en: Bell studied the new map fragment with a careful eye.
sentences.cn: 小铃用仔细的目光研究这份新的地图碎片。

sentences.en: Each island, she explained, had its own *personality* — one island was bold and windy, another shy and wrapped in fog.
Knowing an island's nature, she said, was the only safe way to land without trouble.
sentences.cn: 她说，懂得一个岛屿的性格，才是安全着陆不出事的唯一办法。

size:1.en: From the deck, the island ahead looked small enough to hold in one hand. But as we sailed closer, its true *size* became clear — cliffs rose as tall as clouds, and forests spread as far as the eye could follow. Old Helm let out a low whistle.
size:1.cnHint: 靠近后，众人才意识到这座岛的____远超想象。
size:1.hook: Something enormous moved beneath the canopy of trees.
size:1.line: 'Never judge the *size* of an island from a distance,' Old Helm said quietly.

sentences.en: From the deck, the island ahead looked small enough to hold in one hand.
sentences.cn: 从甲板上看，前面那个岛小到能握在手心里。

sentences.en: But as we sailed closer, its true *size* became clear — cliffs rose as tall as clouds, and forests spread as far as the eye could follow.
Old Helm let out a low whistle.
sentences.cn: 老舵吹了一声低沉的口哨。

schedule:1.en: Bell pinned a new sheet to the mast each morning — the day's *schedule*, neat rows of tasks and times. Today it listed: repair the sail, trade for fruit at the next port, and reach the star-mirror island before dark. The troupe moved with purpose.
schedule:1.cnHint: 小铃每天早晨都会把新的____贴在桅杆上。
schedule:1.hook: Today's final task had no time written next to it — only a question mark.
schedule:1.line: 'The *schedule* says we dock before the second star rises,' Bell reminded us.

sentences.en: Bell pinned a new sheet to the mast each morning — the day's *schedule*, neat rows of tasks and times.
Today it listed: repair the sail, trade for fruit at the next port, and reach the star-mirror island before dark.
sentences.cn: 今天的单子上写着：修帆、在下一个港口换水果、天黑前到达星镜岛。

sentences.en: The troupe moved with purpose.
sentences.cn: 剧团的人干起活来井井有条。

towards:1.en: A ribbon of light appeared on the horizon, pale gold and steady. Old Helm turned the wheel slowly, pointing the bow *towards* it without a word. The rest of us leaned forward, scarves lifting in the warm wind, as the light grew wider and the unknown came nearer.
towards:1.cnHint: 老舵主默默将船头朝____那道光驶去。
towards:1.hook: The light pulsed once, as if it had noticed us coming.
towards:1.line: 'We sail *towards* the light, whatever waits inside it,' Old Helm decided.

sentences.en: A ribbon of light appeared on the horizon, pale gold and steady.
sentences.cn: 地平线上出现了一条光带，淡金色，稳稳地闪烁。

sentences.en: Old Helm turned the wheel slowly, pointing the bow *towards* it without a word.

sentences.cn: 我们都身体前倾，围巾在温暖的风中飘起来，看着那束光越来越宽，未知的东西也越来越近。

background:1.en: The new island rose steeply, and carved into the rock face behind the market stalls was a mosaic of coloured stone. Bell said the mosaic was the island's *background* — its history told in pictures so that even visitors with no shared language could understand where they had arrived.
background:1.cnHint: 小铃说，那面彩石马赛克记录着这座岛的____。
background:1.hook: One picture in the mosaic showed our own ship, though we had never been here before.
background:1.line: 'The *background* of this island is older than any map we carry,' Bell said softly.

sentences.en: The new island rose steeply, and carved into the rock face behind the market stalls was a mosaic of coloured stone.
sentences.cn: 这座岛屿陡峭地拔起，市集摊位后面的岩石上雕着一幅彩色石头的镶嵌画。

sentences.en: Bell said the mosaic was the island's *background* — its history told in pictures so that even visitors with no shared language could understand where they had arrived.

department:1.en: The floating market was divided into bright sections, each with its own colour of lantern. The word-seller's *department* hung silver lanterns and kept the quietest corner of all. Old Helm led us straight there, past spice stalls and rope merchants, without stopping once.
department:1.cnHint: 字词商人的____挂着银色灯笼，是集市最安静的角落。
department:1.hook: The word-seller looked up before we arrived, as though she had expected us.
department:1.line: 'Welcome to my *department* — every word here wants to be found,' she smiled.

sentences.en: The floating market was divided into bright sections, each with its own colour of lantern.
sentences.cn: 浮动市集被分成几个亮闪闪的区域，每个区域都挂着自己颜色的灯笼。

sentences.en: The word-seller's *department* hung silver lanterns and kept the quietest corner of all.

sentences.cn: 老舵直接带我们过去，穿过香料摊和绳索商人，一步都没停。

detail:1.en: Silverfang spread a rival map across a barrel and tapped one corner with a sharp finger. 'Your chart is missing a *detail*,' she said. A tiny symbol, shaped like a crescent, marked a passage between two storm clouds that our own map left blank. We had nearly flown into those clouds.
detail:1.cnHint: 竞争船长银牙指出，我们的地图上少了一个重要的____。
detail:1.hook: Silverfang rolled the map back up and did not offer to share it.
detail:1.line: 'One missing *detail* can send a whole ship off course,' Silverfang said flatly.

sentences.en: Silverfang spread a rival map across a barrel and tapped one corner with a sharp finger.
sentences.cn: 银牙把一张对手的地图铺在一个桶上，用尖锐的手指戳了戳角落。

sentences.en: 'Your chart is missing a *detail*,' she said.
A tiny symbol, shaped like a crescent, marked a passage between two storm clouds that our own map left blank.
sentences.cn: 一个新月形的小符号标记了两朵风暴云之间的一条通道，我们的地图上那儿是空白的。

sentences.en: We had nearly flown into those clouds.
sentences.cn: 我们差点就飞进那些云里去了。

rule:1.en: The market square of Cinderstone Island glowed under a hundred lanterns. An old stone post stood at its centre, carved with the words: 'One *rule* governs this place — every trader must give a word before taking a word.' Old Helm pressed his hand to the post and smiled. 'Perfect,' he said. 'We already have plenty to trade.'
rule:1.cnHint: 石碑上刻着这里的____：每位商人必须先给出一个词才能换取一个词，老船长欣然接受。
rule:1.hook: But the last trader in the square had vanished, leaving only a single glowing coin.
rule:1.line: 'One *rule* governs this island, and tonight it works in our favour.'

sentences.en: The market square of Cinderstone Island glowed under a hundred lanterns.
sentences.cn: 灰烬岛的市集广场在百盏灯笼下闪闪发光。

sentences.en: An old stone post stood at its centre, carved with the words: 'One *rule* governs this place — every trader must give a word before taking a word.'
Old Helm pressed his hand to the post and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手按在石柱上，笑了。

sentences.en: 'Perfect,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说，完美。

sentences.en: 'We already have plenty to trade.'
sentences.cn: 我们已经有一大堆词可以拿来交易了。

plant:1.en: Bell led us off the main path to a narrow ledge where a single *plant* grew from a crack in the rock — its leaves silver, its tiny flowers shaped like open eyes. 'The islanders call it a sky-reader,' she said softly. Old Helm crouched beside it and whispered the word we had come for. The plant shivered, and a new map fragment drifted down like a leaf.
plant:1.cnHint: 贝尔带众人找到一株奇特的____，老船长轻声说出关键词后，它颤动着给出了一张地图碎片。
plant:1.hook: The silver leaves began to fold shut, as though the island itself was listening.
plant:1.line: 'Touch that *plant* gently — it remembers every hand that has ever reached for it.'

sentences.en: Bell led us off the main path to a narrow ledge where a single *plant* grew from a crack in the rock — its leaves silver, its tiny flowers shaped like open eyes.
'The islanders call it a sky-reader,' she said softly.
sentences.cn: '岛民们叫它"读天草"，'她轻声说。

sentences.en: Old Helm crouched beside it and whispered the word we had come for.
sentences.cn: 老舵蹲在它旁边，低声说出了我们来这里要找的那个词。

national:1.en: A wide banner hung across the gate of the Highbridge Island fair. It read: 'The *National* Gathering of Sky Traders — all islands welcome.' Old Helm spread his arms wide. 'Every troupe in the sky is here,' he said happily. Silverfang appeared beside us, arms crossed, already scanning the crowd for rivals. 'Then every word we need is here too,' I realised.

national:1.hook: Somewhere in that crowd, someone already held the word we needed most.
national:1.line: 'This *national* gathering only happens once every hundred star-turns — do not waste it.'

sentences.en: A wide banner hung across the gate of the Highbridge Island fair.
