sentences.cn: 她把它夹在腋下，嘴角带着笑容，仿佛已经知道上面写的是什么。

rely:2.en: The bridge of vines between the two islands had begun to fray. Old Helm tested it with one boot and shook his head. 'We *rely* on this path every season,' he said quietly, almost to himself. He knelt and began to weave the loose strands back together with careful hands.
rely:2.cnHint: 藤桥开始老化，老舵说我们每个季节都____这条路，他开始动手修缮。
rely:2.hook: Halfway across, the whole bridge gave a long, slow groan.
rely:2.line: 'We *rely* on this path — so we must also mend it.'

sentences.en: The bridge of vines between the two islands had begun to fray.
sentences.cn: 连接两座岛屿的藤蔓桥开始破损了。

sentences.en: Old Helm tested it with one boot and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 老舵用一只靴子踩了踩，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'We *rely* on this path every season,' he said quietly, almost to himself.
He knelt and began to weave the loose strands back together with careful hands.
sentences.cn: 他跪了下来，用粗糙的手开始小心地把散开的藤条重新编织在一起。

connect:2.en: Bell discovered two stone pillars on opposite ends of the island, each carved with half a sentence. When she placed her palm on one, the carvings lit up and a thin thread of light began to *connect* the two pillars across the open sky. The air smelled of pine and distant rain.
connect:2.cnHint: 小铃发现两根石柱各刻着半句话，她触碰其中一根后，光线开始____它们。
connect:2.hook: The completed sentence spelled a name none of us recognised.
connect:2.line: 'Touch both stones and let the light *connect* them.'

sentences.en: Bell discovered two stone pillars on opposite ends of the island, each carved with half a sentence.
sentences.cn: 小铃在岛的两端发现了两根石柱，每根上都刻着半句话。

sentences.en: When she placed her palm on one, the carvings lit up and a thin thread of light began to *connect* the two pillars across the open sky.
The air smelled of pine and distant rain.
sentences.cn: 空气里弥漫着松树和远方雨水的味道。

indicate:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a thin copper sheet printed with dozens of tiny arrows. Each arrow pointed toward the centre of the sheet where a single island shape was drawn. 'These arrows *indicate* where the next fragment is hidden,' he said. I counted twelve arrows. They all agreed.
indicate:2.cnHint: 老舵展开铜片，说上面的箭头____着下一块碎片藏在何处。
indicate:2.hook: One arrow, unlike the rest, pointed straight up.
indicate:2.line: 'All these arrows *indicate* the same island — we leave at dawn.'

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a thin copper sheet printed with dozens of tiny arrows.
sentences.cn: 老舵展开了一张薄薄的铜片，上面印满了几十个细小的箭头。

sentences.en: Each arrow pointed toward the centre of the sheet where a single island shape was drawn.
sentences.cn: 每个箭头都指向纸张的中心，那里画着一个孤独的岛屿轮廓。

sentences.en: 'These arrows *indicate* where the next fragment is hidden,' he said.
I counted twelve arrows.
sentences.cn: 我数了数，一共十二个箭头。

sentences.en: They all agreed.
sentences.cn: 大家都数出了一样的数字。

period:2.en: Bell found a log book wedged behind a loose stone in the wall. Its pages described a *period* of great storms that had once scattered the floating islands far apart. During those years, she read aloud, the troupe had kept going by collecting one word at a time.
period:2.cnHint: 小铃找到一本航海日志，记录了一段____，那时风暴将各岛吹散，船队靠收集词语坚持前行。
period:2.hook: The last entry was dated the very night I joined the troupe.
period:2.line: 'That *period* of storms is what made the troupe who they are.'

sentences.en: Bell found a log book wedged behind a loose stone in the wall.
sentences.cn: 小铃在墙上一块松动的石头后面找到了一本航海日志。

sentences.en: Its pages described a *period* of great storms that had once scattered the floating islands far apart.
During those years, she read aloud, the troupe had kept going by collecting one word at a time.
sentences.cn: 她读出来，在那些年里，为了活下去，全队人靠一次收集一个词的办法坚持着。

picture:2.en: Tucked inside the cracked lantern at the camp's edge was a small *picture* — ink on bark — showing three figures standing on an island that none of us recognised. Bell held it up to the starlight. Old Helm went very still, then said softly, 'I drew that years ago.'
picture:2.cnHint: 营地旧灯笼里藏着一幅____，画着三个站在陌生岛屿上的人影，老舵认出了它。
picture:2.hook: The island in the drawing matched the one on our next map.
picture:2.line: 'I drew this *picture* the night we first set sail together.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside the cracked lantern at the camp's edge was a small *picture* — ink on bark — showing three figures standing on an island that none of us recognised.
Bell held it up to the starlight.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它举到星光下。

sentences.en: Old Helm went very still, then said softly, 'I drew that years ago.'
sentences.cn: 老舵忽然变得很沉静，然后轻声说，"那是我多年前画的。"

relate:2.en: Old Helm spread the star-map across the deck and began to *relate* the story of the lost island to Bell and me. Each detail connected to the next like links in a chain. The stars above blinked as if they, too, were listening.
relate:2.cnHint: 老船长向大家____着失落岛屿的故事，每个细节都紧密相连。
relate:2.hook: But the last detail made Bell go very quiet.
relate:2.line: 'Let me *relate* what the old chart says, before the stars shift.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the star-map across the deck and began to *relate* the story of the lost island to Bell and me.
Each detail connected to the next like links in a chain.
sentences.cn: 每个细节都像链条一样相互连接。

sentences.en: The stars above blinked as if they, too, were listening.
sentences.cn: 头顶的星星眨眼着，好像它们也在倾听。

attitude:2.en: Bell stood at the bow with a straight back and lifted chin — her whole *attitude* said she had no fear of the dark sky ahead. Old Helm watched her and smiled. 'That one was born for floating islands,' he said softly.
attitude:2.cnHint: 贝尔的____让老舵长感叹她天生就是为浮岛而生的。
attitude:2.hook: Then the wind turned, and even Bell's shoulders dropped a little.
attitude:2.line: 'Your *attitude* at the bow tells me you have sailed before.'

sentences.en: Bell stood at the bow with a straight back and lifted chin — her whole *attitude* said she had no fear of the dark sky ahead.
Old Helm watched her and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵看着她，笑了。

sentences.en: 'That one was born for floating islands,' he said softly.
sentences.cn: "这个姑娘是为漂浮的岛屿而生的，"他轻声说。

fill:2.en: We pulled open the old chest and found it packed with glowing fragments — enough to *fill* every blank corner of our map for weeks. Bell gasped. Old Helm simply nodded, as if he had always known such a treasure was waiting here among the stars.
fill:2.cnHint: 我们打开宝箱，发现里面的碎片足以____地图上所有空白处。
fill:2.hook: One fragment, however, was shaped like a door.
fill:2.line: 'These fragments will *fill* the map all the way to the edge.'

sentences.en: We pulled open the old chest and found it packed with glowing fragments — enough to *fill* every blank corner of our map for weeks.
Bell gasped.
sentences.cn: 小铃惊呼一声。

sentences.en: Old Helm simply nodded, as if he had always known such a treasure was waiting here among the stars.
sentences.cn: 老舵只是点了点头，仿佛他一直都知道这样的宝藏在星辰之间等着我们。

ignore:2.en: A soft chime rang from inside the locked lantern hanging at the mast. I tried to *ignore* it and keep sorting the map pieces, but the sound grew warmer and more insistent, as though the lantern itself had something urgent to say to me alone.
ignore:2.cnHint: 桅杆上的灯笼发出铃声，叙述者想____它，却发现声音越来越急切。
ignore:2.hook: When I finally looked, a tiny face was pressed against the glass.
ignore:2.line: 'Do not *ignore* that lantern — it only chimes when danger is close.'

sentences.en: A soft chime rang from inside the locked lantern hanging at the mast.
sentences.cn: 一声柔和的鸣响从桅杆上挂着的上锁灯笼内传出。

sentences.en: I tried to *ignore* it and keep sorting the map pieces, but the sound grew warmer and more insistent, as though the lantern itself had something urgent to say to me alone.

necessary:2.en: Bell checked the rigging, tested the wind, then marked two words on the chart in red. 'Only these two stops are *necessary*,' she said firmly. 'The rest are pretty, but they will not get us to the night-fall island before the stars move.'
necessary:2.cnHint: 贝尔告诉大家，只有两个停靠点是____的，其余的都可以跳过。
necessary:2.hook: Old Helm crossed out one of her red marks without a word.
necessary:2.line: 'One stop is *necessary* — skip it and we lose the wind entirely.'

sentences.en: Bell checked the rigging, tested the wind, then marked two words on the chart in red.
sentences.cn: 小铃检查了索具，试了试风向，然后在海图上用红笔标出了两个词。

sentences.en: 'Only these two stops are *necessary*,' she said firmly.
'The rest are pretty, but they will not get us to the night-fall island before the stars move.'
sentences.cn: "只有这两个地方是必经的，"她坚定地说，"其余的都很漂亮，但赶不上星辰移动之前到达夜幕岛。"

definitely:2.en: I held the glowing shard up to the night sky, and the pattern on it *definitely* matched the cluster of stars just above the eastern edge of our map. Old Helm leaned in close. 'Good eyes,' he said. 'We know where we are going now.'
definitely:2.cnHint: 叙述者发现碎片上的图案____与星图东侧的星群吻合。
definitely:2.hook: Yet the matched stars were already beginning to drift apart.
definitely:2.line: 'That marking is *definitely* the eastern gate — I have seen it before.'

sentences.en: I held the glowing shard up to the night sky, and the pattern on it *definitely* matched the cluster of stars just above the eastern edge of our map.
Old Helm leaned in close.
sentences.cn: 老舵靠得很近。

sentences.en: 'Good eyes,' he said.
sentences.cn: "眼力不错，"他说。

sentences.en: 'We know where we are going now.'
sentences.cn: "现在我们知道要去哪儿了。"

forget:2.en: Old Helm pressed a small carved coin into my hand before I climbed down to sleep. 'Do not *forget* this,' he said quietly. 'Every island gives one token. Lose it and the island will not let you return.' I closed my fingers around it tight.
forget:2.cnHint: 老舵长叮嘱叙述者不要____那枚小硬币，因为失去它就无法重返那座岛。
forget:2.hook: I dreamed of the coin melting like warm starlight.
forget:2.line: 'Do not *forget* the token — the island will close its gate to you.'

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed a small carved coin into my hand before I climbed down to sleep.
sentences.cn: 在我爬下去睡觉前，老舵把一枚小小的雕刻硬币塞进了我的手里。

sentences.en: 'Do not *forget* this,' he said quietly.
'Every island gives one token.
sentences.cn: "每座岛都会给一枚令牌。

sentences.en: Lose it and the island will not let you return.'
sentences.cn: 丢了它，岛就不会让你回来。"

sentences.en: I closed my fingers around it tight.
sentences.cn: 我紧紧地把它握在手心里。

particularly:2.en: The night market on the edge of the cloud-dock sold all manner of strange things, but one stall caught my eye *particularly* — a row of tiny bottled sounds, each one buzzing with a different voice. Bell picked one up and tilted her head, listening hard.
particularly:2.cnHint: 夜市里有一个摊位____吸引了叙述者的注意——那里摆着一排装着声音的小瓶子。
particularly:2.hook: The voice inside the bottle said my name.
particularly:2.line: 'This bottle *particularly* feels warm — as if it has been waiting for us.'

sentences.en: The night market on the edge of the cloud-dock sold all manner of strange things, but one stall caught my eye *particularly* — a row of tiny bottled sounds, each one buzzing with a different voice.
Bell picked one up and tilted her head, listening hard.
sentences.cn: 小铃捡起一个，歪着头，认真地听。

model:2.en: Deep inside the library island, Bell lifted a glass case from a dusty shelf. Inside sat a tiny *model* of all the floating islands, each one linked by silver threads. 'This is how the whole sky-map fits together,' she said softly. Every island we had visited glowed with a faint light.
model:2.cnHint: 小铃在图书馆岛发现了一个浮岛群的____，每座已到访的岛都在发光。
model:2.hook: But one island on the model had no thread at all.
model:2.line: 'This *model* shows every island we still need to find.'

sentences.en: Deep inside the library island, Bell lifted a glass case from a dusty shelf.
sentences.cn: 在图书馆岛的深处，小铃从落满灰尘的架子上取下一个玻璃罩。

sentences.en: Inside sat a tiny *model* of all the floating islands, each one linked by silver threads.
'This is how the whole sky-map fits together,' she said softly.
sentences.cn: "整个天空地图就是这样拼在一起的，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: Every island we had visited glowed with a faint light.
sentences.cn: 我们去过的每座岛都闪烁着微弱的光。

spot:2.en: We drifted over the Mirror Flats, a wide island covered in still pools. Old Helm pressed a finger to his lips, then pointed down. I squinted and managed to *spot* a single glowing word half-buried in the silver sand below one of the pools. My heart jumped straight into my throat.
spot:2.cnHint: 在镜面平原，叙述者终于____了藏在水池下沙中的发光词语。
spot:2.hook: The word began to sink deeper the moment I saw it.
spot:2.line: 'Quick — did you *spot* it before it disappears?'

sentences.en: We drifted over the Mirror Flats, a wide island covered in still pools.
sentences.cn: 我们漂浮过镜面平原，一个岛屿广阔而光滑，覆盖着静止的池塘。

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed a finger to his lips, then pointed down.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手指放在嘴唇上，然后向下指。

sentences.en: I squinted and managed to *spot* a single glowing word half-buried in the silver sand below one of the pools.
My heart jumped straight into my throat.
sentences.cn: 我的心一下子跳到了嗓子眼。

achievement:2.en: At the top of Crestfall Tower, a stone board listed every troupe that had ever passed through. Old Helm ran his finger along the names until he found ours, freshly carved. 'Reaching the top floor is no small *achievement*,' he said, his old eyes bright. I stood a little taller without meaning to.
achievement:2.cnHint: 在高塔顶层，老舵指着石板上的记录，称赞众人的____。
achievement:2.hook: Below our name, someone had carved a warning we could not yet read.
achievement:2.line: 'Finishing that climb is a real *achievement* for any new member.'

sentences.en: At the top of Crestfall Tower, a stone board listed every troupe that had ever passed through.
sentences.cn: 在崖顶塔的顶端，一块石板上列出了所有曾经经过这里的剧团。

sentences.en: Old Helm ran his finger along the names until he found ours, freshly carved.
sentences.cn: 老舵用手指沿着名字滑过去，直到找到我们的名字，刚刚刻下来的。

sentences.en: 'Reaching the top floor is no small *achievement*,' he said, his old eyes bright.
I stood a little taller without meaning to.
sentences.cn: 我不由自主地挺直了腰。

enter:2.en: A narrow gate of woven starlight blocked the path to the Inkwell Caves. Bell read the faded sign aloud: only those who carry a living word may *enter*. Old Helm nodded at me and placed a glowing word-fragment gently into my palm. The gate hummed, shivered, and swung open.
enter:2.cnHint: 通往墨水洞穴的星光之门只允许携带词语的人____。
enter:2.hook: A cold wind rushed out from the dark beyond the gate.
enter:2.line: 'Hold your word up and *enter* — the cave will know you.'

sentences.en: A narrow gate of woven starlight blocked the path to the Inkwell Caves.
sentences.cn: 一扇用星光编织成的狭窄大门挡住了通往墨井洞窟的路。

sentences.en: Bell read the faded sign aloud: only those who carry a living word may *enter*.
Old Helm nodded at me and placed a glowing word-fragment gently into my palm.
sentences.cn: 老舵朝我点了点头，轻轻地把一个闪闪发光的词语碎片放在了我的手心。

sentences.en: The gate hummed, shivered, and swung open.
sentences.cn: 大门嗡鸣着，颤抖着，然后打开了。

eye:2.en: Silverfang found us on the Cloud Step Bridge, leaning on the rail as if she had been there all morning. She had a sharp *eye* for rare word-fragments; a small blue one glinted in her coat pocket. She tossed it into the air once, caught it, and smiled without saying a word.
eye:2.cnHint: 银牙凭借敏锐的____，早早发现了桥上那枚珍贵的蓝色词语碎片。
eye:2.hook: That fragment was the exact one Old Helm had been hunting for years.
eye:2.line: 'You need a good *eye* to find the blue ones before dawn.'

sentences.en: Silverfang found us on the Cloud Step Bridge, leaning on the rail as if she had been there all morning.
sentences.cn: 银牙在云阶桥上找到了我们，靠着栏杆，仿佛她整个上午都在那里。

sentences.en: She had a sharp *eye* for rare word-fragments; a small blue one glinted in her coat pocket.
She tossed it into the air once, caught it, and smiled without saying a word.
sentences.cn: 她把它扔向空中一次，接住了，咧嘴一笑，什么也没说。

shift:2.en: We were resting on Amber Ledge when the whole island gave a slow *shift*, tilting just enough to roll our cups across the deck. Bell checked her charts and went pale. 'It is drifting off the mapped lane,' she said quietly. Above us, the star patterns had already begun to change.
shift:2.cnHint: 在琥珀崖休息时，岛屿发生了____，小铃发现它已偏离既定航道。
shift:2.hook: The next island on their route was drifting away just as fast.
shift:2.line: 'That *shift* in the island means we have very little time left.'

sentences.en: We were resting on Amber Ledge when the whole island gave a slow *shift*, tilting just enough to roll our cups across the deck.
Bell checked her charts and went pale.
sentences.cn: 小铃查看了她的海图，脸色苍白。

sentences.en: 'It is drifting off the mapped lane,' she said quietly.
sentences.cn: "它偏离了标绘的航道，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: Above us, the star patterns had already begun to change.
sentences.cn: 我们上方，星辰的图案已经开始改变了。

agree:2.en: Old Helm spread the word-map on the deck and looked from Bell to me. 'We go south toward the Storm Ring, or north to the Quiet Shelf. I say north.' Bell crossed her arms, then slowly nodded. 'I *agree*,' she said. They both turned to me, and for the first time, my vote would break the tie.
agree:2.cnHint: 面对两条路线的抉择，小铃表示____老舵的方案，但最终由叙述者投出关键一票。
agree:2.hook: My finger hovered above the map, trembling just slightly.
agree:2.line: 'I *agree* with north — the Quiet Shelf holds the word we need.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the word-map on the deck and looked from Bell to me.
sentences.cn: 老舵在甲板上展开了词图，目光在小铃和我之间扫过。

sentences.en: 'We go south toward the Storm Ring, or north to the Quiet Shelf.
sentences.cn: "我们可以向南驶向风暴环，也可以向北去寂静架。

sentences.en: I say north.'
sentences.cn: 我投票去北边。"

sentences.en: Bell crossed her arms, then slowly nodded.
sentences.cn: 小铃交叉双臂，然后慢慢点了点头。

sentences.en: 'I *agree*,' she said.
They both turned to me, and for the first time, my vote would break the tie.
sentences.cn: 他们俩都转向我，这一次，我的选择将打破僵局。

aware:2.en: I was copying the star chart when Bell sat beside me and spoke low. 'Are you *aware* that the word we found today is one of the rarest in the whole sky?' I had not known. I looked at the tiny fragment glowing in the jar and felt the weight of it settle over me like a second coat.
aware:2.cnHint: 小铃悄悄告诉叙述者，他们今天找到的词语十分珍贵，问他是否____这一点。
aware:2.hook: She then told me what that word was rumoured to unlock.
aware:2.line: 'I want you to be *aware* — this word changes everything for our route.'

sentences.en: I was copying the star chart when Bell sat beside me and spoke low.
sentences.cn: 我正在抄绘星图，小铃坐到我身边，压低了声音说话。

sentences.en: 'Are you *aware* that the word we found today is one of the rarest in the whole sky?'
I had not known.
sentences.cn: 我之前不知道。

sentences.en: I looked at the tiny fragment glowing in the jar and felt the weight of it settle over me like a second coat.
sentences.cn: 我看着罐子里发光的细小碎片，感觉它的分量像第二件外套一样沉沉地压在我身上。

management:2.en: The old chest at the centre of Dustmere Island held not gold but a rolled-up chart. Old Helm lifted it carefully and smiled. 'Good *management* of records is what keeps a troupe alive,' he said. Every route we had ever sailed was drawn there in faded ink, waiting to guide us forward.
management:2.cnHint: 老舵在浮岛中央的旧箱子里发现了一份航行记录图，感慨____的重要性。
management:2.hook: One route on the chart led somewhere none of us recognised.
management:2.line: 'Good *management* of records is what keeps a troupe alive.'

sentences.en: The old chest at the centre of Dustmere Island held not gold but a rolled-up chart.
sentences.cn: 尘雾岛中央的古老木箱里装的不是黄金，而是一张卷起来的图。

sentences.en: Old Helm lifted it carefully and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵小心翼翼地抬起它，露出了笑容。

sentences.en: 'Good *management* of records is what keeps a troupe alive,' he said.
Every route we had ever sailed was drawn there in faded ink, waiting to guide us forward.
sentences.cn: 我们曾经航行过的每一条路线都用褪色的墨水画在上面，等着为我们指引方向。

perfect:2.en: Bell held the small glass sphere up to the starlight and turned it slowly. Inside, a tiny island floated in pale mist. 'It is a *perfect* model of Mirren Isle,' she whispered. We had searched three clouds for this thing. Now the word carved on its base glowed, and a new path opened across the sky.
perfect:2.cnHint: 小铃找到了一个玻璃球，里面有一座浮岛的____微缩模型，新路径随之开启。
perfect:2.hook: The glow from the sphere spelled a word none of us had ever spoken.
perfect:2.line: 'It is a *perfect* model of Mirren Isle,' she whispered.

sentences.en: Bell held the small glass sphere up to the starlight and turned it slowly.
sentences.cn: 小铃举起那个小玻璃球对着星光，慢慢转动它。

sentences.en: Inside, a tiny island floated in pale mist.
sentences.cn: 球内，一座tiny小岛浮在淡淡的雾气中。

sentences.en: 'It is a *perfect* model of Mirren Isle,' she whispered.
We had searched three clouds for this thing.
sentences.cn: 我们为了找这东西在三片云里翻腾。

sentences.en: Now the word carved on its base glowed, and a new path opened across the sky.
sentences.cn: 现在球底部刻着的词开始发光，天空上开启了一条新的路。

along:2.en: A line of lanterns hung *along* the rope bridge between Ashfen Island and the cloud beyond. Old Helm found a folded note tied to the third lantern. It read: follow the lights, trust the gaps. We did. At the far end, a stone pillar held our next word, still warm as if placed moments ago.
along:2.cnHint: 绳桥上的灯笼____延伸，老舵在第三盏灯处发现了一张神秘纸条。
along:2.hook: The stone pillar had no footprints around it, yet the word was fresh.
along:2.line: 'Walk *along* the lanterns and do not look down,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: A line of lanterns hung *along* the rope bridge between Ashfen Island and the cloud beyond.
Old Helm found a folded note tied to the third lantern.
sentences.cn: 老舵在第三盏灯笼上找到了一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: It read: follow the lights, trust the gaps.
sentences.cn: 纸条上写着：跟着灯光走，相信那些空隙。

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.cn: 我们照做了。

sentences.en: At the far end, a stone pillar held our next word, still warm as if placed moments ago.
sentences.cn: 在远端，一根石柱上放着我们的下一个词，还温热得像刚放上去没多久。

harm:2.en: Silverfang picked up the cracked lens from the floor of the old signal tower. 'Rain and salt water can *harm* even the strongest glass,' she said quietly. But the lens still worked well enough: tilted at the right angle, it caught starlight and cast a bright word on the far wall — our next destination.
harm:2.cnHint: 银牙在信号塔里发现一片破损的镜片，感叹风雨能____坚固的玻璃，但镜片仍映出了下一个目的地。
harm:2.hook: The word on the wall flickered once, then pointed east.
harm:2.line: 'Rain and salt can *harm* even the strongest glass,' Silverfang said quietly.

sentences.en: Silverfang picked up the cracked lens from the floor of the old signal tower.
sentences.cn: 银牙从古老信号塔的地板上捡起了那块裂开的透镜。

sentences.en: 'Rain and salt water can *harm* even the strongest glass,' she said quietly.
But the lens still worked well enough: tilted at the right angle, it caught starlight and cast a bright word on the far wall — our next destination.
sentences.cn: 但透镜的效能还足够好：以正确的角度倾斜，它能捕捉星光，在远处的墙上投出一个发亮的词——我们的下一个目的地。

increasingly:2.en: The fog around Veilreach Island grew *increasingly* thick as we descended from the ship. Bell kept one hand on the guide-rope and the other stretched ahead. Then her fingers touched something solid: a stone box half-buried in the cloud-floor, its lid engraved with the word we needed. She laughed with relief.
increasingly:2.cnHint: 在Veilreach岛，浓雾____加深，小铃摸索中意外发现了刻有关键词的石盒。
increasingly:2.hook: The stone box was sealed — and the engraving was still wet.
increasingly:2.line: 'The fog grows *increasingly* thick; stay close,' Bell called back to us.

sentences.en: The fog around Veilreach Island grew *increasingly* thick as we descended from the ship.
Bell kept one hand on the guide-rope and the other stretched ahead.
sentences.cn: 小铃一只手按在导绳上，另一只手向前伸探。

sentences.en: Then her fingers touched something solid: a stone box half-buried in the cloud-floor, its lid engraved with the word we needed.
sentences.cn: 然后她的手指碰到了什么坚硬的东西：半埋在云雾地面上的石盒，盒盖上刻着我们需要的那个词。

sentences.en: She laughed with relief.
sentences.cn: 她松了口气，笑出了声。

opinion:2.en: Old Helm, Silverfang, and Bell stood around the carved pillar on Greyvane Isle, each pointing a different direction. 'In my *opinion*,' said Bell, 'the arrow points east.' Silverfang disagreed. I looked closer and noticed a small star etched beneath the arrow. East was right. Bell grinned, and we set our course.
opinion:2.cnHint: 三人对Greyvane岛石柱上箭头的方向意见不一，小铃坚持自己的____，最终被证实正确。
opinion:2.hook: East meant flying straight into the storm wall — but we went anyway.
opinion:2.line: 'In my *opinion*, the arrow points east,' said Bell with a calm smile.

sentences.en: Old Helm, Silverfang, and Bell stood around the carved pillar on Greyvane Isle, each pointing a different direction.
sentences.cn: 老舵、银牙和小铃站在灰烷岛的刻有纹样的石柱周围，各自指向不同的方向。

sentences.en: 'In my *opinion*,' said Bell, 'the arrow points east.'
Silverfang disagreed.
sentences.cn: 银牙不同意。

sentences.en: I looked closer and noticed a small star etched beneath the arrow.
sentences.cn: 我靠近看，注意到箭头下刻着一颗小星星。

sentences.en: East was right.
sentences.cn: 东方是对的。

sentences.en: Bell grinned, and we set our course.
sentences.cn: 小铃咧嘴一笑，我们调整了航向。

previous:2.en: Tucked inside the wall of the old waystation was a worn logbook. Its *previous* entries were written in three different hands — travellers who had passed through long before us. The last entry ended mid-sentence, but the final word written was exactly the word we were searching for. We added our own line below.
previous:2.cnHint: 在废弃中转站的旧航行日志里，____旅人留下的记录中藏着我们寻找的关键词。
previous:2.hook: The mid-sentence entry cut off with a single question mark.
previous:2.line: 'The *previous* travellers left us more than we expected,' said Old Helm softly.

sentences.en: Tucked inside the wall of the old waystation was a worn logbook.
sentences.cn: 旧驿站的墙壁里塞着一本磨损的日志。

sentences.en: Its *previous* entries were written in three different hands — travellers who had passed through long before us.
The last entry ended mid-sentence, but the final word written was exactly the word we were searching for.
sentences.cn: 最后一条记录在中途戛然而止，但最后写下的词正好就是我们在寻找的词。

sentences.en: We added our own line below.
sentences.cn: 我们在下面添了自己的记录。

aim:2.en: Silverfang set the small brass device on the railing of Crestholm Island and looked through its sight. 'The *aim* of this tool is to find true north by starlight,' she explained. She turned it once, twice, then stopped. A faint click sounded, and a hidden drawer slid open in the railing, holding our next word inside.
aim:2.cnHint: 银牙在Crestholm岛用黄铜仪器以星光校准方向，仪器的____是寻找正北，随后暗格弹开露出了下一个词。
aim:2.hook: Inside the drawer was the word — and a second, smaller device we did not recognise.
aim:2.line: 'The *aim* of this tool is to find true north by starlight,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang set the small brass device on the railing of Crestholm Island and looked through its sight.
sentences.cn: 银牙把那个小黄铜装置放在克雷斯托姆岛的栏杆上，透过它的瞄准器向外看。

sentences.en: 'The *aim* of this tool is to find true north by starlight,' she explained.
She turned it once, twice, then stopped.
sentences.cn: 她转了一下，又转了一下，然后停了下来。

sentences.en: A faint click sounded, and a hidden drawer slid open in the railing, holding our next word inside.
sentences.cn: 一声微弱的咔哒声响起，栏杆上的一个隐藏抽屉滑了出来，里面装着我们的下一个词。

mistake:2.en: Deep inside the Amber Vault, I found an old map carved into the wall. One island was drawn twice — in two different places. Old Helm studied it and shook his head slowly. 'Someone made a *mistake*,' he said, 'or they were hiding a second path on purpose.'
mistake:2.cnHint: 琥珀密室的石壁地图上，老舵发现了一处奇怪的____。
mistake:2.hook: Both paths led somewhere — but only one led back.
mistake:2.line: 'Every *mistake* on an old map is really a secret wearing a disguise.'

sentences.en: Deep inside the Amber Vault, I found an old map carved into the wall.
sentences.cn: 深入琥珀穴库，我在墙上找到了一张刻在石头上的古地图。

sentences.en: One island was drawn twice — in two different places.
sentences.cn: 一座岛屿被画了两次——在两个不同的地方。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied it and shook his head slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究着它，慢慢摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'Someone made a *mistake*,' he said, 'or they were hiding a second path on purpose.'

staff:2.en: The Observatory of Hollow Peak kept its lights on through the night. We knocked, and the whole *staff* — all four of them — opened the door together, as if they had been expecting us. One held a lantern. Another held a list of names. Mine was at the bottom.
staff:2.cnHint: 空峰天文台的全体____整整齐齐地在深夜迎接了我们。
staff:2.hook: My name was there — written before I ever arrived.
staff:2.line: 'The entire *staff* agreed: we have been watching your troupe for weeks.'

sentences.en: The Observatory of Hollow Peak kept its lights on through the night.
sentences.cn: 空心峰的观象台整夜都亮着灯。

sentences.en: We knocked, and the whole *staff* — all four of them — opened the door together, as if they had been expecting us.
One held a lantern.
sentences.cn: 一个人拿着灯笼。

sentences.en: Another held a list of names.
sentences.cn: 另一个人拿着一份名单。

sentences.en: Mine was at the bottom.
sentences.cn: 我的名字在最下面。

enhance:2.en: Bell spread the new star chart across the deck and pointed to a cluster of dim lights near the edge. 'If we pass through that silver fog,' she said, 'it will *enhance* our compass signal — the islands beyond will finally show their true names.' Old Helm smiled wide.
enhance:2.cnHint: 小铃说穿过银雾能____指南针的信号，让更多岛屿现出真名。
enhance:2.hook: Beyond the fog, something enormous was already turning toward us.
enhance:2.line: 'A little silver mist can *enhance* even the oldest compass, trust me.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the new star chart across the deck and pointed to a cluster of dim lights near the edge.
sentences.cn: 小铃把新的星图铺开在甲板上，指向边缘附近一簇昏暗的光点。

sentences.en: 'If we pass through that silver fog,' she said, 'it will *enhance* our compass signal — the islands beyond will finally show their true names.'
Old Helm smiled wide.
sentences.cn: 老舵咧嘴笑了。

project:2.en: Inside the ruined lighthouse, we found a notebook filled with careful drawings. It was someone's life *project* — a complete map of every floating island above the Cloud Line. Hundreds of pages. Bell turned to the last entry and went very quiet. The final island had no name, only a question mark.
project:2.cnHint: 废弃灯塔里，有人用一生完成了一个____：绘制云线以上所有浮岛。
project:2.hook: The question mark was drawn in a different colour — and still wet.
project:2.line: 'This *project* took one person thirty years — and they still never finished it.'

sentences.en: Inside the ruined lighthouse, we found a notebook filled with careful drawings.
sentences.cn: 在那座破败的灯塔里，我们找到了一本笔记本，里面全是精心绘制的图画。

sentences.en: It was someone's life *project* — a complete map of every floating island above the Cloud Line.
Hundreds of pages.
sentences.cn: 足足有几百页。

sentences.en: Bell turned to the last entry and went very quiet.
sentences.cn: 小铃翻到最后一页，突然没了声音。

sentences.en: The final island had no name, only a question mark.
sentences.cn: 最后那座岛没有名字，只有一个问号。

record:2.en: The Drift Archive smelled of old paper and cool air. A keeper in a blue coat handed me a small disc of pale stone. 'This is your troupe's *record*,' she said. Every island we had ever touched was marked on it as a tiny glowing dot. We had visited far more than I thought.
record:2.cnHint: 漂流档案馆的管理员递给我们一份旅团旅行的____，上面的光点比我想象的多得多。
record:2.hook: One dot was blinking — a place none of us remembered visiting.
record:2.line: 'Your *record* shows courage — and one very interesting detour you may have forgotten.'

sentences.en: The Drift Archive smelled of old paper and cool air.
sentences.cn: 漂流档案馆闻起来是旧纸张和冷空气的味道。

sentences.en: A keeper in a blue coat handed me a small disc of pale stone.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着蓝色大衣的守卷人递给我一块淡色的石盘。

sentences.en: 'This is your troupe's *record*,' she said.
Every island we had ever touched was marked on it as a tiny glowing dot.
sentences.cn: 我们曾经踏足过的每一座岛都在上面标成了一个微小的发光点。

sentences.en: We had visited far more than I thought.
sentences.cn: 我们去过的地方远比我想象的多得多。

regular:2.en: Silverfang docked beside us at Saltmere Platform and leaned over the rail. 'We do a *regular* sweep of the eastern channels every three nights,' she said, almost kindly. 'Last sweep, something large moved under the clouds. No shape, no sound. Just a shadow going the wrong way.'
regular:2.cnHint: 银牙告诉我们，他们____扫描东部航道时发现了一个奇怪的影子。
regular:2.hook: The shadow, she said, had been following a map — our map.
regular:2.line: 'A *regular* patrol sounds dull until you find something that should not be there.'

sentences.en: Silverfang docked beside us at Saltmere Platform and leaned over the rail.
sentences.cn: 银牙在盐湖平台旁靠了岸，身子探过栏杆。

sentences.en: 'We do a *regular* sweep of the eastern channels every three nights,' she said, almost kindly.
'Last sweep, something large moved under the clouds.
sentences.cn: 上次巡查时，有什么庞然大物在云层下面移动。

sentences.en: No shape, no sound.
sentences.cn: 没有形状，没有声音。

sentences.en: Just a shadow going the wrong way.'
sentences.cn: 只是一道影子朝着诡异的方向游去。

security:2.en: The Gate of Pale Winds had two guards and a long list of rules. Bell read every line without blinking. 'The *security* here is tight because something valuable was once carried out and never returned,' the older guard explained. He looked at Old Helm's coat pocket when he said it.
security:2.cnHint: 苍风之门戒备森严，老卫兵暗示这里的____是因为曾有珍贵之物被带走。
security:2.hook: Old Helm's hand moved — just slightly — to his coat pocket.
security:2.line: 'Strong *security* always means something worth finding is just on the other side.'

sentences.en: The Gate of Pale Winds had two guards and a long list of rules.
sentences.cn: 苍风门有两个卫兵和一长串的规则。

sentences.en: Bell read every line without blinking.
sentences.cn: 小铃一行一行地读，眼睛都没眨一下。

sentences.en: 'The *security* here is tight because something valuable was once carried out and never returned,' the older guard explained.
He looked at Old Helm's coat pocket when he said it.
sentences.cn: 他说这话时瞥了一眼老舵外套的口袋。

return:2.en: Inside a hollow star-stone on the island of Emberglow, I found a folded note. Old Helm read it aloud, his voice soft: someone had made the long *return* to this island decades ago, leaving this very message for the next traveller who arrived. We were not the first.
return:2.cnHint: 在星落之夜，我们在一块空心星石中发现了一张纸条，纸条讲述着某人曾经的____。
return:2.hook: The handwriting on the note matched Old Helm's own.
return:2.line: 'A *return* to this island means the stars chose you,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Inside a hollow star-stone on the island of Emberglow, I found a folded note.
sentences.cn: 在余烬辉岛的一块中空星石里，我找到了一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it aloud, his voice soft: someone had made the long *return* to this island decades ago, leaving this very message for the next traveller who arrived.
We were not the first.
sentences.cn: 我们不是第一批到这里的人。

remove:2.en: Bell discovered a locked hatch beneath a carpet of silver moss on Driftledge Island. She pressed her palm flat against the moss and began to *remove* it layer by layer, careful not to tear the delicate roots. Underneath, carved letters spelled a single word we did not yet know.
remove:2.cnHint: 小铃在银苔之下____覆盖物，露出了一扇隐藏的舱门和一行神秘的字。
remove:2.hook: The carved word was glowing faintly, as if freshly cut.
remove:2.line: '*Remove* the moss gently,' Bell said, 'or the letters vanish.'

sentences.en: Bell discovered a locked hatch beneath a carpet of silver moss on Driftledge Island.
sentences.cn: 小铃在漂流峡岛上的银苔毯下发现了一道上锁的舱口。

sentences.en: She pressed her palm flat against the moss and began to *remove* it layer by layer, careful not to tear the delicate roots.
Underneath, carved letters spelled a single word we did not yet know.
sentences.cn: 下面刻着一个我们还不认识的词。

colleague:2.en: A small wooden boat drifted up to our platform, carrying a sealed jar and a note signed by Silverfang. Old Helm looked surprised. 'She is not our enemy tonight,' he said quietly. 'She is acting as a *colleague*.' We opened the jar to find a glowing map fragment inside.
colleague:2.cnHint: 银牙送来了一只装有地图碎片的罐子，老舵手说她今晚是我们的____。
colleague:2.hook: The fragment pointed to an island none of us had ever named.
colleague:2.line: 'Even a rival can act as a *colleague* when the stars fall,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: A small wooden boat drifted up to our platform, carrying a sealed jar and a note signed by Silverfang.
sentences.cn: 一只小木船漂到了我们的平台边，船上载着一个密封的罐子和银牙签名的纸条。

sentences.en: Old Helm looked surprised.
sentences.cn: 老舵看起来很惊讶。

sentences.en: 'She is not our enemy tonight,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: 他轻声说，今晚她不是我们的敌人。

sentences.en: 'She is acting as a *colleague*.'
We opened the jar to find a glowing map fragment inside.
sentences.cn: 我们打开罐子，里面装着一块发光的地图碎片。

normal:2.en: The sky above Cinderperch Island looked *normal* at first — deep blue, scattered stars, a quiet wind. Then Old Helm pointed to a gap where three stars had been only an hour before. Bell opened her compass and found the needle spinning without pause. Nothing was normal anymore.
normal:2.cnHint: Cinderperch岛上的星空起初看起来____，但三颗星消失后，一切都变了。
normal:2.hook: Bell's compass needle stopped — pointing straight down.
normal:2.line: 'It looked *normal*,' Bell said, 'but normal skies don't swallow stars.'

sentences.en: The sky above Cinderperch Island looked *normal* at first — deep blue, scattered stars, a quiet wind.
Then Old Helm pointed to a gap where three stars had been only an hour before.
sentences.cn: 老舵指向一个地方，三颗星在一小时前还在那儿。

sentences.en: Bell opened her compass and found the needle spinning without pause.
sentences.cn: 小铃打开指南针，发现指针不停地旋转。

sentences.en: Nothing was normal anymore.
sentences.cn: 什么都不正常了。

succeed:2.en: We had tried twice to lift the heavy star-anchor blocking the gate of Ashwing Crossing. On the third attempt, Bell and I leaned together, and Old Helm pulled from above. We felt it shift, then rise. 'We *succeed* only when we all move at once,' Old Helm said, breathing hard.
succeed:2.cnHint: 我们第三次合力才终于____，抬起了挡住通道的星锚。
succeed:2.hook: Behind the gate, a staircase led upward into open sky.
succeed:2.line: 'We *succeed* together, or not at all,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: We had tried twice to lift the heavy star-anchor blocking the gate of Ashwing Crossing.
sentences.cn: 我们已经试过两次去搬开堵住灰翼交界口的那个沉重星锚。

sentences.en: On the third attempt, Bell and I leaned together, and Old Helm pulled from above.
sentences.cn: 第三次，小铃和我一起用力，老舵从上面拉。

sentences.en: We felt it shift, then rise.
sentences.cn: 我们感觉到它动了，然后抬起来了。

sentences.en: 'We *succeed* only when we all move at once,' Old Helm said, breathing hard.

image:2.en: At the centre of Mirrorhollow Island stood a still pool. I leaned over and saw not my own face but an *image* of a place I had never visited — tall silver towers on a distant cloud. Old Helm said the pool showed each person the next island they were meant to reach.
image:2.cnHint: Mirrorhollow岛的水池中出现了一个____，显示的不是我的脸，而是一处陌生的地方。
image:2.hook: Silverfang's reflection appeared in the pool beside mine.
image:2.line: 'Trust the *image*,' said Old Helm. 'The pool has never lied.'

sentences.en: At the centre of Mirrorhollow Island stood a still pool.
sentences.cn: 在镜空岛的中央有一个静止的池塘。

sentences.en: I leaned over and saw not my own face but an *image* of a place I had never visited — tall silver towers on a distant cloud.
Old Helm said the pool showed each person the next island they were meant to reach.
sentences.cn: 老舵说这口池子会向每个人显示他们下一个应该去的岛屿。

ourselves:2.en: After a long crossing through cold cloud, we landed on a quiet ledge and sat in a circle. We had no map, no signal, and no guide. 'We have only *ourselves*,' Bell said, and somehow that felt like enough. Old Helm spread the fragments we carried, and together we drew our next route.
ourselves:2.cnHint: 迷失在云中后，我们只能依靠____，围坐在一起，凭着手中的碎片重新规划路线。
ourselves:2.hook: The route we drew led toward a sound like distant bells.
ourselves:2.line: 'We have only *ourselves* tonight,' said Bell, 'so let us be enough.'

sentences.en: After a long crossing through cold cloud, we landed on a quiet ledge and sat in a circle.
sentences.cn: 穿过漫长而寒冷的云层后，我们在一个安静的崖边着陆，围成一圈坐了下来。

sentences.en: We had no map, no signal, and no guide.
sentences.cn: 我们没有地图，没有信号，也没有导游。

sentences.en: 'We have only *ourselves*,' Bell said, and somehow that felt like enough.
Old Helm spread the fragments we carried, and together we drew our next route.
sentences.cn: 老舵摊开我们携带的碎片，我们一起规划了下一条路线。

catch:2.en: A glowing shard fell from the sky above Dustwhirl Platform, spinning fast. Bell sprinted across the boards while Old Helm shouted directions. She jumped, arm stretched wide, and managed to *catch* the shard just before it struck the edge and shattered. Inside it was a single written word, still warm.
catch:2.cnHint: 一块发光的碎片从天空坠落，小铃奔跑跳跃，终于____住了它。
catch:2.hook: The word inside was our own troupe's name.
catch:2.line: '*Catch* it before the word burns out!' Bell cried, already running.

sentences.en: A glowing shard fell from the sky above Dustwhirl Platform, spinning fast.
sentences.cn: 一块发光的碎片从尘旋平台上空坠落，急速旋转。

sentences.en: Bell sprinted across the boards while Old Helm shouted directions.
sentences.cn: 小铃在木板上冲刺，老舵在后面大喊指挥。

sentences.en: She jumped, arm stretched wide, and managed to *catch* the shard just before it struck the edge and shattered.
Inside it was a single written word, still warm.
sentences.cn: 碎片里面写着一个字，还温热着。

review:2.en: Deep inside the map-vault island, Bell spread the glowing fragments across a stone table. 'Before we move on, let us do a quick *review* of every word we have collected,' she said. Each piece lit up in turn, forming a trail of islands stretching toward the horizon.
review:2.cnHint: 小铃在地图库岛上把所有碎片铺开，带大家对收集的词语做一次____。
review:2.hook: One fragment pulsed strangely, as if hiding a secret.
review:2.line: 'A good *review* now saves us trouble later,' Bell said softly.

sentences.en: Deep inside the map-vault island, Bell spread the glowing fragments across a stone table.
sentences.cn: 在地图库岛的深处，小铃把发光的碎片铺展在石桌上。

sentences.en: 'Before we move on, let us do a quick *review* of every word we have collected,' she said.
Each piece lit up in turn, forming a trail of islands stretching toward the horizon.
sentences.cn: 每块碎片依次亮起，形成一条岛屿之路，延伸向地平线。

ahead:2.en: Old Helm climbed to the prow of the sky-boat and squinted at the darkness. A faint glow shimmered far in the distance. '*Ahead* of us,' he called back, voice full of quiet wonder, 'floats an island no chart has ever named.' The whole troupe leaned forward, breath held.
ahead:2.cnHint: 老舵在船头望向远方，宣布____方向有一座从未被记录的岛屿。
ahead:2.hook: The glow blinked once, then doubled in size.
ahead:2.line: 'Something *ahead* is calling to us,' Old Helm murmured.

sentences.en: Old Helm climbed to the prow of the sky-boat and squinted at the darkness.
sentences.cn: 老舵爬到天船的船首，眯眼盯着黑暗。

sentences.en: A faint glow shimmered far in the distance. '*Ahead* of us,' he called back, voice full of quiet wonder, 'floats an island no chart has ever named.'
The whole troupe leaned forward, breath held.
sentences.cn: 整支队伍都探身向前，屏住了呼吸。

cheap:2.en: At the trading post on Copper-Cloud Island, a merchant offered Bell a bundle of blank map-sheets for almost nothing. Bell narrowed her eyes. 'These feel too *cheap*,' she said, turning the sheets over. Hidden on the back of each one was a faded word waiting to be found.
cheap:2.cnHint: 商人以极低的价格出售一批空白地图纸，小铃觉得东西太____而心生疑惑。
cheap:2.hook: The last sheet held a word none of them could read.
cheap:2.line: 'Anything this *cheap* must carry a surprise,' Bell warned.

sentences.en: At the trading post on Copper-Cloud Island, a merchant offered Bell a bundle of blank map-sheets for almost nothing.
sentences.cn: 在铜云岛的交易站，一个商人以几乎白送的价格给小铃一捆空白地图纸。

sentences.en: Bell narrowed her eyes.
sentences.cn: 小铃眯起眼睛。

sentences.en: 'These feel too *cheap*,' she said, turning the sheets over.
Hidden on the back of each one was a faded word waiting to be found.
sentences.cn: 每张纸的背面都藏着一个褪色的字，等待被发现。

critical:2.en: The sky-boat's steering crystal had cracked. Bell knelt beside it, face serious. 'This part is *critical*,' she told me, pressing both hands around the crack. 'Without it we drift wherever the wind wishes.' Old Helm handed her a word-fragment, and its warm light sealed the crystal whole again.
critical:2.cnHint: 操控晶石出现裂缝，小铃告诉大家这个部件____，必须立刻修好。
critical:2.hook: The repaired crystal began to spin in a direction it never had before.
critical:2.line: 'Staying calm at a *critical* moment is its own kind of skill,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The sky-boat's steering crystal had cracked.
sentences.cn: 天船的操舵晶体裂了。

sentences.en: Bell knelt beside it, face serious.
sentences.cn: 小铃跪在它旁边，脸色凝重。

sentences.en: 'This part is *critical*,' she told me, pressing both hands around the crack.
'Without it we drift wherever the wind wishes.'
sentences.cn: 没有它，我们就随风飘浮。

sentences.en: Old Helm handed her a word-fragment, and its warm light sealed the crystal whole again.
sentences.cn: 老舵递给她一片带字的碎片，温暖的光芒把晶体重新封合在一起。

motivate:2.en: I had begun to feel tired, my notebook nearly empty of new words. Old Helm sat beside me and told a story of his first island, found by accident in a rainstorm. 'Let that *motivate* you,' he said gently. By the time he finished, my pen was already moving again.
motivate:2.cnHint: 我感到疲惫，老舵讲述自己的故事，希望以此____我重新振作。
motivate:2.hook: Outside, a new island drifted into view like an answer.
motivate:2.line: 'Let the road itself *motivate* you when words run dry,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: I had begun to feel tired, my notebook nearly empty of new words.
sentences.cn: 我开始感到疲倦，笔记本里新字越来越少。

sentences.en: Old Helm sat beside me and told a story of his first island, found by accident in a rainstorm.
sentences.cn: 老舵坐在我身边，讲了一个故事——他第一个岛屿，是在暴雨中意外发现的。

sentences.en: 'Let that *motivate* you,' he said gently.
By the time he finished, my pen was already moving again.
sentences.cn: 等他讲完时，我的笔已经又动起来了。

charge:2.en: At the Sky-Lantern Dock, the harbour keeper announced he would *charge* one riddle for every vessel that wanted to moor. Old Helm smiled, reached into his coat, and produced a word so rare the keeper gasped and waved us in without another question.
charge:2.cnHint: 港口管理员宣布要向每艘船____一道谜题才能停靠，老舵用一个罕见的词轻松应对。
charge:2.hook: The harbour keeper watched us go, eyes wide with envy.
charge:2.line: 'He can *charge* whatever he likes; we pay in words,' Old Helm laughed.

sentences.en: At the Sky-Lantern Dock, the harbour keeper announced he would *charge* one riddle for every vessel that wanted to moor.
Old Helm smiled, reached into his coat, and produced a word so rare the keeper gasped and waved us in without another question.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑着，从外套里掏出一个字，稀罕得让港务长倒吸一口气，直接放我们进去了。

complex:2.en: The new word we found that night was 'labyrinth'. Bell traced its letters slowly. 'The meaning is *complex*,' she admitted, 'but look — the map-fragment it unlocks shows a whole spiral island.' She set it in place and the chart bloomed outward, revealing passages within passages, glowing softly.
complex:2.cnHint: 小铃研究新词时说它的含义____，但它解锁的岛屿地图却令人叹为观止。
complex:2.hook: At the spiral island's centre, something was already moving.
complex:2.line: 'Do not fear what is *complex*; that is where the good things hide,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The new word we found that night was 'labyrinth'.
sentences.cn: 那晚我们找到的新字是"迷宫"。

sentences.en: Bell traced its letters slowly.
sentences.cn: 小铃慢慢地描着它的笔画。

sentences.en: 'The meaning is *complex*,' she admitted, 'but look — the map-fragment it unlocks shows a whole spiral island.'
She set it in place and the chart bloomed outward, revealing passages within passages, glowing softly.
sentences.cn: 她把它放进去，地图向外绽开，露出了一圈圈通道，闪烁着温和的光。

itself:2.en: We found the word 'radiant' carved on a pillar of ice high above the cloud-line. As I copied it into my notebook, the pillar began to glow. Old Helm watched, calm and certain. 'The word knows *itself* once someone reads it aloud,' he said. So I read it aloud.
itself:2.cnHint: 我抄下冰柱上的新词，老舵说这个词一旦被朗读就会认识____。
itself:2.hook: The light shot upward and painted a new map on the sky.
itself:2.line: 'Every word carries *itself* like a lantern in the dark,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: We found the word 'radiant' carved on a pillar of ice high above the cloud-line.
sentences.cn: 我们在云线上方的冰柱上找到了"灿烂"这个字。

sentences.en: As I copied it into my notebook, the pillar began to glow.
sentences.cn: 我把它抄进笔记本时，冰柱开始发光。

sentences.en: Old Helm watched, calm and certain.
sentences.cn: 老舵看着，神情平静而笃定。

sentences.en: 'The word knows *itself* once someone reads it aloud,' he said.
So I read it aloud.
sentences.cn: 所以我大声读了出来。

join:2.en: Deep in the Crystal Cavern, I found two broken rope bridges hanging over a dark drop. Bell knelt down, studied the frayed ends, and began to weave them together. 'We can *join* these,' she said softly. The moment the last knot held, a hidden door in the cave wall slid open with a gentle hum.
join:2.cnHint: 小铃把两段断桥____在一起，隐藏的门缓缓开启。
join:2.hook: Beyond the door, something glowed with an unknown colour.
join:2.line: 'We can *join* these two bridges and reach the other side.'

sentences.en: Deep in the Crystal Cavern, I found two broken rope bridges hanging over a dark drop.
sentences.cn: 在水晶洞穴深处，我发现两座断裂的绳桥悬挂在黑暗的深渊上。

sentences.en: Bell knelt down, studied the frayed ends, and began to weave them together.
sentences.cn: 小铃跪下来，研究了松散的绳头，开始把它们编织在一起。

sentences.en: 'We can *join* these,' she said softly.
The moment the last knot held, a hidden door in the cave wall slid open with a gentle hum.
sentences.cn: 最后一个结扣紧的瞬间，洞穴墙上的一扇隐门无声地滑开了。

significant:2.en: Old Helm spread the star-map across a flat stone and pointed to a faint circle near the edge. 'Most people ignore this mark,' he said, 'but it is *significant*.' He tapped it twice. The circle began to shine, and a thin beam of light shot upward, drawing a path across the night sky.
significant:2.cnHint: 老赫姆在星图上发现一个____的标记，它射出一道光柱。
significant:2.hook: The beam of light pointed straight at the largest floating island.
significant:2.line: 'That small mark is *significant* — it shows the island no one has found.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the star-map across a flat stone and pointed to a faint circle near the edge.
sentences.cn: 老舵把星图铺在平石上，指向边缘附近一个淡淡的圆圈。

sentences.en: 'Most people ignore this mark,' he said, 'but it is *significant*.'
He tapped it twice.
sentences.cn: 他敲了两下。

sentences.en: The circle began to shine, and a thin beam of light shot upward, drawing a path across the night sky.
sentences.cn: 圆圈开始闪耀，一束细光射向天空，在夜色中画出了一条路。

step:2.en: The stone path leading to the Observatory Tower was narrow and uneven. I moved slowly, testing each stone before trusting my weight. Bell called from behind, 'One *step* at a time!' On the final stone, my foot pressed a hidden switch, and the great iron door swung open on its own with a long, low groan.
step:2.cnHint: 我一____一步走上石径，最后一步触发了隐藏的开关。
step:2.hook: Inside, a single lantern burned as if it had been waiting for us.
step:2.line: 'One careful *step* at a time — this path is full of surprises.'

sentences.en: The stone path leading to the Observatory Tower was narrow and uneven.
sentences.cn: 通往观星塔的石板路很窄，也不平整。

sentences.en: I moved slowly, testing each stone before trusting my weight.
sentences.cn: 我走得很慢，每块石头都要试试能不能踩。

sentences.en: Bell called from behind, 'One *step* at a time!'
On the final stone, my foot pressed a hidden switch, and the great iron door swung open on its own with a long, low groan.
sentences.cn: 在最后一块石头上，我的脚踩到了一个隐藏的开关，巨大的铁门自己打开了，发出长长的低沉呻吟。

unique:2.en: Among the hundreds of jars lining the Archive Island shelves, one stood apart. Its surface carried a pattern unlike any other — a swirl of silver and gold that seemed to move when you looked away. Old Helm lifted it carefully. 'This is *unique*,' he whispered. 'There is no other jar like it in any record I have read.'
unique:2.cnHint: 老赫姆在档案岛找到一个____的罐子，上面的图案会动。
unique:2.hook: When he opened the lid, music, not air, came out.
unique:2.line: 'This jar is *unique* — I have never seen its pattern in any book.'

sentences.en: Among the hundreds of jars lining the Archive Island shelves, one stood apart.
sentences.cn: 档案岛的架子上摆着数百个罐子，其中一个显得格外不同。

sentences.en: Its surface carried a pattern unlike any other — a swirl of silver and gold that seemed to move when you looked away.
sentences.cn: 它的表面刻着独特的图案——银金相间的漩涡，当你转开视线时似乎还在流动。

sentences.en: Old Helm lifted it carefully.
sentences.cn: 老舵小心地拿起了它。

sentences.en: 'This is *unique*,' he whispered.
'There is no other jar like it in any record I have read.'
sentences.cn: 我翻遍了所有记录，没有任何一个罐子与它相像。

inside:2.en: Silverfang handed me a small copper box sealed with wax. 'Open it only when you reach the Sky Meadow,' he said, with an odd smile. I waited, as promised. Standing among the tall silver grass, I finally broke the seal. *Inside* the box lay a single folded note and a tiny glowing seed resting on blue cloth.
inside:2.cnHint: 银牙给了我一个铜盒，打开后____装着纸条和发光的种子。
inside:2.hook: The note was written in a language I almost recognised.
inside:2.line: 'Look *inside* the box — you will find something worth the wait.'

sentences.en: Silverfang handed me a small copper box sealed with wax.
sentences.cn: 银牙递给我一个用蜡封住的小铜盒。

sentences.en: 'Open it only when you reach the Sky Meadow,' he said, with an odd smile.
sentences.cn: 他带着奇异的微笑说，等到了天空草甸再打开。

sentences.en: I waited, as promised.
sentences.cn: 我遵守了诺言，一直等着。

sentences.en: Standing among the tall silver grass, I finally broke the seal.
sentences.cn: 站在齐腰高的银色草丛中，我终于打破了封蜡。

sentences.en: *Inside* the box lay a single folded note and a tiny glowing seed resting on blue cloth.

majority:2.en: When the troupe gathered to choose a new route, everyone spoke at once. Old Helm raised a hand for quiet. 'The *majority* of us favour the cloud road,' he said, counting the raised hands again to be sure. Silverfang shrugged and folded his map. A moment later, the cloud road lit up as though it had heard its name.
majority:2.cnHint: 团员们投票决定路线，____人选择云之路，云路随即发光。
majority:2.hook: The road moved, pulling itself closer to our island.
majority:2.line: 'The *majority* has chosen — we take the cloud road at first light.'

sentences.en: When the troupe gathered to choose a new route, everyone spoke at once.
sentences.cn: 车队聚在一起选择新路线时，大家都在七嘴八舌地说话。

sentences.en: Old Helm raised a hand for quiet.
sentences.cn: 老舵抬起一只手示意安静。

sentences.en: 'The *majority* of us favour the cloud road,' he said, counting the raised hands again to be sure.
Silverfang shrugged and folded his map.
sentences.cn: 银牙耸了耸肩，把地图折了起来。

sentences.en: A moment later, the cloud road lit up as though it had heard its name.
sentences.cn: 片刻之后，云道亮了起来，仿佛听到了自己的名字。

notice:2.en: I almost walked past the mossy wall entirely. Then something made me stop — a tiny carved arrow, no bigger than my thumbnail, pointing left. Had it always been there? Bell came up beside me. 'Did you *notice* that?' she asked, eyes wide. We followed the arrow and found a hidden garden full of floating stones and quiet light.
notice:2.cnHint: 小铃让我____到苔藓墙上的小箭头，它指引我们找到了秘密花园。
notice:2.hook: In the centre of the garden stood a door with no wall around it.
notice:2.line: 'Did you *notice* the small arrow on the wall? It is pointing left.'

sentences.en: I almost walked past the mossy wall entirely.
sentences.cn: 我几乎要走过那堵长满苔藓的墙了。

sentences.en: Then something made me stop — a tiny carved arrow, no bigger than my thumbnail, pointing left.
sentences.cn: 然后有什么让我停住了脚——一个只有我指甲盖大小的雕刻箭头，指向左边。

sentences.en: Had it always been there?
sentences.cn: 它一直都在这儿吗？

sentences.en: Bell came up beside me.
sentences.cn: 小铃走到了我身边。

sentences.en: 'Did you *notice* that?' she asked, eyes wide.
We followed the arrow and found a hidden garden full of floating stones and quiet light.
sentences.cn: 我们跟着箭头走，发现了一个隐秘的花园，里面漂浮着石块和柔和的光。

taste:2.en: At the edge of Amber Falls, a local keeper offered us each a small cup of golden liquid. 'From the island's oldest tree,' she said proudly. I took a sip. The *taste* was warm and a little sweet, like sunlight trapped in honey. Bell laughed in surprise, and even Old Helm smiled — something he rarely did before noon.
taste:2.cnHint: 我们品尝了金色液体，它的____温暖甜蜜，连老赫姆都罕见地笑了。
taste:2.hook: The keeper then pointed us toward a tree none of us had noticed.
taste:2.line: 'The *taste* of this drink will stay with you longer than you think.'

sentences.en: At the edge of Amber Falls, a local keeper offered us each a small cup of golden liquid.
sentences.cn: 在琥珀瀑布的边缘，一位当地守卫者给我们每人递了一小杯金色液体。

sentences.en: 'From the island's oldest tree,' she said proudly.
sentences.cn: 她骄傲地说，这是岛上最老的树出产的。

sentences.en: I took a sip.
sentences.cn: 我尝了一口。

sentences.en: The *taste* was warm and a little sweet, like sunlight trapped in honey.
Bell laughed in surprise, and even Old Helm smiled — something he rarely did before noon.
sentences.cn: 小铃惊喜地笑出了声，连老舵也笑了——这在午前是极少见的。

whatever:2.en: Old Helm spread the star-map across the deck and tapped a blank patch near the edge. 'Fill it in,' he said. I asked which word I should use. He smiled and said, '*whatever* word calls to you is the right one.' I pressed my palm to the paper and whispered the first word that rose in my chest. A new island shimmered into view.
whatever:2.cnHint: 老舵告诉我，____我心中浮现的词语，都能让新岛屿出现在星图上。
whatever:2.hook: The island had no name yet — only a soft, waiting glow.
whatever:2.line: '*Whatever* word calls to you is the right one,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the star-map across the deck and tapped a blank patch near the edge.
sentences.cn: 老舵把星图铺在甲板上，点了点边缘一个空白的地方。

sentences.en: 'Fill it in,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说，填上它。

sentences.en: I asked which word I should use.
sentences.cn: 我问该用哪个字。

sentences.en: He smiled and said, '*whatever* word calls to you is the right one.'
I pressed my palm to the paper and whispered the first word that rose in my chest.
sentences.cn: 我把手掌按在纸上，低声说出了第一个浮现在心里的字。

sentences.en: A new island shimmered into view.
sentences.cn: 一个新的岛屿在视野中闪现出来。

predict:2.en: Bell stood at the prow, studying the clouds below our hull. 'I can *predict* where the wind will carry us next,' she said, tracing a slow arc with one finger. A faint outline appeared on the map — three small islands in a curve, just as she had drawn. Old Helm nodded, looking more impressed than he let on.
predict:2.cnHint: 小铃能够____风的走向，并在星图上提前勾勒出前方岛屿的轮廓。
predict:2.hook: Three islands waited ahead, already knowing we were coming.
predict:2.line: 'I can *predict* where the wind will carry us, if you trust me,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell stood at the prow, studying the clouds below our hull.
sentences.cn: 小铃站在船头，研究着船体下方的云层。

sentences.en: 'I can *predict* where the wind will carry us next,' she said, tracing a slow arc with one finger.
A faint outline appeared on the map — three small islands in a curve, just as she had drawn.
sentences.cn: 地图上出现了一道淡淡的轮廓——三个小岛排成一道弧线，正如她画的那样。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded, looking more impressed than he let on.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头，看起来比他表现出来的更印象深刻。

road:2.en: The island had no soil, only flat white stone stretching in every direction. Then Bell pointed down. A single carved line ran through the rock like a *road*, leading toward a tall arch at the far end. Old Helm said old travellers had cut that path long before us. We followed it, one step at a time, and the arch began to glow.
road:2.cnHint: 这座岛屿上有一条石刻的____，引导我们走向一座发光的拱门。
road:2.hook: Beyond the arch, the stars looked close enough to touch.
road:2.line: 'This *road* was carved by hands older than our troupe,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The island had no soil, only flat white stone stretching in every direction.
sentences.cn: 那个岛没有土壤，只有平坦的白石向四面八方延伸。

sentences.en: Then Bell pointed down.
sentences.cn: 然后小铃指向下方。

sentences.en: A single carved line ran through the rock like a *road*, leading toward a tall arch at the far end.
Old Helm said old travellers had cut that path long before us.
sentences.cn: 老舵说远古的旅人早在我们之前就凿出了这条路。

sentences.en: We followed it, one step at a time, and the arch began to glow.
sentences.cn: 我们一步步跟着走，那个拱门开始发出光来。

solution:2.en: The lock on the archive door was shaped like a word — literally. Each letter could spin. Silverfang had tried a dozen combinations and was ready to give up. Bell studied it quietly, then turned three letters with a soft click. 'Simple,' she said. I asked how. 'The *solution* was written on the door itself, if you read it slowly.' The door swung open.
solution:2.cnHint: 小铃仔细观察后，找到了解开档案室门锁的____，答案就藏在门上的文字里。
solution:2.hook: Inside, a hundred glowing words floated in the dark, waiting to be claimed.
solution:2.line: 'The *solution* was written on the door itself,' said Bell quietly.

sentences.en: The lock on the archive door was shaped like a word — literally.
sentences.cn: 档案门上的锁是一个词的形状——真的是一个词。

sentences.en: Each letter could spin.
sentences.cn: 每个字母都能转动。

sentences.en: Silverfang had tried a dozen combinations and was ready to give up.
sentences.cn: 银牙试了十几个组合，已经打算放弃了。

sentences.en: Bell studied it quietly, then turned three letters with a soft click.
sentences.cn: 小铃静静地研究了一下，然后轻轻地转动了三个字母。

sentences.en: 'Simple,' she said.
sentences.cn: 她说，很简单。

sentences.en: I asked how.
sentences.cn: 我问怎么做到的。

sentences.en: 'The *solution* was written on the door itself, if you read it slowly.'
The door swung open.
sentences.cn: 门被推开了。

total:2.en: We counted the words we had collected since leaving the first island. Old Helm marked each one with a small dot of light on the map. 'The *total* is forty-seven,' I said, feeling proud. Silverfang crossed his arms and said his crew had gathered sixty before the third moon. Old Helm just laughed and said the map only cared about the next one.
total:2.cnHint: 我们统计了迄今为止收集的词语____数量，银牙却不以为然地提起了他的记录。
total:2.hook: Somewhere ahead, word forty-eight was already waiting for us.
total:2.line: 'The *total* is forty-seven — not bad for a new crew,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: We counted the words we had collected since leaving the first island.
sentences.cn: 我们数了数自从离开第一个岛以来收集到的词汇。

sentences.en: Old Helm marked each one with a small dot of light on the map.
sentences.cn: 老舵在地图上用一个小光点标记每一个。

sentences.en: 'The *total* is forty-seven,' I said, feeling proud.
Silverfang crossed his arms and said his crew had gathered sixty before the third moon.
sentences.cn: 银牙交叉双臂说他的船队在第三个月圆之前就收集了六十个。

sentences.en: Old Helm just laughed and said the map only cared about the next one.
sentences.cn: 老舵只是笑了，说地图只在乎下一个。

fail:2.en: The bridge between two islands was made of frozen sound — you crossed it by humming the right note. I tried twice and felt the bridge tremble under my feet. 'Don't *fail* now,' Silverfang called from behind, not unkindly. I took a breath, hummed lower, and the bridge held firm all the way across. My heartbeat was still loud when I reached the other side.
fail:2.cnHint: 我在哼唱正确音调时差点____，险些让冰桥在脚下颤动坍塌。
fail:2.hook: On the far side, a word glowed in midair, gold and steady.
fail:2.line: 'Don't *fail* now — you're closer than you think,' called Silverfang.

sentences.en: The bridge between two islands was made of frozen sound — you crossed it by humming the right note.
sentences.cn: 两个岛之间的桥是由冻结的声音组成的——你得哼出正确的音符才能过去。

sentences.en: I tried twice and felt the bridge tremble under my feet.
sentences.cn: 我试了两次，感觉桥在我脚下颤抖。

sentences.en: 'Don't *fail* now,' Silverfang called from behind, not unkindly.
I took a breath, hummed lower, and the bridge held firm all the way across.
sentences.cn: 我深吸了一口气，哼得更低一些，桥坚定地支撑我走过了整个桥面。

sentences.en: My heartbeat was still loud when I reached the other side.
sentences.cn: 我到达另一边时，心跳声仍然很响。

function:2.en: The old tower in the centre of the island had four doors but no windows. Bell walked around it twice. 'Each door has a different *function*,' she said. 'One opens the sky map, one calls the wind, one stores the words we have found, and one — ' She stopped. The fourth door had no handle. Old Helm placed his ear against it and smiled a quiet smile.
function:2.cnHint: 小铃发现古塔的四扇门各有不同的____，但第四扇门没有把手，令人好奇。
function:2.hook: Whatever the fourth door did, Old Helm already knew.
function:2.line: 'Each door has a different *function* — choose carefully,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The old tower in the centre of the island had four doors but no windows.
sentences.cn: 岛中心的老塔有四扇门，却没有窗户。

sentences.en: Bell walked around it twice.
sentences.cn: 小铃绕了它两圈。

sentences.en: 'Each door has a different *function*,' she said.
'One opens the sky map, one calls the wind, one stores the words we have found, and one — ' She stopped.
sentences.cn: 她说，打开天空地图的是一扇，召唤风的是一扇，储存我们找到的词汇的是一扇，还有一扇——她停住了。

sentences.en: The fourth door had no handle.
sentences.cn: 第四扇门没有把手。

sentences.en: Old Helm placed his ear against it and smiled a quiet smile.
sentences.cn: 老舵把耳朵贴在上面，露出了一个轻微的微笑。

method:2.en: Silverfang joined our camp that evening, claiming he had a better *method* for reading the star-map. He laid it flat, turned it forty-five degrees, and suddenly two hidden islands appeared in the fold lines. Old Helm said nothing for a moment. Then he quietly turned the map back and pointed to a third island that only his angle revealed. Both men grinned at the same time.
method:2.cnHint: 银牙展示了一种阅读星图的新____，却发现老舵的方式能找到更多隐藏岛屿。
method:2.hook: Three new islands meant three new words — the night felt suddenly full of promise.
method:2.line: 'My *method* is different from yours, but maybe both are right,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Silverfang joined our camp that evening, claiming he had a better *method* for reading the star-map.
He laid it flat, turned it forty-five degrees, and suddenly two hidden islands appeared in the fold lines.
sentences.cn: 他把地图铺平，转了四十五度，忽然两座隐没的岛屿在褶皱里现了形。

sentences.en: Old Helm said nothing for a moment.
sentences.cn: 老舵沉默了一会儿。

sentences.en: Then he quietly turned the map back and pointed to a third island that only his angle revealed.
sentences.cn: 然后他轻轻把地图转回来，指向只有他这个角度才能看见的第三座岛。

sentences.en: Both men grinned at the same time.
sentences.cn: 两个人同时咧开了嘴。

differ:2.en: Inside the hollow of the drifting island, Bell held two star-charts up to the light. 'These *differ* more than I expected,' she said softly. One showed a bridge of stone; the other, a bridge of cloud. Both claimed to lead to the same lost harbour, yet they could not both be right.
differ:2.cnHint: 小铃发现两张星图上的路线____，令她困惑不已。
differ:2.hook: Only one chart could be true — but which one?
differ:2.line: 'The two paths *differ*, and only the stars know which is real.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow of the drifting island, Bell held two star-charts up to the light.
sentences.cn: 在飘浮岛屿的空心里，小铃把两张星图举向光线。

sentences.en: 'These *differ* more than I expected,' she said softly.
One showed a bridge of stone; the other, a bridge of cloud.
sentences.cn: 一张画着石头桥；另一张，是云桥。

sentences.en: Both claimed to lead to the same lost harbour, yet they could not both be right.
sentences.cn: 两张都声称通往同一个失落的港口，可它们不可能都对。

shape:2.en: Old Helm pressed the fragment of bark against the stone wall, and the wet ink left a perfect print. The *shape* that appeared was not a letter or a number — it was an outline of an island none of us had ever visited, with three peaks pointing at the sky like fingers.
shape:2.cnHint: 老赫姆拓印树皮碎片，墙上出现了一个奇特的____。
shape:2.hook: Three peaks, one destination — and no way to know the danger ahead.
shape:2.line: 'Look at this *shape* — it matches nothing on any chart we carry.'

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed the fragment of bark against the stone wall, and the wet ink left a perfect print.
sentences.cn: 老舵把树皮碎片贴在石墙上，湿润的墨水留下了完美的印痕。

sentences.en: The *shape* that appeared was not a letter or a number — it was an outline of an island none of us had ever visited, with three peaks pointing at the sky like fingers.

twice:2.en: Bell rang the small bell she wore at her collar — the one she used to signal safe landing. She rang it *twice*, which was the code for something rare: a word fragment found intact, unbroken, still glowing at the edges. The whole troupe fell quiet and gathered close around her open palm.
twice:2.cnHint: 小铃摇铃____下，意味着她发现了一块完整的字词碎片。
twice:2.hook: The glow in her palm pulsed once — then began to fade fast.
twice:2.line: 'I rang it *twice* — that means what I found is real and whole.'

sentences.en: Bell rang the small bell she wore at her collar — the one she used to signal safe landing.
sentences.cn: 小铃摇了摇挂在衣领上的小铃——那只用来信号安全着陆的铃。

sentences.en: She rang it *twice*, which was the code for something rare: a word fragment found intact, unbroken, still glowing at the edges.
The whole troupe fell quiet and gathered close around her open palm.
sentences.cn: 整个队伍安静下来，围拢到她张开的手掌边。

aspect:2.en: Old Helm walked a slow circle around the floating stone, studying it from every angle. 'Every *aspect* of this thing feels wrong,' he muttered. The carvings faced inward instead of out. The steps led down instead of up. Even the shadow it cast pointed toward the sun rather than away.
aspect:2.cnHint: 老赫姆仔细观察那块浮石的每个____，感到处处不对劲。
aspect:2.hook: A stone built backwards can only mean one thing: a warning.
aspect:2.line: 'Every *aspect* of this stone tells us someone wanted it hidden.'

sentences.en: Old Helm walked a slow circle around the floating stone, studying it from every angle.
sentences.cn: 老舵绕着浮石走了一圈，从每个角度研究着它。

sentences.en: 'Every *aspect* of this thing feels wrong,' he muttered.
The carvings faced inward instead of out.
sentences.cn: 雕刻面向内侧而不是外侧。

sentences.en: The steps led down instead of up.
sentences.cn: 台阶向下而不是向上。

sentences.en: Even the shadow it cast pointed toward the sun rather than away.
sentences.cn: 连它投出的影子都指向太阳而不是背离太阳。

currently:2.en: Bell unrolled the living map — the one that updated itself as the troupe travelled. 'We are *currently* above the Amber Drift,' she announced, tapping a soft golden region near the map's centre. Below us, through a gap in the clouds, we could see warm light rising like breath from a sleeping creature.
currently:2.cnHint: 小铃查看活地图，确认船队____所在的位置。
currently:2.hook: The warm light below was rising — and rising far too quickly.
currently:2.line: 'We are *currently* right above the thing that is waking up.'

sentences.en: Bell unrolled the living map — the one that updated itself as the troupe travelled.
sentences.cn: 小铃卷开了生活地图——那张随着队伍旅行而自我更新的地图。

sentences.en: 'We are *currently* above the Amber Drift,' she announced, tapping a soft golden region near the map's centre.
Below us, through a gap in the clouds, we could see warm light rising like breath from a sleeping creature.
sentences.cn: 透过云层的间隙往下看，我们能看到温暖的光从一个沉睡生物的体内升起，如同呼吸。

decrease:2.en: 'The stars are going out,' Old Helm said quietly. I looked up and saw he was right. One by one, small lights were vanishing from the edge of the sky inward. Each minute brought a *decrease* in their number, as if someone far away was folding the night like a cloth, tucking the stars inside.
decrease:2.cnHint: 老赫姆注意到星星的数量在____，仿佛夜空正在收拢。
decrease:2.hook: When the last star folds away, what will light our path?
decrease:2.line: 'This steady *decrease* means the chapter of the night is closing.'

sentences.en: 'The stars are going out,' Old Helm said quietly.
sentences.cn: "星星在熄灭，"老舵轻声说。

sentences.en: I looked up and saw he was right.
sentences.cn: 我抬起头，发现他说得对。

sentences.en: One by one, small lights were vanishing from the edge of the sky inward.
sentences.cn: 一颗接一颗的微光从天边的边缘往里消失。

sentences.en: Each minute brought a *decrease* in their number, as if someone far away was folding the night like a cloth, tucking the stars inside.

possibility:2.en: Silverfang spread the recovered fragments across the deck and stared at them for a long time. 'There is a *possibility*,' he said at last, 'that these pieces do not form a map at all.' He looked up, eyes bright with something between worry and excitement. 'They might be a door — or the key to one.'
possibility:2.cnHint: 竞争船长凝视碎片，提出了一个令人震惊的____。
possibility:2.hook: A door to where — and should we dare to open it?
possibility:2.line: 'The *possibility* that this is a key, not a map, changes everything.'

sentences.en: Silverfang spread the recovered fragments across the deck and stared at them for a long time.
sentences.cn: 银牙把找回的碎片铺在甲板上，盯着它们看了很久。

sentences.en: 'There is a *possibility*,' he said at last, 'that these pieces do not form a map at all.'
He looked up, eyes bright with something between worry and excitement.
sentences.cn: 他抬起头，眼睛里闪烁着忧虑和兴奋之间的某种光芒。

sentences.en: 'They might be a door — or the key to one.'
sentences.cn: "它们可能是一扇门——或者是打开门的钥匙。"

crucial:2.en: The ink on the bark was already fading in the cold air. Bell worked fast, copying the symbol onto a fresh sheet. 'This detail here is *crucial*,' she said, pressing her finger just above a tiny spiral at the base of the mark. Without it, the copied symbol would point us to open sky — nowhere at all.
crucial:2.cnHint: 小铃抓紧抄写符文，叮嘱大家其中一个细节____，绝不能遗漏。
crucial:2.hook: One missing spiral, and the whole journey leads to nothing.
crucial:2.line: 'That small spiral is *crucial* — lose it and we lose our way entirely.'

sentences.en: The ink on the bark was already fading in the cold air.
sentences.cn: 树皮上的墨水已经在冷空气里褪色了。

sentences.en: Bell worked fast, copying the symbol onto a fresh sheet.
sentences.cn: 小铃快手快脚地把符号复制到新纸张上。

sentences.en: 'This detail here is *crucial*,' she said, pressing her finger just above a tiny spiral at the base of the mark.
Without it, the copied symbol would point us to open sky — nowhere at all.
sentences.cn: 没有它，复制的符号会指向空无一物的天空——哪儿都不是。

rule:2.en: Deep inside the Archive Grotto, shelves of carved stone held every *rule* the island councils had ever written. Bell ran her finger along one dusty tablet and whispered that whoever first set these rules had wanted peace, not power. A single tablet near the back was blank — waiting.
rule:2.cnHint: 小铃在档案洞窟里发现石板上刻满了岛屿议会定下的____，其中一块却空白。
rule:2.hook: The blank tablet began to glow the moment she touched it.
rule:2.line: 'Every *rule* here was written to protect someone,' Bell said softly.

sentences.en: Deep inside the Archive Grotto, shelves of carved stone held every *rule* the island councils had ever written.
Bell ran her finger along one dusty tablet and whispered that whoever first set these rules had wanted peace, not power.
sentences.cn: 小铃用指尖沿着一块尘封的石板滑动，低声说最初制定这些规则的人想要的是和平，而不是权力。

sentences.en: A single tablet near the back was blank — waiting.
sentences.cn: 靠后的一块石板是空白的——在等待。

plant:2.en: Old Helm held up a tiny *plant* he had found wedged between two sky-stones at the island's edge. Its roots gripped nothing but thin air, yet its leaves shone silver in the starlight. He said it was proof that life finds a way even where there is no ground.
plant:2.cnHint: 老赫尔姆在悬空岛边缘发现了一株奇异的____，它的根悬在空中却生长茂盛。
plant:2.hook: Then the plant released a single glowing seed into the dark.
plant:2.line: 'This little *plant* has more courage than most sailors I know,' Old Helm laughed.

sentences.en: Old Helm held up a tiny *plant* he had found wedged between two sky-stones at the island's edge.
Its roots gripped nothing but thin air, yet its leaves shone silver in the starlight.
sentences.cn: 它的根须没有任何着力点，只抓住了薄薄的空气，可叶子在星光下闪闪发银。

sentences.en: He said it was proof that life finds a way even where there is no ground.
sentences.cn: 他说这证明了生命即使在没有地面的地方也能找到出路。

national:2.en: We discovered a faded banner stretched across the gateway to the Amber Market — a *national* flag of an island-state that no longer existed. Bell said every nation leaves something behind. We folded the banner carefully and carried it with us as a kind of tribute.
national:2.cnHint: 我们在琥珀市场的门廊发现了一面已消失的岛国____旗帜。
national:2.hook: Stitched into the hem was a tiny map no one had noticed before.
national:2.line: 'A *national* flag is a story stitched in cloth,' Bell said quietly.

sentences.en: We discovered a faded banner stretched across the gateway to the Amber Market — a *national* flag of an island-state that no longer existed.
Bell said every nation leaves something behind.
sentences.cn: 小铃说每个国家都会留下什么东西。

sentences.en: We folded the banner carefully and carried it with us as a kind of tribute.
sentences.cn: 我们小心地折起那面旗帜，把它带在身边作为一种致敬。

doctor:2.en: A brass nameplate on the observatory door read: DR. VELL, KEEPER OF FALLING STARS. Old Helm called out, but no one answered. Still, the title — *doctor* of stars — made me feel that whoever worked here had dedicated a whole life to this sky.
doctor:2.cnHint: 观测台门上的铭牌显示着一位____的名字，但屋内空无一人。
doctor:2.hook: A chair still rocked gently, as if someone had just stood up.
doctor:2.line: 'A *doctor* of stars — now that is a title worth earning,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: A brass nameplate on the observatory door read: DR.
sentences.cn: 天文台门上的铜牌写着：博士

sentences.en: VELL, KEEPER OF FALLING STARS.
sentences.cn: 韦尔，陨星守护者。

sentences.en: Old Helm called out, but no one answered.
sentences.cn: 老舵喊了一声，没人应答。

sentences.en: Still, the title — *doctor* of stars — made me feel that whoever worked here had dedicated a whole life to this sky.

economy:2.en: Inside the old trading post we found a ledger titled THE *ECONOMY* OF THE HIGH ISLANDS — every exchange logged in careful ink: words traded for maps, maps traded for safe passage. Bell said the whole floating world ran not on gold but on knowledge shared freely.
economy:2.cnHint: 小铃在贸易站的账本里发现了高空岛屿间的____体系——以知识换地图，以地图换通行。
economy:2.hook: The last entry was dated the very night the islands went silent.
economy:2.line: 'A true *economy* runs on what people choose to share,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Inside the old trading post we found a ledger titled THE *ECONOMY* OF THE HIGH ISLANDS — every exchange logged in careful ink: words traded for maps, maps traded for safe passage.
Bell said the whole floating world ran not on gold but on knowledge shared freely.
sentences.cn: 小铃说整个浮空世界运转靠的不是金子，而是自由分享的知识。

global:2.en: The cartographer's table held a single great sphere etched with every known floating island — a *global* map of our whole sky-world. Silverfang traced the trade routes with one claw and said, quietly, that she had never seen all the paths drawn together before.
global:2.cnHint: 制图师的桌上放着一个刻有全部浮岛的____地图球体，银牙第一次看到所有航路汇聚在一起。
global:2.hook: One island on the sphere had no name — only a question mark.
global:2.line: 'A *global* view changes everything you thought you knew,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: The cartographer's table held a single great sphere etched with every known floating island — a *global* map of our whole sky-world.
Silverfang traced the trade routes with one claw and said, quietly, that she had never seen all the paths drawn together before.
sentences.cn: 银牙用一只爪子沿着贸易路线描过，轻声说她从未见过所有的路线聚在一起过。

leader:2.en: Carved above the council chamber entrance was a single sentence: A TRUE *LEADER* LISTENS BEFORE SHE SPEAKS. Bell stood under it for a long moment. She said she had read those words before, somewhere far away, and finding them here felt like a sign meant only for her.
leader:2.cnHint: 小铃在议事堂门楣上读到了一句关于____的格言，感到这像是专门写给她的。
leader:2.hook: Below the carving, someone had recently scratched one word: 'when?'
leader:2.line: 'A *leader* who only talks is just a very loud echo,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Carved above the council chamber entrance was a single sentence: A TRUE *LEADER* LISTENS BEFORE SHE SPEAKS.
Bell stood under it for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 小铃在那儿站了好一会儿。

sentences.en: She said she had read those words before, somewhere far away, and finding them here felt like a sign meant only for her.
sentences.cn: 她说自己在远方某处读过这些字，在这儿看到它们感觉像是只为她留下的信号。

scientific:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow sky-stone we found a notebook full of careful diagrams and neat numbers — a *scientific* record of how the islands stayed afloat. Old Helm flipped to the last page and found a single line: 'the answer is simpler than we feared.' He looked up, eyes bright.
scientific:2.cnHint: 我们在空心天石里找到了一本关于浮岛如何漂浮的____笔记，最后一页写着答案比想象中简单。
scientific:2.hook: But the page that should explain the answer had been torn out.
scientific:2.line: '*Scientific* or not, someone went to great trouble to hide this,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Tucked inside a hollow sky-stone we found a notebook full of careful diagrams and neat numbers — a *scientific* record of how the islands stayed afloat.
Old Helm flipped to the last page and found a single line: 'the answer is simpler than we feared.'
sentences.cn: 老舵翻到最后一页，发现了一句话："答案比我们害怕的要简单。"

sentences.en: He looked up, eyes bright.
sentences.cn: 他抬起头，眼睛闪闪发亮。

enormous:2.en: The message was carved into the side of an *enormous* rock that floated all on its own between two islands. I had to lean over the ship's edge just to read it. Old Helm placed a hand on my shoulder. The letters spelled out a single word — and that word was our next map fragment.
enormous:2.cnHint: 我们在一块漂浮的巨石上发现了刻着____文字的神秘信息。
enormous:2.hook: The word on the rock pointed to an island none of us had ever heard of.
