enormous:2.line: 'That *enormous* rock has been waiting here longer than our ship has been flying,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The message was carved into the side of an *enormous* rock that floated all on its own between two islands.
I had to lean over the ship's edge just to read it.
sentences.cn: 我不得不探出船舷才能读清楚。

sentences.en: Old Helm placed a hand on my shoulder.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手放在我肩上。

sentences.en: The letters spelled out a single word — and that word was our next map fragment.
sentences.cn: 那些字母拼出了一个单词——也是我们下一块地图碎片。

pet:2.en: Tucked inside the hollow of a drifting log, we found a tiny creature with silver ears and calm eyes. Bell knelt down and smiled. Old Helm called it a stray, but the way it followed Bell back to the deck told a different story. By evening, the troupe had a new *pet* — and a new reason to keep sailing.
pet:2.cnHint: 小铃在漂流木中发现了一只小动物，它成了大家的____。
pet:2.hook: The little creature's eyes reflected a star that did not appear on any chart.
pet:2.line: 'Every good crew needs a *pet* to keep their hearts warm on cold nights,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Tucked inside the hollow of a drifting log, we found a tiny creature with silver ears and calm eyes.
sentences.cn: 在一根漂流木的空心处，我们发现了一只小生物，有银色的耳朵和沉静的眼睛。

sentences.en: Bell knelt down and smiled.
sentences.cn: 小铃跪下来，笑了。

sentences.en: Old Helm called it a stray, but the way it followed Bell back to the deck told a different story.
sentences.cn: 老舵说它是只流浪的，但它跟着小铃回到甲板的样子讲了另一个故事。

sentences.en: By evening, the troupe had a new *pet* — and a new reason to keep sailing.

restaurant:2.en: The island of Calla had only one building — a small *restaurant* carved from pale stone, its windows glowing with amber light. A folded note on the counter read: 'The next word is hidden under the table by the window.' We found it pressed beneath a smooth river rock, waiting like a quiet secret.
restaurant:2.cnHint: 我们在一座小岛的____里找到了藏着地图碎片的便条。
restaurant:2.hook: The chair by the window was still warm, as though someone had just stood up.
restaurant:2.line: 'I have never walked into a *restaurant* and found a map fragment before,' Silverfang said, almost smiling.

sentences.en: The island of Calla had only one building — a small *restaurant* carved from pale stone, its windows glowing with amber light.
A folded note on the counter read: 'The next word is hidden under the table by the window.'
sentences.cn: 柜台上放着一张折叠的纸条，写着："下一个字藏在靠窗的桌子底下。"

sentences.en: We found it pressed beneath a smooth river rock, waiting like a quiet secret.
sentences.cn: 我们在一块光滑的河石下找到了它，像一个安静的秘密一样等着我们。

driver:2.en: The old sky-sled at the edge of the island had no crew — only a wooden seat and a brass lever. A sign above the lever named its last *driver* as someone called Wren. Below the name, scratched in small letters, was a word we recognised at once. Old Helm read it aloud, and the map in his hand gave a soft, bright pulse.
driver:2.cnHint: 我们在无人驾驶的旧飞橇上发现了前____留下的地图碎片线索。
driver:2.hook: The brass lever moved on its own, just once, as if offering to take us somewhere.
driver:2.line: 'The last *driver* of this sled left us exactly what we needed,' Old Helm said quietly.

sentences.en: The old sky-sled at the edge of the island had no crew — only a wooden seat and a brass lever.
sentences.cn: 岛边的旧天空雪橇上没有船员——只有一张木椅和一根铜杆。

sentences.en: A sign above the lever named its last *driver* as someone called Wren.
Below the name, scratched in small letters, was a word we recognised at once.
sentences.cn: 名字下面用小字刻着一个我们立刻认出来的字。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it aloud, and the map in his hand gave a soft, bright pulse.
sentences.cn: 老舵大声读了出来，他手里的地图发出了柔和明亮的脉动。

dream:2.en: Bell found the glass bottle wedged between two roots on the edge of the island. Inside was a rolled note that read: 'Follow your *dream* — it leads east, past the twin moons.' We had no twin moons on our charts. Old Helm tapped his chin. Silverfang was already turning the wheel east.
dream:2.cnHint: 小铃在瓶中发现了一张字条，指引我们追随____向东航行。
dream:2.hook: Past the clouds, two faint silver shapes hung in the sky side by side.
dream:2.line: 'Every *dream* worth chasing leaves a trail,' Old Helm said, folding the note with care.

sentences.en: Bell found the glass bottle wedged between two roots on the edge of the island.
sentences.cn: 小铃在岛边两根树根之间发现了那个玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside was a rolled note that read: 'Follow your *dream* — it leads east, past the twin moons.'
We had no twin moons on our charts.
sentences.cn: 我们的海图上没有双月。

sentences.en: Old Helm tapped his chin.
sentences.cn: 老舵敲了敲下巴。

sentences.en: Silverfang was already turning the wheel east.
sentences.cn: 银牙已经把舵向东转了。

consumer:2.en: The market stall was abandoned, but a chalk board still listed its goods — light, warmth, and sound, each priced in words. A small printed card explained: 'Every *consumer* pays with one word and receives one in return.' I reached into my pocket and paid. What came back was a fragment that fit perfectly into our map.
consumer:2.cnHint: 在一个奇特的市集摊位，每个____用一个词语换取一个地图碎片。
consumer:2.hook: The word I received glowed faintly, as if it had been waiting only for me.
consumer:2.line: 'As a *consumer* of words, you must spend them wisely,' the chalk board read at the bottom.

sentences.en: The market stall was abandoned, but a chalk board still listed its goods — light, warmth, and sound, each priced in words.
sentences.cn: 集市摊位被废弃了，但一块粉笔板上仍然列着它的商品——光、温暖和声音，每样都标着价格。

sentences.en: A small printed card explained: 'Every *consumer* pays with one word and receives one in return.'
I reached into my pocket and paid.
sentences.cn: 我伸进口袋付了钱。

sentences.en: What came back was a fragment that fit perfectly into our map.
sentences.cn: 得到的东西完美地拼进了我们的地图里。

interesting:2.en: Silverfang spread the new chart across the navigation table and studied it for a long moment. 'Look here,' she said, pointing to a cluster of islands shaped like a key. 'This is *interesting* — the shape only appears when you hold the three fragments together.' We pressed them side by side, and a path lit up across the chart like a river of gold.
interesting:2.cnHint: 银牙发现把三块地图碎片拼在一起会出现____的新图案。
interesting:2.hook: The golden path on the chart led to an island marked only with a question mark.
interesting:2.line: '*Interesting* — the fragments only make sense when they are together,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang spread the new chart across the navigation table and studied it for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 银牙把新海图铺开在航海台上，研究了很久。

sentences.en: 'Look here,' she said, pointing to a cluster of islands shaped like a key.
sentences.cn: "看这儿，"她指着一簇形如钥匙的岛屿说。

sentences.en: 'This is *interesting* — the shape only appears when you hold the three fragments together.'
We pressed them side by side, and a path lit up across the chart like a river of gold.
sentences.cn: 我们把三块碎片并排按到一起，一条路径在海图上亮了起来，像一条黄金之河。

grade:2.en: The stone pillar near the island's edge was covered in small marks, each one a *grade* carved by a traveller who had solved the riddle here before us. The highest mark had a name beneath it: Old Helm. He looked away quickly, but I could see him smile. Below the marks, the next word was etched in clean, careful letters.
grade:2.cnHint: 我们在石柱上发现了历代旅行者留下的____刻痕，最高等级下写着老舵的名字。
grade:2.hook: The clean letters at the bottom of the pillar seemed to have been carved only yesterday.
grade:2.line: 'I left that *grade* many years ago, when I was as new to this world as you are now,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The stone pillar near the island's edge was covered in small marks, each one a *grade* carved by a traveller who had solved the riddle here before us.
The highest mark had a name beneath it: Old Helm.
sentences.cn: 最高的刻痕下面刻着一个名字：老舵。

sentences.en: He looked away quickly, but I could see him smile.
sentences.cn: 他很快移开了视线，但我看到他在笑。

sentences.en: Below the marks, the next word was etched in clean, careful letters.
sentences.cn: 刻痕下面，下一个词用笔直、谨慎的字体蚀刻在石头上。

evidence:2.en: Deep in the Archive Shelf — a cluster of stone tablets floating in a slow circle — I found a cracked tablet covered in star-charts. Old Helm knelt beside it, tracing the lines with one finger. 'This is *evidence*,' he said quietly, 'that someone mapped these islands long before us.'
evidence:2.cnHint: 在档案架岛上，老舵发现了一块古老石板，认为它是某个先行者留下的____。
evidence:2.hook: But whose hand had carved those charts, and why stop here?
evidence:2.line: 'This is *evidence* that someone sailed these skies before us.'

sentences.en: Deep in the Archive Shelf — a cluster of stone tablets floating in a slow circle — I found a cracked tablet covered in star-charts.
sentences.cn: 在档案架深处——一簇悬浮缓缓转动的石板——我找到了一块布满星图的裂纹石板。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt beside it, tracing the lines with one finger.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪在它旁边，用一根手指描过那些线条。

sentences.en: 'This is *evidence*,' he said quietly, 'that someone mapped these islands long before us.'

prefer:2.en: The Blossom Terrace island smelled of warm rain and pale flowers. Bell offered me two paths: a rope bridge swaying in the wind, or a narrow ledge cut into the rock. I told her I would *prefer* the ledge. She smiled and said that was the answer she had hoped for.
prefer:2.cnHint: 在花台岛，小铃让我选择路线，我说我____走岩石小道。
prefer:2.hook: The ledge was narrower than either of us had admitted.
prefer:2.line: 'I *prefer* the quiet road — it always hides the better view.'

sentences.en: The Blossom Terrace island smelled of warm rain and pale flowers.
sentences.cn: 花开台地岛闻起来有温暖的雨水和淡色花朵的味道。

sentences.en: Bell offered me two paths: a rope bridge swaying in the wind, or a narrow ledge cut into the rock.
sentences.cn: 小铃给了我两条路：一座在风中摇晃的绳桥，或一条凿在岩石里的狭窄石笋。

sentences.en: I told her I would *prefer* the ledge.
She smiled and said that was the answer she had hoped for.
sentences.cn: 她笑着说那是她希望听到的答案。

interview:2.en: On the Lantern Barge — a wide, flat island lit by a hundred hanging lights — Silverfang sat across from me with a small notebook. He said he liked to *interview* every new member of a troupe before trusting them with a route. I answered each question as honestly as I could.
interview:2.cnHint: 在灯笼浮岛上，竞争船长拿着小册子正式____了我，考察我是否值得信任。
interview:2.hook: His last question was the one I had not prepared for.
interview:2.line: 'I *interview* every navigator before I share my maps — no exceptions.'

sentences.en: On the Lantern Barge — a wide, flat island lit by a hundred hanging lights — Silverfang sat across from me with a small notebook.
sentences.cn: 在灯笼驳船上——一个宽阔平坦的岛屿，被百盏悬挂的灯光照亮——银牙坐在我对面，手里拿着一本小笔记本。

sentences.en: He said he liked to *interview* every new member of a troupe before trusting them with a route.
I answered each question as honestly as I could.
sentences.cn: 我尽可能诚实地回答了每一个问题。

middle:2.en: The Crystal Drift island had a single glowing pillar standing in the *middle* of a flat stone floor. Old Helm circled it twice without speaking. The pillar hummed at a low, steady pitch, and faint letters rose and fell along its surface like fish moving under clear water.
middle:2.cnHint: 在水晶漂流岛上，正中央有一根发光柱子，老舵绕着它转圈研究。
middle:2.hook: When he finally touched it, the hum changed to a name.
middle:2.line: 'Stand in the *middle* and listen — the island speaks from its centre.'

sentences.en: The Crystal Drift island had a single glowing pillar standing in the *middle* of a flat stone floor.
Old Helm circled it twice without speaking.
sentences.cn: 老舵绕着它转了两圈，一言不发。

sentences.en: The pillar hummed at a low, steady pitch, and faint letters rose and fell along its surface like fish moving under clear water.
sentences.cn: 石柱发出低沉、稳定的嗡鸣，微弱的字母在它的表面上升起又消落，就像鱼在清水下游动。

standard:2.en: Silverfang unrolled a chart on the deck of the Cloud Notch, a crescent island shaped like a bent finger. He tapped a small symbol printed in every corner. 'That mark is the *standard* seal of the old sky-guilds,' he said. 'Any map without it is a guess dressed as a fact.'
standard:2.cnHint: 竞争船长在云缺岛上展开地图，解释角落里的印记是古老天空行会的____印章。
standard:2.hook: Our newest map carried no such seal at all.
standard:2.line: 'A *standard* seal means someone staked their name on this route.'

sentences.en: Silverfang unrolled a chart on the deck of the Cloud Notch, a crescent island shaped like a bent finger.
sentences.cn: 银牙在云缺的甲板上展开了一张海图，那是一个弯曲得像弓指的新月形岛屿。

sentences.en: He tapped a small symbol printed in every corner.
sentences.cn: 他点了点印在每个角落的一个小符号。

sentences.en: 'That mark is the *standard* seal of the old sky-guilds,' he said.
'Any map without it is a guess dressed as a fact.'
sentences.cn: 任何没有这个标记的地图都只是猜测披着事实的外衣。

subject:2.en: Around the fire on Ember Notch, Old Helm told stories about the old sky-guilds. I noticed that every tale circled the same *subject*: a missing island that appeared on charts but was never found. Bell watched the flames and said nothing, though her eyes gave away that she knew more than the rest of us.
subject:2.cnHint: 在余烬缺口岛，老舵讲的故事都围绕着同一个____——一座从未被找到的神秘岛屿。
subject:2.hook: Bell's silence on that subject felt louder than any answer.
subject:2.line: 'Every map we own shares the same *subject* — that one lost island.'

sentences.en: Around the fire on Ember Notch, Old Helm told stories about the old sky-guilds.
sentences.cn: 在余烬凹陷的篝火旁，老舵讲了一些关于古代空中行会的故事。

sentences.en: I noticed that every tale circled the same *subject*: a missing island that appeared on charts but was never found.
Bell watched the flames and said nothing, though her eyes gave away that she knew more than the rest of us.
sentences.cn: 小铃盯着火焰什么也没说，不过她的眼睛泄露了秘密——她比我们任何人都懂得更多。

accept:2.en: At the Driftwood Gate — an island built entirely from pale, tangled timber — Silverfang offered Old Helm a sealed route-scroll in exchange for safe passage through our airspace. Old Helm held it for a long moment before deciding to *accept*. The scroll felt heavier than paper had any right to feel.
accept:2.cnHint: 在浮木关岛，老舵考虑再三后决定____了竞争船长递来的航线卷轴。
accept:2.hook: Whatever was sealed inside had been waiting a very long time.
accept:2.line: 'I will *accept* this scroll, but the debt between us is not settled.'

sentences.en: At the Driftwood Gate — an island built entirely from pale, tangled timber — Silverfang offered Old Helm a sealed route-scroll in exchange for safe passage through our airspace.
sentences.cn: 在漂木门岛——一个完全由苍白的、缠绕的木头建造的岛屿——银牙向老舵提出用一份密封的路线卷轴来交换安全通过我们领空的权利。

sentences.en: Old Helm held it for a long moment before deciding to *accept*.
The scroll felt heavier than paper had any right to feel.
sentences.cn: 那卷轴的分量比纸张理应有的重量要沉。

act:2.en: On the Pale Mirror island — a stretch of smooth white stone that reflected the stars perfectly — Old Helm gave me my first real task. He said that finding a route is only half the work; the harder *act* is choosing which stars to follow when the sky gives you too many answers at once.
act:2.cnHint: 在白镜岛，老舵告诉我，在星光中选择正确的方向才是真正困难的____。
act:2.hook: Above us, three new stars blinked on at exactly the same moment.
act:2.line: 'Choosing which star to trust — that is the bravest *act* I know.'

sentences.en: On the Pale Mirror island — a stretch of smooth white stone that reflected the stars perfectly — Old Helm gave me my first real task.
sentences.cn: 在苍白镜子岛上——一片光滑的白色石头，能完美地反射星光——老舵给了我第一个真正的任务。

sentences.en: He said that finding a route is only half the work; the harder *act* is choosing which stars to follow when the sky gives you too many answers at once.

meanwhile:2.en: Bell spread the old chart across the deck and traced the ink lines with one careful finger. The star called Ember had moved since the map was drawn. *Meanwhile*, Old Helm stood at the bow, watching the sky with quiet eyes, as if the stars were old friends arriving late to a long-planned gathering.
meanwhile:2.cnHint: 小铃研究星图时，老舵手在船头静静注视星空，____，风在桅杆间低鸣。
meanwhile:2.hook: One star on the chart had no name — only a question mark.
meanwhile:2.line: '*Meanwhile*, you were sleeping, the sky was writing us a new road,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell spread the old chart across the deck and traced the ink lines with one careful finger.
sentences.cn: 小铃把那张老地图铺在甲板上，用一根仔细的手指沿着墨线描过。

sentences.en: The star called Ember had moved since the map was drawn.
sentences.cn: 名叫余烬的星星自从地图被画出来以后就移动过了。

sentences.en: *Meanwhile*, Old Helm stood at the bow, watching the sky with quiet eyes, as if the stars were old friends arriving late to a long-planned gathering.

damage:2.en: The small island had drifted too close to the frost current. Ice had crept across its stone bridge, cracking it from end to end. Old Helm knelt and pressed his palm to the break. 'The *damage* is deep,' he said softly, 'but islands have a way of healing if you give them time and a kind word.'
damage:2.cnHint: 浮岛的石桥被寒流冻裂，老舵手察看____后若有所思地站起身。
damage:2.hook: Beneath the cracked stone, something faintly glowed.
damage:2.line: 'The *damage* looks bad, but I have seen worse things mend,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The small island had drifted too close to the frost current.
sentences.cn: 这个小岛漂得太靠近寒流了。

sentences.en: Ice had crept across its stone bridge, cracking it from end to end.
sentences.cn: 冰已经爬过了它的石桥，从头到尾把它裂开了。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt and pressed his palm to the break.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪下来，把手掌贴在裂口上。

sentences.en: 'The *damage* is deep,' he said softly, 'but islands have a way of healing if you give them time and a kind word.'

police:2.en: The market island of Twinbell had its own order-keepers: three tall figures in silver coats who called themselves the *police* of the high roads. They stopped our cart at the gate, checked each word-fragment we carried, and stamped them with a small cloud-shaped seal before letting us roll through the lantern-lit street.
police:2.cnHint: 在双铃岛的集市入口，浮空____拦下了我们的货车，仔细检查我们携带的词语碎片。
police:2.hook: The third officer stared at our newest word-fragment a moment too long.
police:2.line: 'The *police* here see every word that passes through this gate,' the officer said.

sentences.en: The market island of Twinbell had its own order-keepers: three tall figures in silver coats who called themselves the *police* of the high roads.
They stopped our cart at the gate, checked each word-fragment we carried, and stamped them with a small cloud-shaped seal before letting us roll through the lantern-lit street.
sentences.cn: 他们在大门口拦下了我们的车，检查了我们携带的每一个词语碎片，用一个小云朵形的印章给它们盖章，然后才让我们驶过灯火通明的街道。

race:2.en: Silverfang challenged Old Helm to a *race* across the Needle Straits: first ship to touch the red buoy and return would claim the fragment called 'Dawn.' Our whole troupe lined the rail, hearts loud in our chests, as both vessels leaned into the wind like two great birds chasing the same bright horizon.
race:2.cnHint: 竞争船长向老舵手发起了一场____，胜者将获得名为"黎明"的词语碎片。
race:2.hook: Then a third sail appeared from behind the clouds.
race:2.line: 'A *race* is the fairest way to decide who earns the word,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Silverfang challenged Old Helm to a *race* across the Needle Straits: first ship to touch the red buoy and return would claim the fragment called 'Dawn.'
Our whole troupe lined the rail, hearts loud in our chests, as both vessels leaned into the wind like two great birds chasing the same bright horizon.
sentences.cn: 我们整个剧团都靠在栏杆边，心跳声响得能听见，两艘船都倾身向风，就像两只巨鸟追逐同一条明亮的地平线。

medical:2.en: High on the Herb Shelf island, a small stone room held shelves of dried flowers, pressed roots, and jars of blue powder. Bell called it the *medical* store of the sky roads — a place old travellers had built so that anyone hurt by wind or cold could find help without needing a coin in their pocket.
medical:2.cnHint: 在草架岛的石屋里，小铃向我介绍了这间____储藏室，说它是天空航路上的免费救助站。
medical:2.hook: One jar on the highest shelf had today's date scratched into its lid.
medical:2.line: 'Every *medical* supply here was left by someone who once needed help themselves,' said Bell.

sentences.en: High on the Herb Shelf island, a small stone room held shelves of dried flowers, pressed roots, and jars of blue powder.
sentences.cn: 在草药架岛的高处，有间小石屋，架子上放着干花、压干的根茎，还有装着蓝色粉末的罐子。

sentences.en: Bell called it the *medical* store of the sky roads — a place old travellers had built so that anyone hurt by wind or cold could find help without needing a coin in their pocket.

wear:2.en: Old Helm handed me a coat stitched from sky-cloth — light as breath but warm as a held hand. 'You will *wear* the cold up here if you have nothing between you and the wind,' he said, fastening the top button with careful fingers. The fabric shimmered once, as if the sky was glad to be worn.
wear:2.cnHint: 老舵手把一件天空布料的外套递给我，说在高空____上这种寒意需要好好防护。
wear:2.hook: The coat's lining was covered in tiny stitched words I could not read yet.
wear:2.line: '*Wear* it well — this coat has crossed more skies than either of us,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Old Helm handed me a coat stitched from sky-cloth — light as breath but warm as a held hand.
sentences.cn: 老舵递给我一件用天布缝的外套——轻得像呼吸，暖得像被握住的手。

sentences.en: 'You will *wear* the cold up here if you have nothing between you and the wind,' he said, fastening the top button with careful fingers.
The fabric shimmered once, as if the sky was glad to be worn.
sentences.cn: 布料闪烁了一下，好像天空很高兴被穿在身上。

climate:2.en: The island of Driftmoss sat inside its own bubble of warm, wet air. Bell explained that each floating island makes its own small *climate*, the way a person carries their own mood into a room. Here, ferns curled over every surface and soft rain tapped the leaves in a steady, gentle rhythm that made you want to stay.
climate:2.cnHint: 小铃解释说，漂流苔岛拥有独特的____，温暖湿润，仿佛一个人将自己的心情带入了房间。
climate:2.hook: But something in that perfect warmth felt deliberately arranged.
climate:2.line: 'The *climate* here is too comfortable — someone is keeping it this way on purpose,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The island of Driftmoss sat inside its own bubble of warm, wet air.
sentences.cn: 浮萍岛坐在自己的温暖潮湿的空气泡里。

sentences.en: Bell explained that each floating island makes its own small *climate*, the way a person carries their own mood into a room.
Here, ferns curled over every surface and soft rain tapped the leaves in a steady, gentle rhythm that made you want to stay.
sentences.cn: 这里蕨类铺满每个表面，细雨敲打着树叶，节奏稳定而温柔，让人想停留。

head:2.en: At the very *head* of the stone table sat an empty chair, and on the chair rested a folded note sealed with wax the colour of old stars. Old Helm picked it up slowly, turned it over twice, and looked at each of us in turn. No one had put it there when we arrived. The room had been empty.
head:2.cnHint: 在石桌的____端，一把空椅子上安静地放着一封封蜡印信件，而我们到来时房间明明是空的。
head:2.hook: The wax seal bore the shape of our own troupe's flag.
head:2.line: 'Whoever left this note at the *head* of the table knew we were coming,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: At the very *head* of the stone table sat an empty chair, and on the chair rested a folded note sealed with wax the colour of old stars.
Old Helm picked it up slowly, turned it over twice, and looked at each of us in turn.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢拿起来，翻转了两次，逐个看向我们每一个人。

sentences.en: No one had put it there when we arrived.
sentences.cn: 没有人在我们到达时放过东西。

sentences.en: The room had been empty.
sentences.cn: 房间是空的。

field:2.en: Bell spread the star-chart across a flat rock and pointed to a glowing patch near the island's edge. 'This *field* of light,' she said softly, 'is where fallen stars collect before they rise again.' Old Helm knelt beside her, eyes wide, reading the map like a letter from an old friend.
field:2.cnHint: 小铃在星图上发现了一片发光的____，据说那里是星星重新升起的地方。
field:2.hook: Something beneath the glowing field had just begun to move.
field:2.line: 'This *field* of light holds every star that ever fell.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the star-chart across a flat rock and pointed to a glowing patch near the island's edge.
sentences.cn: 小铃把星图铺在平石上，指向岛边附近一个发光的区域。

sentences.en: 'This *field* of light,' she said softly, 'is where fallen stars collect before they rise again.'
Old Helm knelt beside her, eyes wide, reading the map like a letter from an old friend.
sentences.cn: 老舵在她身边跪下，眼睛睁得很大，读着地图就像读一封老朋友的信。

personality:2.en: We found a carved stone near the bridge, etched with tiny faces, each one different. Old Helm laughed and said the island itself had a *personality* — stubborn in the morning, generous by night. He pressed his hand to the stone and the whole bridge lit up, warm as a lantern.
personality:2.cnHint: 老船长说这座岛有自己的____，并用手触碰了刻有面孔的石头。
personality:2.hook: The lantern-light spelled out a name none of us recognised.
personality:2.line: 'Every island has its own *personality*, if you take time to listen.'

sentences.en: We found a carved stone near the bridge, etched with tiny faces, each one different.
sentences.cn: 我们在桥边找到一块雕过的石头，上面刻满了细小的脸孔，每一个都不一样。

sentences.en: Old Helm laughed and said the island itself had a *personality* — stubborn in the morning, generous by night.
He pressed his hand to the stone and the whole bridge lit up, warm as a lantern.
sentences.cn: 他把手放在石头上，整座桥都亮了起来，暖得像一盏灯笼。

size:2.en: The message-bottle Bell pulled from the cloud-stream was no bigger than her thumb. The *size* surprised us all — how could anything so small carry a full set of map-words? Old Helm held it to the starlight and smiled. Inside, folded impossibly thin, was an entire new island.
size:2.cnHint: 小铃从云流中取出一个瓶子，它的____让大家都感到惊讶，但里面藏着一整座新岛屿。
size:2.hook: The island inside the bottle was already disappearing.
size:2.line: 'Don't let the *size* fool you — small things carry the biggest secrets.'

sentences.en: The message-bottle Bell pulled from the cloud-stream was no bigger than her thumb.
sentences.cn: 小铃从云流里拉出来的信瓶小得不超过她的拇指。

sentences.en: The *size* surprised us all — how could anything so small carry a full set of map-words?
Old Helm held it to the starlight and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它对着星光，笑了。

sentences.en: Inside, folded impossibly thin, was an entire new island.
sentences.cn: 里面折得不可思议地薄，是整整一座新岛屿。

schedule:2.en: Pinned to the old watchtower door was a faded paper — a *schedule* of star-crossings, written in a hand none of us knew. Bell read each line aloud, her voice careful and low. According to the last entry, the next crossing was tonight, and we had less than an hour.
schedule:2.cnHint: 大家在瞭望塔门上发现了一张陌生人写的____，上面显示星星穿越的时间就在今晚。
schedule:2.hook: The final line of the schedule had been torn away.
schedule:2.line: 'The *schedule* says the stars cross only once — and that is tonight.'

sentences.en: Pinned to the old watchtower door was a faded paper — a *schedule* of star-crossings, written in a hand none of us knew.
Bell read each line aloud, her voice careful and low.
sentences.cn: 小铃逐行大声读出来，声音小心翼翼。

sentences.en: According to the last entry, the next crossing was tonight, and we had less than an hour.
sentences.cn: 根据最后一条记录，下一次星际穿越就在今晚，我们只剩不到一小时。

towards:2.en: A trail of soft blue sparks drifted *towards* the far cliff, and Bell was already following them, lantern raised. Old Helm called after her, but she waved without turning. We found her at the cliff's edge, kneeling over a hollow stone filled with folded paper-words, still warm.
towards:2.cnHint: 一串蓝色火花飘____远处悬崖，小铃跟了过去，并在那里发现了装满纸质词语的石洞。
towards:2.hook: The hollow stone had not been empty for very long.
towards:2.line: 'Every spark drifts *towards* something worth finding — trust them.'

sentences.en: A trail of soft blue sparks drifted *towards* the far cliff, and Bell was already following them, lantern raised.
Old Helm called after her, but she waved without turning.
sentences.cn: 老舵在她身后喊，但她挥挥手没有转身。

sentences.en: We found her at the cliff's edge, kneeling over a hollow stone filled with folded paper-words, still warm.
sentences.cn: 我们在悬崖边找到她，她跪在一块中空的石头前，里面装满了折叠的纸条，还是温的。

background:2.en: The old map had a strange *background* — not blank, but covered in faint writing, visible only when held against starlight. Old Helm turned it slowly, reading aloud in a quiet voice. The words described an island that had been lost for a hundred years, and its name matched ours.
background:2.cnHint: 老船长把地图对着星光，发现____上隐藏着描述一座失落岛屿的文字，那座岛的名字与我们的相同。
background:2.hook: Our island's name should not exist on a hundred-year-old map.
background:2.line: 'Look at the *background* of the map — there are words hiding there.'

sentences.en: The old map had a strange *background* — not blank, but covered in faint writing, visible only when held against starlight.
Old Helm turned it slowly, reading aloud in a quiet voice.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢转动它，用低沉的嗓音大声读出来。

sentences.en: The words described an island that had been lost for a hundred years, and its name matched ours.
sentences.cn: 这些字描述了一座失落了百年的岛屿，它的名字和我们的一样。

department:2.en: Inside the drifting archive-island, each room was a *department* — one for wind-words, one for water-words, one for words that belonged to no element at all. We were looking for fire-words when Bell found a sealed door marked with our troupe's symbol, as if someone had been expecting us.
department:2.cnHint: 在漂浮的档案岛里，每个房间是一个不同的____，小铃发现了一扇贴有我们团队标志的密封门。
department:2.hook: No one in our troupe had ever visited this island before.
department:2.line: 'The *department* of fire-words is sealed — only we can open it.'

sentences.en: Inside the drifting archive-island, each room was a *department* — one for wind-words, one for water-words, one for words that belonged to no element at all.
We were looking for fire-words when Bell found a sealed door marked with our troupe's symbol, as if someone had been expecting us.
sentences.cn: 我们在找火之字时，小铃发现了一扇密封的门，上面标着我们剧团的符号，好像有人在等我们一样。

detail:2.en: The carved tablet we uncovered was covered in pictures, but one small *detail* caught Bell's eye — a tiny boat at the corner, exactly like ours, down to the flag. Old Helm went very still. He said no one could have carved that tablet recently; the stone was far too old.
detail:2.cnHint: 小铃注意到石碑上的一个小____——角落里有一艘和我们一模一样的船，而石碑已有几百年历史。
detail:2.hook: Our boat had not existed when that stone was carved.
detail:2.line: 'Look at this *detail* — that tiny boat is ours, down to the flag.'

sentences.en: The carved tablet we uncovered was covered in pictures, but one small *detail* caught Bell's eye — a tiny boat at the corner, exactly like ours, down to the flag.
Old Helm went very still.
sentences.cn: 老舵一下子僵住了。

sentences.en: He said no one could have carved that tablet recently; the stone was far too old.
sentences.cn: 他说没人可能近期刻过这块石板，石头老得不像话。

decline:2.en: Inside a hollow star-coral, I found an old logbook. Its first pages were full of neat maps, but the later ones showed a clear *decline* — the drawings grew shaky, the notes shorter, until the final page held only one word: 'falling.' Old Helm pressed his hand over the cover and said nothing for a long time.
decline:2.cnHint: 我们在星珊瑚里发现了一本旧航海日志，记录着某段旅程逐渐走向____。
decline:2.hook: Whose hand had written that last word, and why had they stopped?
decline:2.line: Old Helm: 'This *decline* tells me someone lost more than direction out here.'

sentences.en: Inside a hollow star-coral, I found an old logbook.
sentences.cn: 我在一个中空的星形珊瑚里找到了一本旧航海日志。

sentences.en: Its first pages were full of neat maps, but the later ones showed a clear *decline* — the drawings grew shaky, the notes shorter, until the final page held only one word: 'falling.'
Old Helm pressed his hand over the cover and said nothing for a long time.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手按在封面上，久久没有说话。

extra:2.en: Bell spread the sky-chart across the deck and tapped a faint dotted line near the edge. 'That is an *extra* route,' she said, 'drawn in after the main map was finished.' The ink was a different colour — darker, newer — and it led toward an island none of us had ever named.
extra:2.cnHint: 小铃在星图边缘发现了一条____的航线，墨迹颜色与原图不同。
extra:2.hook: Someone had added that route in secret — but when, and for whom?
extra:2.line: Bell: 'One *extra* line on a map can change the whole journey.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the sky-chart across the deck and tapped a faint dotted line near the edge.
sentences.cn: 小铃把天空图摊开在甲板上，轻轻点了点靠近边缘的一条淡淡虚线。

sentences.en: 'That is an *extra* route,' she said, 'drawn in after the main map was finished.'
The ink was a different colour — darker, newer — and it led toward an island none of us had ever named.
sentences.cn: 墨水颜色不一样——更深、更新——它指向一个我们都没有命名过的岛屿。

income:2.en: At the market-post on Ember Isle, the stall-keeper shook his head sadly. 'Words are rare this season,' he said. 'My *income* used to be ten sky-coins a day, but now travellers pass without stopping.' He handed us a small carved token anyway, saying it might open a door further north.
income:2.cnHint: 市集摊主告诉我们，这个季节稀少的"词语"让他的____大不如前。
income:2.hook: The token felt warm in my palm, as though it remembered a fire.
income:2.line: Stall-keeper: 'When words dry up, so does every trader's *income*.'

sentences.en: At the market-post on Ember Isle, the stall-keeper shook his head sadly.
sentences.cn: 在灰烬岛的驿站市集，摊主沮丧地摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'Words are rare this season,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说，"这季节言语难得。"

sentences.en: 'My *income* used to be ten sky-coins a day, but now travellers pass without stopping.'
He handed us a small carved token anyway, saying it might open a door further north.
sentences.cn: 他还是递给我们一个小木雕符号，说它可能能打开北边某扇门。

medicine:2.en: Tucked behind a loose stone in the waystation wall, I found a tiny glass bottle. A label read: '*medicine* for a heavy heart — open only above the clouds.' Old Helm raised an eyebrow. Bell smiled. We agreed, without speaking, to keep it until the highest island on our map.
medicine:2.cnHint: 我们在驿站墙缝里找到了一瓶神秘的____，标签上写着要在云端以上才能开启。
medicine:2.hook: What kind of sorrow had the bottle been made to heal?
medicine:2.line: Old Helm: 'Good *medicine* waits for the right moment — so will we.'

sentences.en: Tucked behind a loose stone in the waystation wall, I found a tiny glass bottle.
sentences.cn: 我在驿站墙里一块松动的石头后面找到了一个微小的玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: A label read: '*medicine* for a heavy heart — open only above the clouds.'
Old Helm raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 老舵扬了扬眉毛。

sentences.en: Bell smiled.
sentences.cn: 小铃笑了。

sentences.en: We agreed, without speaking, to keep it until the highest island on our map.
sentences.cn: 我们无言地达成一致，要把它留到地图上最高的岛屿。

private:2.en: Slipped under my hammock was a folded note I had not put there. It bore a small wax seal shaped like a crescent. Inside, in careful letters, were the words: 'This route is *private*. Turn back at the amber reef.' I looked around the quiet cabin, but everyone seemed to be asleep.
private:2.cnHint: 我在吊床下发现了一张陌生的纸条，上面说这条航路是____的，警告我们返回。
private:2.hook: Someone on board already knew where we were going.
private:2.line: Silverfang: 'Mark my words — some routes are meant to stay *private*.'

sentences.en: Slipped under my hammock was a folded note I had not put there.
sentences.cn: 我的吊床下面塞着一张我没放过的折叠纸条。

sentences.en: It bore a small wax seal shaped like a crescent.
sentences.cn: 上面盖着一个新月形的蜡封。

sentences.en: Inside, in careful letters, were the words: 'This route is *private*.
Turn back at the amber reef.'
sentences.cn: 转身离开琥珀礁。

sentences.en: I looked around the quiet cabin, but everyone seemed to be asleep.
sentences.cn: 我环顾安静的舱室，但每个人似乎都睡着了。

side:2.en: The message stone glowed on one *side* only — the face turned toward the eastern wind. Old Helm explained that the builders had carved it that way on purpose: the glowing side points to the next island at dawn, the dark side warns of storms. We had been reading it backwards for two days.
side:2.cnHint: 消息石只有一____发光，老舵解释说我们一直看错了方向。
side:2.hook: If we had kept reading it wrong, where would we have ended up?
side:2.line: Old Helm: 'Always check which *side* the light is on before you sail.'

sentences.en: The message stone glowed on one *side* only — the face turned toward the eastern wind.
Old Helm explained that the builders had carved it that way on purpose: the glowing side points to the next island at dawn, the dark side warns of storms.
sentences.cn: 老舵解释说，建造者们故意这样刻的：闪亮的一面在黎明时指向下一个岛屿，暗的一面警告风暴。

sentences.en: We had been reading it backwards for two days.
sentences.cn: 我们已经把它读反了两天。

air:2.en: At the centre of the Driftstone Archive, a glass case held a single suspended feather. The *air* inside the case was perfectly still — no breath, no current — yet the feather turned slowly, as if reading something written in the quiet. A small card below it read: 'Last breath of the lost island, Velmoor.'
air:2.cnHint: 档案馆玻璃罩里的羽毛在静止的____中缓缓旋转，卡片上写着它来自失落之岛。
air:2.hook: If Velmoor was truly lost, why did the feather still seem to listen?
air:2.line: Bell: 'Feel that — even the *air* here is trying to tell us something.'

sentences.en: At the centre of the Driftstone Archive, a glass case held a single suspended feather.
sentences.cn: 在漂流石档案馆的中央，一个玻璃柜里悬着一根单独的羽毛。

sentences.en: The *air* inside the case was perfectly still — no breath, no current — yet the feather turned slowly, as if reading something written in the quiet.
A small card below it read: 'Last breath of the lost island, Velmoor.'
sentences.cn: 下面的小卡片写着："失落岛屿瓦尔摩尔的最后呼吸。"

consumption:2.en: The engineer at the fuel-dock looked at our vessel's log and frowned. 'Your sky-crystal *consumption* has doubled since the Ashveil crossing,' she said, handing us a printed slip covered in numbers. Old Helm studied it quietly, then looked up toward the clouds where something vast and invisible seemed to be pulling us onward.
consumption:2.cnHint: 码头工程师查看航行记录后发现，我们自从穿越灰幕以来，能量____增加了一倍。
consumption:2.hook: What out there in the dark was drawing so much power from our ship?
consumption:2.line: Bell: 'High *consumption* means something is pushing back against us.'

sentences.en: The engineer at the fuel-dock looked at our vessel's log and frowned.
sentences.cn: 燃料码头的工程师看了看我们船的航海日志，皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: 'Your sky-crystal *consumption* has doubled since the Ashveil crossing,' she said, handing us a printed slip covered in numbers.
Old Helm studied it quietly, then looked up toward the clouds where something vast and invisible seemed to be pulling us onward.
sentences.cn: 老舵静静地研究了它，然后向上看向云层，那里似乎有什么巨大而看不见的东西在把我们往前拉。

attack:2.en: Deep inside the Crystal Cavern, Old Helm held up his lantern. A swarm of tiny glowing beetles suddenly launched an *attack* on our light source, buzzing and striking the glass again and again. Bell pulled us back toward the tunnel entrance, her voice steady and calm.
attack:2.cnHint: 在水晶洞穴中，一群甲虫突然对我们的灯笼发起____，小铃带大家撤退。
attack:2.hook: Something larger stirred in the darkness beyond the beetles.
attack:2.line: 'This *attack* tells me something guards this cavern,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Deep inside the Crystal Cavern, Old Helm held up his lantern.
sentences.cn: 在水晶洞穴的深处，老舵举起了他的灯笼。

sentences.en: A swarm of tiny glowing beetles suddenly launched an *attack* on our light source, buzzing and striking the glass again and again.
Bell pulled us back toward the tunnel entrance, her voice steady and calm.
sentences.cn: 小铃拉着我们往隧道入口退去，她的声音平稳而冷静。

heavy:2.en: At the edge of Driftstone Bridge, Bell discovered a locked chest wedged between two rocks. It took all three of us to slide it free. The chest was so *heavy* that the old bridge boards groaned beneath it, and dust fell like snow into the clouds below.
heavy:2.cnHint: 小铃在桥边发现一只____的箱子，三人合力才将它挪开。
heavy:2.hook: Whatever was inside had not shifted once during the whole struggle.
heavy:2.line: 'It is far too *heavy* to carry alone,' Bell said quietly.

sentences.en: At the edge of Driftstone Bridge, Bell discovered a locked chest wedged between two rocks.
sentences.cn: 在漂流石桥的边缘，小铃发现了一个夹在两块岩石间的上锁木箱。

sentences.en: It took all three of us to slide it free.
sentences.cn: 我们三个人费力才把它拽出来。

sentences.en: The chest was so *heavy* that the old bridge boards groaned beneath it, and dust fell like snow into the clouds below.

thought:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a dusty map beside the campfire on Ember Ledge. He traced a faint dotted line with one finger and went quiet for a long moment. 'I have a *thought*,' he said at last, tapping a blank space near the map's edge. 'This island was never meant to be found.'
thought:2.cnHint: 在营地，老团长望着地图陷入沉思，分享了一个令人惊讶的____。
thought:2.hook: The blank space on the map began to glow faint gold.
thought:2.line: 'My *thought* is that someone hid this island on purpose,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a dusty map beside the campfire on Ember Ledge.
sentences.cn: 老舵在灰烬崖的篝火旁展开了一张积满灰尘的地图。

sentences.en: He traced a faint dotted line with one finger and went quiet for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 他用一根手指追踪着一条淡淡的虚线，然后陷入了沉默。

sentences.en: 'I have a *thought*,' he said at last, tapping a blank space near the map's edge.
'This island was never meant to be found.'
sentences.cn: "这个岛屿本不应该被发现。"

attract:2.en: Bell hung a small wind chime made of sea glass above the entrance to our camp on Pale Mesa. She said the soft ringing would *attract* the map-birds, rare creatures that carry word-fragments in their tail feathers. We waited. The stars above us turned slowly, and we listened.
attract:2.cnHint: 小铃用风铃来____地图鸟，希望它们带来新的词语碎片。
attract:2.hook: One feather drifted down from the dark sky above.
attract:2.line: 'The sound should *attract* them before dawn,' Bell said with a smile.

sentences.en: Bell hung a small wind chime made of sea glass above the entrance to our camp on Pale Mesa.
sentences.cn: 小铃在苍白台地营地的入口上方挂了一个用海玻璃做的小风铃。

sentences.en: She said the soft ringing would *attract* the map-birds, rare creatures that carry word-fragments in their tail feathers.
We waited.
sentences.cn: 我们等待着。

sentences.en: The stars above us turned slowly, and we listened.
sentences.cn: 头顶的星星缓缓转动，我们静静聆听。

define:2.en: Old Helm spread three glowing word-stones across the navigation table. 'Each word we find helps *define* the shape of the next island,' he explained, pressing them into a triangle. The stones hummed and a faint outline appeared in the air above them, like a mountain seen through morning fog.
define:2.cnHint: 老团长解释说，收集到的词语石能够____下一座岛屿的轮廓。
define:2.hook: The outline trembled, then split slowly into two shapes.
define:2.line: 'These three words *define* our next destination,' Old Helm said firmly.

sentences.en: Old Helm spread three glowing word-stones across the navigation table.
sentences.cn: 老舵在导航台上铺开三块发光的字石。

sentences.en: 'Each word we find helps *define* the shape of the next island,' he explained, pressing them into a triangle.
The stones hummed and a faint outline appeared in the air above them, like a mountain seen through morning fog.
sentences.cn: 石头嗡鸣着，它们上方的空气中出现了一个淡淡的轮廓，像晨雾中远眺的山峰。

executive:2.en: A sealed letter was tucked inside the hollow of an old sky-pine on Ridgewing Island. The wax stamp showed a compass rose. Bell read it aloud: the letter was signed by the *executive* of the Word-Keepers Guild, granting our troupe permission to enter the Sealed Archive on the far eastern islands.
executive:2.cnHint: 小铃在树洞里发现一封信，落款是词语守护者公会____的印章。
executive:2.hook: A second, unmarked envelope was folded behind the first.
executive:2.line: 'The *executive* of the Guild has approved our passage,' Bell announced.

sentences.en: A sealed letter was tucked inside the hollow of an old sky-pine on Ridgewing Island.
sentences.cn: 一封封好的信被藏在岭翼岛一棵老天松树的树洞里。

sentences.en: The wax stamp showed a compass rose.
sentences.cn: 蜡印上刻着一朵罗盘玫瑰。

sentences.en: Bell read it aloud: the letter was signed by the *executive* of the Word-Keepers Guild, granting our troupe permission to enter the Sealed Archive on the far eastern islands.

expectation:2.en: Silverfang arrived at the Sky Pier ahead of us and leaned against his ship with crossed arms. Old Helm had promised a rare double-star chart in exchange for safe passage, but Silverfang's *expectation* was clear the moment he looked at the small rolled paper in Old Helm's hand and raised one eyebrow.
expectation:2.cnHint: 银牙船长对交换条件抱有很高的____，老舵拿出的地图令他皱起了眉头。
expectation:2.hook: Old Helm smiled and unrolled a second, much larger chart.
expectation:2.line: 'My *expectation* was something far more valuable,' Silverfang said coolly.

sentences.en: Silverfang arrived at the Sky Pier ahead of us and leaned against his ship with crossed arms.
sentences.cn: 银牙比我们更早抵达天空码头，交叉双臂靠在他的船上。

sentences.en: Old Helm had promised a rare double-star chart in exchange for safe passage, but Silverfang's *expectation* was clear the moment he looked at the small rolled paper in Old Helm's hand and raised one eyebrow.

friendly:2.en: We landed on Mosscap Island just after the stars reached their highest point. A small figure stepped out from behind a carved stone gate and waved both hands above its head. The gesture was unmistakably *friendly*, and Bell waved back at once, her lantern swinging warm orange light across the path.
friendly:2.cnHint: 在Mosscap岛，一个陌生身影向我们做出____的招手姿势，小铃立刻回应。
friendly:2.hook: The figure then pointed urgently at something behind us.
friendly:2.line: 'The wave looked *friendly* enough to me,' Bell said, stepping forward.

sentences.en: We landed on Mosscap Island just after the stars reached their highest point.
sentences.cn: 我们在星星升到最高点刚过不久时在苔盖岛登陆。

sentences.en: A small figure stepped out from behind a carved stone gate and waved both hands above its head.
sentences.cn: 一个小小的身影从雕刻的石门后步出，挥舞双手在头顶上方。

sentences.en: The gesture was unmistakably *friendly*, and Bell waved back at once, her lantern swinging warm orange light across the path.

indeed:2.en: Inside the hollow star-stone, I found a folded map no bigger than my palm. Old Helm held it to the lantern light and nodded slowly. 'This is *indeed* the chart we lost at the Amber Crossing,' he said, his voice soft with relief. The ink still glowed faintly gold.
indeed:2.cnHint: 老舵手在星石内发现了一张失落已久的地图，____是他们寻找的那张。
indeed:2.hook: But one island on the chart had no name — only a question mark.
indeed:2.line: 'This is *indeed* the chart we have been searching for.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow star-stone, I found a folded map no bigger than my palm.
sentences.cn: 在空心星石内部，我找到了一张不超过我手掌大小的折叠地图。

sentences.en: Old Helm held it to the lantern light and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它放到灯光下照着，慢慢点了点头。

sentences.en: 'This is *indeed* the chart we lost at the Amber Crossing,' he said, his voice soft with relief.
The ink still glowed faintly gold.
sentences.cn: 墨迹仍然散发着淡淡的金色光芒。

launch:2.en: We gathered at the edge of Cloud Pier as Bell counted down aloud. On her final word, the little signal kite leapt from her hands into the night wind — a perfect *launch* that pulled the guide-rope all the way across to the next island. A cheer rose from the troupe.
launch:2.cnHint: 贝尔在云码头完成了一次漂亮的____，信风筝顺利飞向对岸。
launch:2.hook: Then the rope went tight — something on the far island had grabbed it.
launch:2.line: 'That *launch* was cleaner than anything I have seen in years,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: We gathered at the edge of Cloud Pier as Bell counted down aloud.
sentences.cn: 我们聚集在云天码头的边缘，小铃大声倒计时。

sentences.en: On her final word, the little signal kite leapt from her hands into the night wind — a perfect *launch* that pulled the guide-rope all the way across to the next island.
A cheer rose from the troupe.
sentences.cn: 一阵欢呼从队伍中升起。

refer:2.en: Bell unrolled a long strip of bark covered in tiny symbols. 'When you are lost,' she told me quietly, 'always *refer* to the star-lines at the top of the chart — they never change, even when the islands drift.' I traced the symbols with one finger, trying to learn their shape.
refer:2.cnHint: 贝尔教我如何____星图上的星线来辨认方向。
refer:2.hook: One star-line, I noticed, pointed straight down through the cloud floor.
refer:2.line: '*Refer* to the star-lines first — they are always honest,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell unrolled a long strip of bark covered in tiny symbols.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开了一长条树皮，上面覆盖着密密麻麻的符号。

sentences.en: 'When you are lost,' she told me quietly, 'always *refer* to the star-lines at the top of the chart — they never change, even when the islands drift.'
I traced the symbols with one finger, trying to learn their shape.
sentences.cn: 我用一根手指描摹那些符号，想要学会它们的形状。

trust:2.en: Old Helm placed the worn compass in my hands without a word. The *trust* he showed in that small act felt heavier than the brass itself. I had only been part of the troupe for three sunrises, yet here I was, holding the instrument that had guided them across forty islands.
trust:2.cnHint: 老舵手将珍贵的罗盘交给我，这份____让我感到责任重大。
trust:2.hook: The needle spun once, then pointed somewhere the maps said was empty.
trust:2.line: '*Trust* is the only compass that never needs winding,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm placed the worn compass in my hands without a word.
sentences.cn: 老舵没有说一句话，就把那只磨损的罗盘放进了我的手里。

sentences.en: The *trust* he showed in that small act felt heavier than the brass itself.
I had only been part of the troupe for three sunrises, yet here I was, holding the instrument that had guided them across forty islands.
sentences.cn: 虽然我只加入队伍三个日出，却已经拿着这件引导他们跨越四十个岛屿的仪器。

discussion:2.en: The troupe sat around the warm lamp long after supper. The *discussion* about which route to take next was gentle but serious — Old Helm tapping the chart, Bell sketching wind-curves on a scrap of bark, Silverfang leaning back with closed eyes, listening. I added one small idea, and nobody laughed.
discussion:2.cnHint: 晚饭后，团员们围灯进行了一场关于下一段航路的____。
discussion:2.hook: Then Silverfang opened one eye and said, 'There is a third way.'
discussion:2.line: 'This *discussion* matters more than any map we carry,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The troupe sat around the warm lamp long after supper.
sentences.cn: 晚饭后很久，队伍还坐在温暖的灯笼周围。

sentences.en: The *discussion* about which route to take next was gentle but serious — Old Helm tapping the chart, Bell sketching wind-curves on a scrap of bark, Silverfang leaning back with closed eyes, listening.
I added one small idea, and nobody laughed.
sentences.cn: 我提了一个小想法，没有人笑我。

extremely:2.en: The star-shower began without warning. Streaks of pale blue light crossed the sky so fast and so close that I ducked instinctively. Bell, *extremely* calm beside me, simply raised her notebook and began sketching each trail. 'Every streak is a clue,' she murmured. 'Don't hide — look.'
extremely:2.cnHint: 星雨突然降临，贝尔____冷静地开始记录每一道光迹。
extremely:2.hook: The final streak did not fade — it curved downward and kept falling.
extremely:2.line: 'Stay *extremely* still and watch — the sky is writing something,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The star-shower began without warning.
sentences.cn: 星雨毫无预兆地降临了。

sentences.en: Streaks of pale blue light crossed the sky so fast and so close that I ducked instinctively.
sentences.cn: 淡蓝色的光线划过天空，速度之快、距离之近让我本能地往后一缩。

sentences.en: Bell, *extremely* calm beside me, simply raised her notebook and began sketching each trail.
'Every streak is a clue,' she murmured.
sentences.cn: "每一道光迹都是线索，"她低声说。

sentences.en: 'Don't hide — look.'
sentences.cn: "别躲——看着。"

organize:2.en: After the star-shower, small glowing pebbles lay scattered across the whole deck. Old Helm asked me to *organize* them by colour into the six clay bowls he set out in a row. As I sorted, a pattern began to appear — the colours matched the six islands shown on our newest chart.
organize:2.cnHint: 老舵手让我把发光石块按颜色____整理，排列结果令人惊喜。
organize:2.hook: The sixth bowl matched an island Old Helm said he had never reached.
organize:2.line: '*Organize* them carefully — the order may be a message,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: After the star-shower, small glowing pebbles lay scattered across the whole deck.
sentences.cn: 星雨之后，闪闪发光的小鹅卵石散落在整个甲板上。

sentences.en: Old Helm asked me to *organize* them by colour into the six clay bowls he set out in a row.
As I sorted, a pattern began to appear — the colours matched the six islands shown on our newest chart.
sentences.cn: 当我分类时，一个图案开始显现——这些颜色和我们最新地图上的六个岛屿完全吻合。

pattern:2.en: I laid the glowing pebbles on the chart and stepped back. The *pattern* was clear now: six points of colour forming a path that curved like a fish-hook through the islands we had not yet visited. Bell whispered the names of each stop aloud, and each name was a word the troupe had collected.
pattern:2.cnHint: 发光石块排列出的____揭示了一条穿越未知岛屿的完整路线。
pattern:2.hook: The path ended at an island that appeared on no chart at all.
pattern:2.line: 'This *pattern* is our next journey, written in starlight,' said Bell.

sentences.en: I laid the glowing pebbles on the chart and stepped back.
sentences.cn: 我把发光的鹅卵石放在海图上，往后退了一步。

sentences.en: The *pattern* was clear now: six points of colour forming a path that curved like a fish-hook through the islands we had not yet visited.
Bell whispered the names of each stop aloud, and each name was a word the troupe had collected.
sentences.cn: 小铃轻声念出每个停靠点的名字，每个名字都是剧团收集来的词汇。

transform:2.en: We landed on the Ink Isle, where the ground was blank white stone. Old Helm pressed a glowing word-fragment against the surface. Before our eyes, the pale rock began to *transform*: colours bloomed outward like ink dropped in water, and a detailed map of three new islands spread beneath our feet.
transform:2.cnHint: 老舵将字片按在白石地面上，地面____了，一幅新地图出现在众人脚下。
transform:2.hook: But one island on the map had no name at all.
transform:2.line: 'Watch the stone *transform* — every colour is a road we have not walked.'

sentences.en: We landed on the Ink Isle, where the ground was blank white stone.
sentences.cn: 我们在墨岛登陆，地面是一片空白的白色石头。

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed a glowing word-fragment against the surface.
sentences.cn: 老舵把一个发光的词语碎片按在表面上。

sentences.en: Before our eyes, the pale rock began to *transform*: colours bloomed outward like ink dropped in water, and a detailed map of three new islands spread beneath our feet.

additional:2.en: Bell spread the route charts across a flat cloud-rock and counted the word-fragments we had collected. 'Five,' she said quietly. Then Old Helm reached into his coat and placed two more on the pile. The *additional* fragments made the chart glow brighter, and a hidden island shimmered into view at the edge of the map.
additional:2.cnHint: 老舵拿出了____的字片，地图上随即浮现出一座此前隐藏的岛屿。
additional:2.hook: The island blinked once, then vanished from the chart.
additional:2.line: 'These *additional* pieces may be the only key to that lost isle.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the route charts across a flat cloud-rock and counted the word-fragments we had collected.
sentences.cn: 小铃把路线图铺在平坦的云石上，数了数我们收集到的词语碎片。

sentences.en: 'Five,' she said quietly.
sentences.cn: "五个，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: Then Old Helm reached into his coat and placed two more on the pile.
sentences.cn: 接着老舵伸手到外套里，又放了两个在堆上。

sentences.en: The *additional* fragments made the chart glow brighter, and a hidden island shimmered into view at the edge of the map.

journal:2.en: Inside a hollow star-coral on the Drift Shelf, I found a small worn book. Its cover read: Navigator's *Journal* — Isle of Echoes. The entries were written in a careful hand, recording winds, strange lights, and one final line: 'The word that opens the last gate sleeps at the centre of the sky.'
journal:2.cnHint: 我在珊瑚礁洞中发现了一本航行____，最后一行写着通往终点的秘密。
journal:2.hook: The final page had been torn cleanly away.
journal:2.line: 'A *journal* left here means someone reached this shelf before us.'

sentences.en: Inside a hollow star-coral on the Drift Shelf, I found a small worn book.
sentences.cn: 我在漂流架上的一个空心星珊瑚里找到了一本破旧的小书。

sentences.en: Its cover read: Navigator's *Journal* — Isle of Echoes.
The entries were written in a careful hand, recording winds, strange lights, and one final line: 'The word that opens the last gate sleeps at the centre of the sky.'
sentences.cn: 日记里用工整的笔迹记录了风向、奇异的光和最后一行："打开最后一扇门的词语在天空的中心沉睡。"

sort:2.en: Silverfang arrived at the Night Pier with a crate of word-fragments, all tangled together. 'What *sort* of order did you keep these in?' Old Helm asked, raising an eyebrow. Silverfang grinned. 'The living sort — they move around on their own.' Sure enough, two fragments were slowly crawling toward each other across the wooden deck.
sort:2.cnHint: 银牙带来一箱乱放的字片，老舵问他用的是哪____整理方式。
sort:2.hook: The two crawling fragments clicked together and lit up red.
sort:2.line: 'What *sort* of map piece moves by itself at midnight?'

sentences.en: Silverfang arrived at the Night Pier with a crate of word-fragments, all tangled together.
sentences.cn: 银牙来到夜码头，带了一箱词语碎片，全都缠在一起。

sentences.en: 'What *sort* of order did you keep these in?'
Old Helm asked, raising an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 老舵问道，扬起眉毛。

sentences.en: Silverfang grinned.
sentences.cn: 银牙咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: 'The living sort — they move around on their own.'
sentences.cn: "活的那种——它们会自己到处乱爬。"

sentences.en: Sure enough, two fragments were slowly crawling toward each other across the wooden deck.
sentences.cn: 果不其然，两个碎片正在木板甲板上缓缓朝彼此爬去。

understanding:2.en: The star charts on the Amber Platform were written in a script none of us could read — until Bell sat with them for a long quiet hour. She looked up with bright eyes. 'I have an *understanding* of it now,' she said. 'Each symbol is not a letter; it is a feeling.' The platform hummed as if it agreed.
understanding:2.cnHint: 小铃独自研究星图一小时后，终于对那种文字有了____，发现每个符号代表一种感受。
understanding:2.hook: Then the symbols began rearranging themselves before her eyes.
understanding:2.line: 'My *understanding* is still small, but enough to find the next isle.'

sentences.en: The star charts on the Amber Platform were written in a script none of us could read — until Bell sat with them for a long quiet hour.
sentences.cn: 琥珀平台上的星图用一种我们都看不懂的文字写成——直到小铃安静地坐了一个小时。

sentences.en: She looked up with bright eyes.
sentences.cn: 她抬起头，眼睛闪闪发光。

sentences.en: 'I have an *understanding* of it now,' she said.
'Each symbol is not a letter; it is a feeling.'
sentences.cn: "每个符号不是一个字母，而是一种感受。"

sentences.en: The platform hummed as if it agreed.
sentences.cn: 平台发出嗡嗡声，仿佛表示同意。

citizen:2.en: At Cloud Harbour we met an old man selling bottled winds. He wore a badge shaped like a winged coin. 'I am a proud *citizen* of this harbour,' he told us, polishing the badge slowly, 'and every wind I sell remembers where it has been.' He handed Old Helm a small bottle, and inside it a tiny star was spinning.
citizen:2.cnHint: 云港的一位老____自豪地向我们介绍这里，并送给老舵一瓶装有星星的风。
citizen:2.hook: The spinning star inside the bottle suddenly stopped.
citizen:2.line: 'As a *citizen* of Cloud Harbour, I know every secret the wind carries.'

sentences.en: At Cloud Harbour we met an old man selling bottled winds.
sentences.cn: 在云港我们遇到了一个老人在卖装在瓶子里的风。

sentences.en: He wore a badge shaped like a winged coin.
sentences.cn: 他戴着一枚翅膀硬币形状的徽章。

sentences.en: 'I am a proud *citizen* of this harbour,' he told us, polishing the badge slowly, 'and every wind I sell remembers where it has been.'
He handed Old Helm a small bottle, and inside it a tiny star was spinning.
sentences.cn: 他递给老舵一个小瓶子，里面一颗小星星在旋转。

contrast:2.en: The twin peaks of Mirror Ridge stood side by side: one covered in soft silver moss, the other bare black rock. The *contrast* between them made the shape of an arrow pointing downward. 'That is not nature,' Bell said softly. We climbed down and found a sealed door right where the arrow aimed, hidden in the cliff face.
contrast:2.cnHint: 镜脊山两座山峰的____形成了一个箭头，小铃由此发现了山崖上隐藏的封门。
contrast:2.hook: Behind the sealed door, something was breathing.
contrast:2.line: 'Notice the *contrast* — someone designed these peaks to point the way.'

sentences.en: The twin peaks of Mirror Ridge stood side by side: one covered in soft silver moss, the other bare black rock.
sentences.cn: 镜岭的双峰并排矗立：一座覆盖着柔软的银色苔藓，另一座是光秃秃的黑色岩石。

sentences.en: The *contrast* between them made the shape of an arrow pointing downward.
'That is not nature,' Bell said softly.
sentences.cn: "这不是自然，"小铃轻声说。

sentences.en: We climbed down and found a sealed door right where the arrow aimed, hidden in the cliff face.
sentences.cn: 我们爬了下去，在箭头指向的地方发现了一扇密闭的门，隐藏在悬崖壁上。

establish:2.en: Old Helm gathered us at the centre of Star Flat Island and drove a glowing staff into the ground. 'We *establish* our base camp here,' he announced. The staff sent a ring of soft light outward across the flat stone, and where the light touched, small lanterns rose from the ground by themselves, forming a warm circle in the dark.
establish:2.cnHint: 老舵将发光的旗杆插入地面，宣布在此____营地，石地上随即升起一圈小灯笼。
establish:2.hook: One lantern rose higher than the rest and drifted away.
establish:2.line: 'We *establish* our camp here tonight — the stars will keep watch for us.'

sentences.en: Old Helm gathered us at the centre of Star Flat Island and drove a glowing staff into the ground.
sentences.cn: 老舵把我们聚集在星平岛的中心，把一根发光的杖插进了地里。

sentences.en: 'We *establish* our base camp here,' he announced.
The staff sent a ring of soft light outward across the flat stone, and where the light touched, small lanterns rose from the ground by themselves, forming a warm circle in the dark.
sentences.cn: 杖向四周散发出柔和的光，光所触之处，小灯笼从地面自己升起，在黑暗中形成了一个温暖的圆圈。

estimate:2.en: Bell spread the star-chart across a flat stone and studied it closely. 'My *estimate* is three islands away,' she said, tapping a cluster of faint lights. The troupe gathered around, breath held. Beyond the edge of the chart, a soft glow pulsed — something unmapped was already calling to us.
estimate:2.cnHint: 小铃看着星图，对目的地的距离做出了一个____。
estimate:2.hook: But the glow moved closer before we could pack our bags.
estimate:2.line: 'My *estimate* is three islands away — maybe less if the wind holds.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the star-chart across a flat stone and studied it closely.
sentences.cn: 小铃把星图摊在一块平石上，仔细研究着。

sentences.en: 'My *estimate* is three islands away,' she said, tapping a cluster of faint lights.
The troupe gathered around, breath held.
sentences.cn: 队伍聚拢过来，屏住呼吸。

sentences.en: Beyond the edge of the chart, a soft glow pulsed — something unmapped was already calling to us.
sentences.cn: 在海图的边界外，一阵柔和的光芒脉动着——某个未知的东西已经在召唤我们了。

explore:2.en: Old Helm handed me a small lantern and pointed toward a cave mouth hidden beneath a curtain of silver moss. 'Your turn to *explore*,' he said with a quiet smile. I stepped inside. The walls were covered in tiny carvings — each one a word, each word a door to somewhere new.
explore:2.cnHint: 老舵让我拿着灯笼去____那个长满苔藓的神秘洞穴。
explore:2.hook: The last carving on the wall was still warm to the touch.
explore:2.line: 'Your turn to *explore* — we will be right here if you need us.'

sentences.en: Old Helm handed me a small lantern and pointed toward a cave mouth hidden beneath a curtain of silver moss.
sentences.cn: 老舵递给我一盏小灯笼，指向一个被银色苔藓帷幕遮挡的洞穴入口。

sentences.en: 'Your turn to *explore*,' he said with a quiet smile.
I stepped inside.
sentences.cn: 我走了进去。

sentences.en: The walls were covered in tiny carvings — each one a word, each word a door to somewhere new.
sentences.cn: 洞壁上布满了细小的刻画——每一个都是一个词，每个词都是通往新地方的门。

fix:2.en: The rope bridge to the next island had snapped at one end, leaving us without a crossing. Bell climbed the anchor post and looped a new line through the iron ring. 'I can *fix* this,' she said calmly, her fingers working fast while the wind pushed the bridge in wide, lazy circles.
fix:2.cnHint: 小铃爬上锚柱，打算____断裂的绳桥。
fix:2.hook: The iron ring groaned once — then held, just barely.
fix:2.line: 'I can *fix* this — hand me that second rope, quickly.'

sentences.en: The rope bridge to the next island had snapped at one end, leaving us without a crossing.
sentences.cn: 通往下一个岛屿的绳桥一端已经断裂，我们没有办法过去。

sentences.en: Bell climbed the anchor post and looped a new line through the iron ring.
sentences.cn: 小铃爬上锚柱，把一根新绳子穿过铁环。

sentences.en: 'I can *fix* this,' she said calmly, her fingers working fast while the wind pushed the bridge in wide, lazy circles.

general:2.en: Old Helm drew a rough map in the dust, marking the floating islands we had visited. 'The *general* shape of this sky-world,' he said, 'is like a wheel — we are somewhere near the rim.' I stared at the circle of dots and felt, for the first time, that the journey had a pattern.
general:2.cnHint: 老舵在尘土上画图，描述这片天空世界的____轮廓。
general:2.hook: One dot on the rim had no name — only a question mark.
general:2.line: 'The *general* shape is clear enough — the centre island must be enormous.'

sentences.en: Old Helm drew a rough map in the dust, marking the floating islands we had visited.
sentences.cn: 老舵在尘埃里粗略地画了张地图，标记出我们访过的浮岛。

sentences.en: 'The *general* shape of this sky-world,' he said, 'is like a wheel — we are somewhere near the rim.'
I stared at the circle of dots and felt, for the first time, that the journey had a pattern.
sentences.cn: 我盯着这些点的圆圈，第一次感到这趟旅程有了图案。

loss:2.en: We found a small wooden chest wedged in the roots of a cloud-tree. Inside lay a single faded letter and nothing else. Bell read it aloud: a traveller writing of the *loss* of a beloved map, hoping whoever found the chest would carry the journey forward. We looked at each other and nodded.
loss:2.cnHint: 木箱里有一封信，讲述了旅人因____珍贵地图而留下的遗愿。
loss:2.hook: The letter was signed with only a symbol — our troupe's own emblem.
loss:2.line: 'Such a great *loss* — but maybe that is why the map found its way to us.'

sentences.en: We found a small wooden chest wedged in the roots of a cloud-tree.
sentences.cn: 我们在一棵云树的根部找到了一只小木箱。

sentences.en: Inside lay a single faded letter and nothing else.
sentences.cn: 里面只有一封褪了色的信，别的什么都没有。

sentences.en: Bell read it aloud: a traveller writing of the *loss* of a beloved map, hoping whoever found the chest would carry the journey forward.
We looked at each other and nodded.
sentences.cn: 我们互相看了看，点了点头。

partner:2.en: Silverfang pulled his ship alongside ours and jumped across with surprising grace. 'I have a proposal,' he said. 'Beyond the twin peaks there is a locked gate — neither of us can open it alone. Be my *partner* for one day.' Old Helm studied him for a long moment, then shook his hand.
partner:2.cnHint: 银牙提出，面对锁着的大门，希望老舵做他一天的____。
partner:2.hook: The gate, Bell whispered, had not opened in a hundred years.
partner:2.line: 'Be my *partner* for one day — after that we go our own ways.'

sentences.en: Silverfang pulled his ship alongside ours and jumped across with surprising grace.
sentences.cn: 银牙把他的船靠向我们的船，以出人意料的优雅姿态跳了过来。

sentences.en: 'I have a proposal,' he said.
sentences.cn: "我有个提议，"他说。

sentences.en: 'Beyond the twin peaks there is a locked gate — neither of us can open it alone.
sentences.cn: "双峰那边有道上了锁的门——我们谁都单独打不开。

sentences.en: Be my *partner* for one day.'
Old Helm studied him for a long moment, then shook his hand.
sentences.cn: 老舵沉思了片刻，然后和他握了握手。

concept:2.en: I asked Bell how the troupe chose which words to collect. She thought for a moment, gazing at the stars. 'Each word carries a *concept* — an idea that opens a new place in the world,' she said. 'Collect enough ideas and the whole sky becomes a map you can read.' I wrote that down carefully.
concept:2.cnHint: 小铃向我解释，每个词都承载着一个____，能打开世界中的新地方。
concept:2.hook: She pointed up — and a new island blinked into view, right on cue.
concept:2.line: 'Every word carries a *concept* — that is what makes it worth collecting.'

sentences.en: I asked Bell how the troupe chose which words to collect.
sentences.cn: 我问小铃队伍怎么选择要收集哪些词。

sentences.en: She thought for a moment, gazing at the stars.
sentences.cn: 她停顿了一下，目光望向星空。

sentences.en: 'Each word carries a *concept* — an idea that opens a new place in the world,' she said.
'Collect enough ideas and the whole sky becomes a map you can read.'
sentences.cn: "集够了想法，整片天空就会变成一张你能读懂的地图。"

sentences.en: I wrote that down carefully.
sentences.cn: 我仔细把这句话记了下来。

history:2.en: Deep in the cave, a wide stone tablet stood upright, covered in neat rows of words. Old Helm ran his fingers along the lines slowly. 'This is the *history* of every troupe that ever travelled these islands,' he said softly. I found a small blank space at the bottom — room for one more story.
history:2.cnHint: 石碑上刻着所有曾在这片岛屿旅行的剧团的____。
history:2.hook: The blank space at the bottom was exactly the right size for our names.
history:2.line: 'This *history* goes back further than any of us imagined — keep reading.'

sentences.en: Deep in the cave, a wide stone tablet stood upright, covered in neat rows of words.
sentences.cn: 深洞里竖着一块宽大的石板，上面整整齐齐地刻满了字。

sentences.en: Old Helm ran his fingers along the lines slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵的手指沿着字迹慢慢滑过。

sentences.en: 'This is the *history* of every troupe that ever travelled these islands,' he said softly.
I found a small blank space at the bottom — room for one more story.
sentences.cn: 我在底部发现了一小块空白——还有位置再刻一个故事。

adopt:2.en: Inside the hollow of a drifting island, I found a wooden box. Bell lifted the lid and showed us a glowing map-word sealed in glass. 'We should *adopt* this method,' she said softly, 'collecting each word as if it were a living thing worth protecting.' Old Helm nodded, and the stars outside burned a little brighter.
adopt:2.cnHint: 小铃在漂浮岛的树洞里发现了一个发光的地图词语，她建议大家____一种新的收集方式。
adopt:2.hook: But the box had already been opened once before.
adopt:2.line: 'We should *adopt* this method of keeping every word safe,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Inside the hollow of a drifting island, I found a wooden box.
sentences.cn: 在一座漂浮岛屿的洞穴里，我找到了一个木盒。

sentences.en: Bell lifted the lid and showed us a glowing map-word sealed in glass.
sentences.cn: 小铃打开盖子，给我们看了一个被封在玻璃里的发光的地图符号。

sentences.en: 'We should *adopt* this method,' she said softly, 'collecting each word as if it were a living thing worth protecting.'
Old Helm nodded, and the stars outside burned a little brighter.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头，窗外的星星烧得更亮了。

famous:2.en: Pinned to the wall of an old sky-dock was a faded chart. Old Helm traced a circle near its edge. 'That is the Lantern Shelf,' he said, 'once *famous* across every floating island for the light it cast at night.' I copied the name into my notebook, and a new word shimmered into view on our map.
famous:2.cnHint: 老舵手在一张旧海图上指出了一个____的地方——灯架礁台，那里曾照亮过无数漂浮岛屿。
famous:2.hook: Yet the Lantern Shelf had vanished from every newer chart.
famous:2.line: 'That shelf was once *famous* for guiding travellers through the darkest sky,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Pinned to the wall of an old sky-dock was a faded chart.
sentences.cn: 在一座老旧天空码头的墙上钉着一张褪色的海图。

sentences.en: Old Helm traced a circle near its edge.
sentences.cn: 老舵在边缘处描了一个圆。

sentences.en: 'That is the Lantern Shelf,' he said, 'once *famous* across every floating island for the light it cast at night.'
I copied the name into my notebook, and a new word shimmered into view on our map.
sentences.cn: 我把这个名字抄进笔记本，地图上又闪现出一个新词。

responsibility:1.en: The night market on Sky-Root Island glowed with a hundred lanterns. Old Helm handed me a small wooden box. 'Every word we collect is a promise,' he said quietly. 'Carrying it is your *responsibility* now.' I held the box tighter, feeling the weight of something far bigger than wood and air.
responsibility:1.cnHint: 老舵手把装有词语碎片的木盒交给我，告诉我这份____不可轻视。
responsibility:1.hook: Somewhere below the island, a second lantern answered ours.
responsibility:1.line: 'Carrying it is your *responsibility* now, and the sky watches you keep it.'

sentences.en: The night market on Sky-Root Island glowed with a hundred lanterns.
sentences.cn: 天根岛上的夜市灯光闪烁，百盏灯笼点亮了整个天空。

sentences.en: Old Helm handed me a small wooden box.
sentences.cn: 老舵递给我一个小木盒。

sentences.en: 'Every word we collect is a promise,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "我们收集的每一个词都是一个承诺，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: 'Carrying it is your *responsibility* now.'
I held the box tighter, feeling the weight of something far bigger than wood and air.
sentences.cn: 我紧紧握着这个盒子，感受到了远比木头和空气更沉重的东西。
